At this time, Akokoro was called "Yamato Nao." The Crown Prince, who was filled with suspicion, became suspicious of Agogo's true intentions and tried to kill him. So Akokoro felt humbled and offered his younger sister, Hinohime, as a tribute, and was spared the death penalty. From this time on, Yamato Nao began to offer court ladies as tribute. 『日本書紀』履中天皇即位前紀条 According to Volume 12 of the "Shoki," Prince Sumiyoshi Nakatsu and Yamato Naokogo were on close terms. Therefore, when Prince Naka rebelled against the Crown Prince, Prince Izahowake (later Emperor Richu), presumably in the year 399, he tried to side with Prince Naka and gathered several hundred elite soldiers at a place called "Kakihami no Kurusu" (said to be Kurusu-go, [[:ja:忍海郡|Oshikai County]] ) and waited for the Crown Prince. However, when he realized that the Crown Prince's troops were more numerous than he had expected, he changed his attitude. === Driftwood of the Oi River === Another part of the Richū Sokui Chronicle states that the Crown Prince, on his way to [[Isonokami Shrine]], encounters a young girl at the foot of Mt. Asuka and asks her about the safety of the journey.{{Quote frame|六十二年の夏五月（推定[[374年]]）に、[[遠淡海国造|遠江国司]]（とほつあふみのくに の みこともち）表上言（まう）さく、「大（おほ）きなる樹（き）有りて、[[大井川|大井河]]（おほゐがは）より流れて、河（かは）曲（くま）り停（とどま）れり。其大きさ十囲（とうだき＝30尺、およそ300メートル）。本（もと）は壱（ひとつ）にして末は両（またまた）なり」とまうす。時に倭直吾子籠（やまとのあたひあごこ）を遣（つかは）して船に造らしむ。而（しかう）して南海（みなみのみち）より運（めぐら）して、難波津（なにはのつ）に将（ゐ）て来（きた）りて、御船（みふね）に充（あ）てつ。『日本書紀』仁徳天皇62年5月条}}There are also situations where you are advised to do so. This shows that the Yamato Naochou clan was familiar with the geography of the surrounding area, to the extent that they were able to set up ambushes. "The mountains are filled with many soldiers. Please go around and cross the Tagima Pass." === Prince Sumiyoshi's Rebellion === The fourteenth volume of the "Shoki" tells the story of Emperor Yuryaku, who, in a fit of rage after a hunt at Mimase, killed Otsu no Umakai with the sword, and his mother, Empress {{ill|Oshisaka no Ōnakatsuhime|en}}, presenting the Wa court lady "Hinohime" to settle the matter. This conversation led to the establishment of [[:ja:宍人部|the Shishihitobe]] (the branch of the Shishihito clan), and the appointment of three members, including Kashiwadeno no Omi Nagano. In addition, the “Oyamato no Kuni no Miyatsuko Agogo no Sukune” presented Sahonoko Toriwake to the Shishihitobe, and “the Ministers of the Imperial Court, Tomo no Miyatsuko and Kuni no Miyatsuko, followed suit and continued to offer tribute.” 『日本書紀』雄略天皇2年10月6日条{{Quote frame|「伝（つて）に聞く、皇太子（ひつぎのみこ）、非常之事（おもほえぬこと）有（ま）しますと。助けまつらむとして兵（つはもの）を備（そな）へて待ちたてまつる」}}As a character in the " [[Nihon Shoki]] ," he appears in relatively many places. Volume 11 of the Nihon Shoki records a dispute over the Yamato military fields and warehouses between [[:ja:額田大中彦皇子|Prince Nukata no]] [[:ja:屯田|Onakahiko]] and the Military Field Commander, [[:ja:淤宇宿禰|Ounosukune]], which took place after the death of the Emperor in what is [[Emperor Ōjin|believed]] to be 310 (the 41st year of the reign of Emperor Ojin) and [[:ja:屯倉|the Imperial Throne]] was in a state of uncertainty. When Prince Nukata no Oonakahiko unilaterally confiscated his land, Ousukune appealed to Uji no Wakairoko and then to Osazaki no Mikoto (later [[Emperor Nintoku]] ), and it was discovered that Agoko, who was currently stationed in Karakuni, knew about the Wa military fields and military storehouses. Following the advice of Ootori-no-Mikoto, Ousukune traveled day and night to Korea with Awaji fishermen and returned with the child's basket. Akogo testified that the "Tonden and Tonkura of Wa" were passed down to Emperor Keikō, who was [[Emperor Keikō|the crown prince]] during the reign of [[Emperor Suinin]], saying, "Generally, the Tonden of Wa are the Tonden of the current emperor. Even if one is the son of the emperor, he cannot be in charge unless he is the emperor's son," and that they were under the control of the emperor of the time. This caused Prince Nukata-Onakahiko to reflect on his actions, and the land management issue was resolved in Ousukune's favor. The [[Kojiki]] makes no mention of such circumstances. === Presentation from the Shishitobe === It is said that the Hihime who appears here and Sumiyoshi's younger sister, Hinohime, are the same person, and that there may be some confusion in the legends. The above description needs to be considered in conjunction with historical facts uncovered by archaeology, which show that the chiefs who became the ancestors of the Izumo no Omi clan in the first half of the 5th century were deeply involved with the Yamato government and engaged in negotiations with the Korean Peninsula. Furthermore, it is necessary to look at the connections with [[:ja:淡路島|the Awaji Island]] fishermen group and the relationship with the {{ill|Nomi no Sukune|en}} legend. == Research == A group of fishermen from Awaji Island appears frequently in the aforementioned story; sailors from this group were active when Ousukune went to retrieve the Akoko basket from Korea; and in the legend of Prince Sumiyoshi Nakatsu, "fishermen from Nojima on Awaji" are secretly active, led by [[:ja:阿曇浜子|Azumi no Muraji Hamako]] . Many artifacts indicating connections to the peninsula and Izumo have been excavated from the Kidohara and Uryu ruins on Awaji Island. Jasper rough stones from [[:ja:玉湯町|Kasenyama]] in Tamayu-cho, [[Matsue|Matsue City]] have been excavated from jade-making sites in the Kinai region, such as the Soga Site, Furu [[:ja:布留遺跡|Site]], and Nagahara Site. In particular, jade-making sites using Izumo-style stone materials such as jasper and quartz have been found at the Tani Site near Ise, the base of the Yamato [[:ja:磯城|Nao]] clan. Outside the Nara Basin, small amounts of remains have been excavated from the Nagahara ruins in Kawachi Province. In addition to Yayoi period ruins, the remains of a jade-making workshop thought to date from the end of the 4th century to the beginning of the 5th century have been discovered along the coasts of Lake Shinji and Lake Nakaumi, and whetstones made from crystalline schist mined in [[:ja:紀の川|the Yoshino River]] and [[:ja:紀の川|Kino River]] basins in Nara Prefecture were used. {{ill|Ichishi no Nagaochi|fr}}, an ancestor of Yamato Nao, appears in the legends of {{ill|Amenohiboko|en}} and is also said to have gone to Izumo to welcome Nomi no Sukune. Nomi no Sukune was famous for his [[:ja:当麻蹴速|sumo]] match with Tagima no Kehaya, and according to Kikuchi Teruo, this story is the origin of the rice farming ritual in which the spirits of the earth are calmed by sumo. In this story, the land of Tagima that Nomi no Sukune acquired was located at the point where the Nara Basin emerges from [[Osaka Bay|Osaka]] Bay via Takenouchi [[:ja:竹内峠|Pass]], where Sugawara Shrine is located, and it was a strategic transportation hub that also leads to [[:ja:葛城|Katsuragi]] to the south. The nearby Ota ruins are the remains of a settlement from the early Kofun period, and pottery from [[:ja:山陰地方|the San'in]] region estimated to date to the first half of the 4th century has also been excavated. This suggests that there was evidence of a connection with the San'in region around the "Tagima Path" from the time of Nomi no Sukune. As described above, the relationship between Yamato Nao, the Izumo forces, and the fishermen of Awaji Island in the Agokoro legend conveys some historical fact, and it is highly likely that these were condensed and linked together in one person called Waagokoro. == Family tree == Many clans may be descendants of Furutama no Mikoto. This includes the {{ill|Owari clan|ja|尾張氏|en}} and [[Yamato no Kuni no Miyatsuko]]. 國學院大學デジタルミュージアム|url=https://d-museum.kokugakuin.ac.jp/eos/detail/id=9159|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20231026183115/https://d-museum.kokugakuin.ac.jp/eos/detail/id=9159|archive-date=2023-10-26|access-date=2023-12-04}} There is a complex myth about the reign of [[Emperor Sujin]] and its link to the worship of [[Yamato Okunitama]] and [[Amaterasu]]. There was a crisis during his reign and eventually the worship of [[Amaterasu]] and [[Yamato Okunitama]] were moved out of the imperial palace to separate shrines. Worship of Amaterasu moved to [[Hibara Shrine]] and then many other shrines called {{ill|Moto-Ise Shrines|lt=|ja|元伊勢}} until eventually reaching [[Ise Jingu]]. By contrast the worship of [[Yamato Okunitama]] moved to [[Oyamato Shrine]], near [[Hibara Shrine]] and [[Omiwa Shrine]]. Yamato Okunitama was first entrusted to a daughter of [[Emperor Sujin]] named {{Ill|Nunaki-iri-hime|ja|渟名城入姫命|fr}}, but shortly afterwards, her health began to fail. It is recorded that she became emaciated and lost all of her hair, which rendered her unable to perform her duties.{{cite book|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=_oEfAAAAYAAJ|title=Nihongi: Chronicles of Japan from the Earliest Times to A.D. 697, Volume 2|author=Aston, William George.|date=1896|publisher=The Japan Society London|isbn=9780524053478|pages=150–164|author-link=William George Aston}} These efforts still did not alleviate the ongoing plague, so Sujin decreed that a [[divination]] be performed sometime during the 7th year of his reign, that would involve him making a trip to the plain of Kami-asaji, and invoking the [[Yaoyorozu no Kami|eighty myriad deities]]. After the divination, {{ill|Ichishi no Nagaochi|ja|市磯長尾市|fr}}, a descendant of {{ill|Saonetsuhiko|ja|椎根津彦|fr}} would conduct the rites pertaining to Okunitama, replacing the emaciated Nunaki-iri-hime. {{ill|Ichishi no Nagaochi|ja|市磯長尾市|fr}} would be the ancestor of the Yamato no Kuni no Miyatsuko.{{Cite web|title=Page:Nihongi by Aston.djvu/208|url=https://en.wikisource.org/wiki/Page:Nihongi_by_Aston.djvu/208|access-date=2023-10-24|website=en.wikisource.org|language=en}} {{ill|Yamato no Agoko|lt=Agoko no Sukune|ja|倭吾子籠}} was a notable member of the clan and governor of Yamato Province{{Cite web|date=April 2022|title=Episode 61: Bad Behavior and the People that Excuse It|url=https://sengokudaimyo.com/podcast/episode-61|access-date=2023-05-04|website=Sengoku Daimyo|language=en-US}} == record == By the way, in the twelfth volume of the "Nihon Shoki," [[Emperor Richū|Emperor Richu]] floats a two-pronged boat on Iware City Isoike Pond. 『日本書紀』履中天皇3年11月6日条 === The Yamato military fields and warehouses === Similarly, Volume 11 of the "Shoki" tells the following story: This is the story of how Akokoro remade a giant tree that had washed up on the Oi River into a boat. At this time, Akokoro was called "Yamato Nao." The Crown Prince, who was filled with suspicion, became suspicious of Agogo's true intentions and tried to kill him. So Akokoro felt humbled and offered his younger sister, Hinohime, as a tribute, and was spared the death penalty. From this time on, Yamato Nao began to offer court ladies as tribute. 『日本書紀』履中天皇即位前紀条 According to Volume 12 of the "Shoki," Prince Sumiyoshi Nakatsu and Yamato Naokogo were on close terms. Therefore, when Prince Naka rebelled against the Crown Prince, Prince Izahowake (later Emperor Richu), presumably in the year 399, he tried to side with Prince Naka and gathered several hundred elite soldiers at a place called "Kakihami no Kurusu" (said to be Kurusu-go, [[:ja:忍海郡|Oshikai County]] ) and waited for the Crown Prince. However, when he realized that the Crown Prince's troops were more numerous than he had expected, he changed his attitude. === Driftwood of the Oi River === Another part of the Richū Sokui Chronicle states that the Crown Prince, on his way to [[Isonokami Shrine]], encounters a young girl at the foot of Mt. Asuka and asks her about the safety of the journey.{{Quote frame|六十二年の夏五月（推定[[374年]]）に、[[遠淡海国造|遠江国司]]（とほつあふみのくに の みこともち）表上言（まう）さく、「大（おほ）きなる樹（き）有りて、[[大井川|大井河]]（おほゐがは）より流れて、河（かは）曲（くま）り停（とどま）れり。其大きさ十囲（とうだき＝30尺、およそ300メートル）。本（もと）は壱（ひとつ）にして末は両（またまた）なり」とまうす。時に倭直吾子籠（やまとのあたひあごこ）を遣（つかは）して船に造らしむ。而（しかう）して南海（みなみのみち）より運（めぐら）して、難波津（なにはのつ）に将（ゐ）て来（きた）りて、御船（みふね）に充（あ）てつ。『日本書紀』仁徳天皇62年5月条}}There are also situations where you are advised to do so. This shows that the Yamato Naochou clan was familiar with the geography of the surrounding area, to the extent that they were able to set up ambushes. "The mountains are filled with many soldiers. Please go around and cross the Tagima Pass." === Prince Sumiyoshi's Rebellion === The fourteenth volume of the "Shoki" tells the story of Emperor Yuryaku, who, in a fit of rage after a hunt at Mimase, killed Otsu no Umakai with the sword, and his mother, Empress {{ill|Oshisaka no Ōnakatsuhime|en}}, presenting the Wa court lady "Hinohime" to settle the matter. This conversation led to the establishment of [[:ja:宍人部|the Shishihitobe]] (the branch of the Shishihito clan), and the appointment of three members, including Kashiwadeno no Omi Nagano. In addition, the “Oyamato no Kuni no Miyatsuko Agogo no Sukune” presented Sahonoko Toriwake to the Shishihitobe, and “the Ministers of the Imperial Court, Tomo no Miyatsuko and Kuni no Miyatsuko, followed suit and continued to offer tribute.” 『日本書紀』雄略天皇2年10月6日条{{Quote frame|「伝（つて）に聞く、皇太子（ひつぎのみこ）、非常之事（おもほえぬこと）有（ま）しますと。助けまつらむとして兵（つはもの）を備（そな）へて待ちたてまつる」}}As a character in the " [[Nihon Shoki]] ," he appears in relatively many places. Volume 11 of the Nihon Shoki records a dispute over the Yamato military fields and warehouses between [[:ja:額田大中彦皇子|Prince Nukata no]] [[:ja:屯田|Onakahiko]] and the Military Field Commander, [[:ja:淤宇宿禰|Ounosukune]], which took place after the death of the Emperor in what is [[Emperor Ōjin|believed]] to be 310 (the 41st year of the reign of Emperor Ojin) and [[:ja:屯倉|the Imperial Throne]] was in a state of uncertainty. When Prince Nukata no Oonakahiko unilaterally confiscated his land, Ousukune appealed to Uji no Wakairoko and then to Osazaki no Mikoto (later [[Emperor Nintoku]] ), and it was discovered that Agoko, who was currently stationed in Karakuni, knew about the Wa military fields and military storehouses. Following the advice of Ootori-no-Mikoto, Ousukune traveled day and night to Korea with Awaji fishermen and returned with the child's basket. Akogo testified that the "Tonden and Tonkura of Wa" were passed down to Emperor Keikō, who was [[Emperor Keikō|the crown prince]] during the reign of [[Emperor Suinin]], saying, "Generally, the Tonden of Wa are the Tonden of the current emperor. Even if one is the son of the emperor, he cannot be in charge unless he is the emperor's son," and that they were under the control of the emperor of the time. This caused Prince Nukata-Onakahiko to reflect on his actions, and the land management issue was resolved in Ousukune's favor. The [[Kojiki]] makes no mention of such circumstances. === Presentation from the Shishitobe === It is said that the Hihime who appears here and Sumiyoshi's younger sister, Hinohime, are the same person, and that there may be some confusion in the legends. The above description needs to be considered in conjunction with historical facts uncovered by archaeology, which show that the chiefs who became the ancestors of the Izumo no Omi clan in the first half of the 5th century were deeply involved with the Yamato government and engaged in negotiations with the Korean Peninsula. Furthermore, it is necessary to look at the connections with [[:ja:淡路島|the Awaji Island]] fishermen group and the relationship with the {{ill|Nomi no Sukune|en}} legend. == Research == A group of fishermen from Awaji Island appears frequently in the aforementioned story; sailors from this group were active when Ousukune went to retrieve the Akoko basket from Korea; and in the legend of Prince Sumiyoshi Nakatsu, "fishermen from Nojima on Awaji" are secretly active, led by [[:ja:阿曇浜子|Azumi no Muraji Hamako]] . Many artifacts indicating connections to the peninsula and Izumo have been excavated from the Kidohara and Uryu ruins on Awaji Island. Jasper rough stones from [[:ja:玉湯町|Kasenyama]] in Tamayu-cho, [[Matsue|Matsue City]] have been excavated from jade-making sites in the Kinai region, such as the Soga Site, Furu [[:ja:布留遺跡|Site]], and Nagahara Site. In particular, jade-making sites using Izumo-style stone materials such as jasper and quartz have been found at the Tani Site near Ise, the base of the Yamato [[:ja:磯城|Nao]] clan. Outside the Nara Basin, small amounts of remains have been excavated from the Nagahara ruins in Kawachi Province. In addition to Yayoi period ruins, the remains of a jade-making workshop thought to date from the end of the 4th century to the beginning of the 5th century have been discovered along the coasts of Lake Shinji and Lake Nakaumi, and whetstones made from crystalline schist mined in [[:ja:紀の川|the Yoshino River]] and [[:ja:紀の川|Kino River]] basins in Nara Prefecture were used. {{ill|Ichishi no Nagaochi|fr}}, an ancestor of Yamato Nao, appears in the legends of {{ill|Amenohiboko|en}} and is also said to have gone to Izumo to welcome Nomi no Sukune. Nomi no Sukune was famous for his [[:ja:当麻蹴速|sumo]] match with Tagima no Kehaya, and according to Kikuchi Teruo, this story is the origin of the rice farming ritual in which the spirits of the earth are calmed by sumo. In this story, the land of Tagima that Nomi no Sukune acquired was located at the point where the Nara Basin emerges from [[Osaka Bay|Osaka]] Bay via Takenouchi [[:ja:竹内峠|Pass]], where Sugawara Shrine is located, and it was a strategic transportation hub that also leads to [[:ja:葛城|Katsuragi]] to the south. The nearby Ota ruins are the remains of a settlement from the early Kofun period, and pottery from [[:ja:山陰地方|the San'in]] region estimated to date to the first half of the 4th century has also been excavated. This suggests that there was evidence of a connection with the San'in region around the "Tagima Path" from the time of Nomi no Sukune. As described above, the relationship between Yamato Nao, the Izumo forces, and the fishermen of Awaji Island in the Agokoro legend conveys some historical fact, and it is highly likely that these were condensed and linked together in one person called Waagokoro. == Family tree == Many clans may be descendants of Furutama no Mikoto. This includes the {{ill|Owari clan|ja|尾張氏|en}} and [[Yamato no Kuni no Miyatsuko]]. Asuka and asks her about the safety of the journey.{{Quote frame|六十二年の夏五月（推定[[374年]]）に、[[遠淡海国造|遠江国司]]（とほつあふみのくに の みこともち）表上言（まう）さく、「大（おほ）きなる樹（き）有りて、[[大井川|大井河]]（おほゐがは）より流れて、河（かは）曲（くま）り停（とどま）れり。其大きさ十囲（とうだき＝30尺、およそ300メートル）。本（もと）は壱（ひとつ）にして末は両（またまた）なり」とまうす。時に倭直吾子籠（やまとのあたひあごこ）を遣（つかは）して船に造らしむ。而（しかう）して南海（みなみのみち）より運（めぐら）して、難波津（なにはのつ）に将（ゐ）て来（きた）りて、御船（みふね）に充（あ）てつ。『日本書紀』仁徳天皇62年5月条}}There are also situations where you are advised to do so. This shows that the Yamato Naochou clan was familiar with the geography of the surrounding area, to the extent that they were able to set up ambushes. "The mountains are filled with many soldiers. Please go around and cross the Tagima Pass." === Prince Sumiyoshi's Rebellion === The fourteenth volume of the "Shoki" tells the story of Emperor Yuryaku, who, in a fit of rage after a hunt at Mimase, killed Otsu no Umakai with the sword, and his mother, Empress {{ill|Oshisaka no Ōnakatsuhime|en}}, presenting the Wa court lady "Hinohime" to settle the matter. This conversation led to the establishment of [[:ja:宍人部|the Shishihitobe]] (the branch of the Shishihito clan), and the appointment of three members, including Kashiwadeno no Omi Nagano. In addition, the “Oyamato no Kuni no Miyatsuko Agogo no Sukune” presented Sahonoko Toriwake to the Shishihitobe, and “the Ministers of the Imperial Court, Tomo no Miyatsuko and Kuni no Miyatsuko, followed suit and continued to offer tribute.” 『日本書紀』雄略天皇2年10月6日条{{Quote frame|「伝（つて）に聞く、皇太子（ひつぎのみこ）、非常之事（おもほえぬこと）有（ま）しますと。助けまつらむとして兵（つはもの）を備（そな）へて待ちたてまつる」}}As a character in the " [[Nihon Shoki]] ," he appears in relatively many places. Volume 11 of the Nihon Shoki records a dispute over the Yamato military fields and warehouses between [[:ja:額田大中彦皇子|Prince Nukata no]] [[:ja:屯田|Onakahiko]] and the Military Field Commander, [[:ja:淤宇宿禰|Ounosukune]], which took place after the death of the Emperor in what is [[Emperor Ōjin|believed]] to be 310 (the 41st year of the reign of Emperor Ojin) and [[:ja:屯倉|the Imperial Throne]] was in a state of uncertainty. When Prince Nukata no Oonakahiko unilaterally confiscated his land, Ousukune appealed to Uji no Wakairoko and then to Osazaki no Mikoto (later [[Emperor Nintoku]] ), and it was discovered that Agoko, who was currently stationed in Karakuni, knew about the Wa military fields and military storehouses. Following the advice of Ootori-no-Mikoto, Ousukune traveled day and night to Korea with Awaji fishermen and returned with the child's basket. Akogo testified that the "Tonden and Tonkura of Wa" were passed down to Emperor Keikō, who was [[Emperor Keikō|the crown prince]] during the reign of [[Emperor Suinin]], saying, "Generally, the Tonden of Wa are the Tonden of the current emperor. Even if one is the son of the emperor, he cannot be in charge unless he is the emperor's son," and that they were under the control of the emperor of the time. This caused Prince Nukata-Onakahiko to reflect on his actions, and the land management issue was resolved in Ousukune's favor. The [[Kojiki]] makes no mention of such circumstances. === Presentation from the Shishitobe === It is said that the Hihime who appears here and Sumiyoshi's younger sister, Hinohime, are the same person, and that there may be some confusion in the legends. The above description needs to be considered in conjunction with historical facts uncovered by archaeology, which show that the chiefs who became the ancestors of the Izumo no Omi clan in the first half of the 5th century were deeply involved with the Yamato government and engaged in negotiations with the Korean Peninsula. Furthermore, it is necessary to look at the connections with [[:ja:淡路島|the Awaji Island]] fishermen group and the relationship with the {{ill|Nomi no Sukune|en}} legend. == Research == A group of fishermen from Awaji Island appears frequently in the aforementioned story; sailors from this group were active when Ousukune went to retrieve the Akoko basket from Korea; and in the legend of Prince Sumiyoshi Nakatsu, "fishermen from Nojima on Awaji" are secretly active, led by [[:ja:阿曇浜子|Azumi no Muraji Hamako]] . Many artifacts indicating connections to the peninsula and Izumo have been excavated from the Kidohara and Uryu ruins on Awaji Island. Jasper rough stones from [[:ja:玉湯町|Kasenyama]] in Tamayu-cho, [[Matsue|Matsue City]] have been excavated from jade-making sites in the Kinai region, such as the Soga Site, Furu [[:ja:布留遺跡|Site]], and Nagahara Site. In particular, jade-making sites using Izumo-style stone materials such as jasper and quartz have been found at the Tani Site near Ise, the base of the Yamato [[:ja:磯城|Nao]] clan. Outside the Nara Basin, small amounts of remains have been excavated from the Nagahara ruins in Kawachi Province. In addition to Yayoi period ruins, the remains of a jade-making workshop thought to date from the end of the 4th century to the beginning of the 5th century have been discovered along the coasts of Lake Shinji and Lake Nakaumi, and whetstones made from crystalline schist mined in [[:ja:紀の川|the Yoshino River]] and [[:ja:紀の川|Kino River]] basins in Nara Prefecture were used. {{ill|Ichishi no Nagaochi|fr}}, an ancestor of Yamato Nao, appears in the legends of {{ill|Amenohiboko|en}} and is also said to have gone to Izumo to welcome Nomi no Sukune. Nomi no Sukune was famous for his [[:ja:当麻蹴速|sumo]] match with Tagima no Kehaya, and according to Kikuchi Teruo, this story is the origin of the rice farming ritual in which the spirits of the earth are calmed by sumo. In this story, the land of Tagima that Nomi no Sukune acquired was located at the point where the Nara Basin emerges from [[Osaka Bay|Osaka]] Bay via Takenouchi [[:ja:竹内峠|Pass]], where Sugawara Shrine is located, and it was a strategic transportation hub that also leads to [[:ja:葛城|Katsuragi]] to the south. The nearby Ota ruins are the remains of a settlement from the early Kofun period, and pottery from [[:ja:山陰地方|the San'in]] region estimated to date to the first half of the 4th century has also been excavated. This suggests that there was evidence of a connection with the San'in region around the "Tagima Path" from the time of Nomi no Sukune. As described above, the relationship between Yamato Nao, the Izumo forces, and the fishermen of Awaji Island in the Agokoro legend conveys some historical fact, and it is highly likely that these were condensed and linked together in one person called Waagokoro. == Family tree == Many clans may be descendants of Furutama no Mikoto. This includes the {{ill|Owari clan|ja|尾張氏|en}} and [[Yamato no Kuni no Miyatsuko]]. {{ill|Saonetsuhiko|ja|椎根津彦|fr}} was given the position of governor of [[Yamato Province]] by [[Emperor Jimmu]].{{Cite web|title=Friday: Kojiki (「乞食」ではなく『古事記』ですヨ！！) 國學院大學デジタルミュージアム|url=https://d-museum.kokugakuin.ac.jp/eos/detail/id=9159|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20231026183115/https://d-museum.kokugakuin.ac.jp/eos/detail/id=9159|archive-date=2023-10-26|access-date=2023-12-04}} There is a complex myth about the reign of [[Emperor Sujin]] and its link to the worship of [[Yamato Okunitama]] and [[Amaterasu]]. There was a crisis during his reign and eventually the worship of [[Amaterasu]] and [[Yamato Okunitama]] were moved out of the imperial palace to separate shrines. Worship of Amaterasu moved to [[Hibara Shrine]] and then many other shrines called {{ill|Moto-Ise Shrines|lt=|ja|元伊勢}} until eventually reaching [[Ise Jingu]]. By contrast the worship of [[Yamato Okunitama]] moved to [[Oyamato Shrine]], near [[Hibara Shrine]] and [[Omiwa Shrine]]. Yamato Okunitama was first entrusted to a daughter of [[Emperor Sujin]] named {{Ill|Nunaki-iri-hime|ja|渟名城入姫命|fr}}, but shortly afterwards, her health began to fail. It is recorded that she became emaciated and lost all of her hair, which rendered her unable to perform her duties.{{cite book|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=_oEfAAAAYAAJ|title=Nihongi: Chronicles of Japan from the Earliest Times to A.D. 697, Volume 2|author=Aston, William George.|date=1896|publisher=The Japan Society London|isbn=9780524053478|pages=150–164|author-link=William George Aston}} These efforts still did not alleviate the ongoing plague, so Sujin decreed that a [[divination]] be performed sometime during the 7th year of his reign, that would involve him making a trip to the plain of Kami-asaji, and invoking the [[Yaoyorozu no Kami|eighty myriad deities]]. After the divination, {{ill|Ichishi no Nagaochi|ja|市磯長尾市|fr}}, a descendant of {{ill|Saonetsuhiko|ja|椎根津彦|fr}} would conduct the rites pertaining to Okunitama, replacing the emaciated Nunaki-iri-hime. {{ill|Ichishi no Nagaochi|ja|市磯長尾市|fr}} would be the ancestor of the Yamato no Kuni no Miyatsuko.{{Cite web|title=Page:Nihongi by Aston.djvu/208|url=https://en.wikisource.org/wiki/Page:Nihongi_by_Aston.djvu/208|access-date=2023-10-24|website=en.wikisource.org|language=en}} {{ill|Yamato no Agoko|lt=Agoko no Sukune|ja|倭吾子籠}} was a notable member of the clan and governor of Yamato Province{{Cite web|date=April 2022|title=Episode 61: Bad Behavior and the People that Excuse It|url=https://sengokudaimyo.com/podcast/episode-61|access-date=2023-05-04|website=Sengoku Daimyo|language=en-US}} == record == By the way, in the twelfth volume of the "Nihon Shoki," [[Emperor Richū|Emperor Richu]] floats a two-pronged boat on Iware City Isoike Pond. 『日本書紀』履中天皇3年11月6日条 === The Yamato military fields and warehouses === Similarly, Volume 11 of the "Shoki" tells the following story: This is the story of how Akokoro remade a giant tree that had washed up on the Oi River into a boat. Jasper rough stones from [[:ja:玉湯町|Kasenyama]] in Tamayu-cho, [[Matsue|Matsue City]] have been excavated from jade-making sites in the Kinai region, such as the Soga Site, Furu [[:ja:布留遺跡|Site]], and Nagahara Site. In particular, jade-making sites using Izumo-style stone materials such as jasper and quartz have been found at the Tani Site near Ise, the base of the Yamato [[:ja:磯城|Nao]] clan. Outside the Nara Basin, small amounts of remains have been excavated from the Nagahara ruins in Kawachi Province. In addition to Yayoi period ruins, the remains of a jade-making workshop thought to date from the end of the 4th century to the beginning of the 5th century have been discovered along the coasts of Lake Shinji and Lake Nakaumi, and whetstones made from crystalline schist mined in [[:ja:紀の川|the Yoshino River]] and [[:ja:紀の川|Kino River]] basins in Nara Prefecture were used. {{ill|Ichishi no Nagaochi|fr}}, an ancestor of Yamato Nao, appears in the legends of {{ill|Amenohiboko|en}} and is also said to have gone to Izumo to welcome Nomi no Sukune. Nomi no Sukune was famous for his [[:ja:当麻蹴速|sumo]] match with Tagima no Kehaya, and according to Kikuchi Teruo, this story is the origin of the rice farming ritual in which the spirits of the earth are calmed by sumo. In this story, the land of Tagima that Nomi no Sukune acquired was located at the point where the Nara Basin emerges from [[Osaka Bay|Osaka]] Bay via Takenouchi [[:ja:竹内峠|Pass]], where Sugawara Shrine is located, and it was a strategic transportation hub that also leads to [[:ja:葛城|Katsuragi]] to the south. The nearby Ota ruins are the remains of a settlement from the early Kofun period, and pottery from [[:ja:山陰地方|the San'in]] region estimated to date to the first half of the 4th century has also been excavated. This suggests that there was evidence of a connection with the San'in region around the "Tagima Path" from the time of Nomi no Sukune. As described above, the relationship between Yamato Nao, the Izumo forces, and the fishermen of Awaji Island in the Agokoro legend conveys some historical fact, and it is highly likely that these were condensed and linked together in one person called Waagokoro. == Family tree == Many clans may be descendants of Furutama no Mikoto. This includes the {{ill|Owari clan|ja|尾張氏|en}} and [[Yamato no Kuni no Miyatsuko]]. 1|access-date=2023-05-04}} [[ja:倭吾子籠]] [[en:draft:Yamato no Agoko]] == History == [[File:Hibara-jinja,_torii_closeup.jpg|thumb|240x240px|[[Hibara Shrine]], at the foot of [[Mount Miwa]] in [[Sakurai, Nara]], identified as the place where the Yata-no-Kagami and the Kusanagi-no-Tsurugi were first enshrined after their removal from the imperial palace.]] During [[Jimmu's Eastern Expedition]] {{ill|Saonetsuhiko|ja|椎根津彦|fr}} was given the position of governor of [[Yamato Province]] by [[Emperor Jimmu]].{{Cite web|title=Friday: Kojiki (「乞食」ではなく『古事記』ですヨ！！) #26|url=https://japaneseexperts.net/972/|access-date=2023-05-04|website=Japanese Experts Net|language=en-US}} And Saonetsuhiko became their ancestor.{{Cite web|date=2023-10-26|title=Saonetsuhiko {{!}} 國學院大學デジタルミュージアム|url=https://d-museum.kokugakuin.ac.jp/eos/detail/id=9159|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20231026183115/https://d-museum.kokugakuin.ac.jp/eos/detail/id=9159|archive-date=2023-10-26|access-date=2023-12-04}} There is a complex myth about the reign of [[Emperor Sujin]] and its link to the worship of [[Yamato Okunitama]] and [[Amaterasu]]. There was a crisis during his reign and eventually the worship of [[Amaterasu]] and [[Yamato Okunitama]] were moved out of the imperial palace to separate shrines. Worship of Amaterasu moved to [[Hibara Shrine]] and then many other shrines called {{ill|Moto-Ise Shrines|lt=|ja|元伊勢}} until eventually reaching [[Ise Jingu]]. By contrast the worship of [[Yamato Okunitama]] moved to [[Oyamato Shrine]], near [[Hibara Shrine]] and [[Omiwa Shrine]]. Yamato Okunitama was first entrusted to a daughter of [[Emperor Sujin]] named {{Ill|Nunaki-iri-hime|ja|渟名城入姫命|fr}}, but shortly afterwards, her health began to fail. It is recorded that she became emaciated and lost all of her hair, which rendered her unable to perform her duties.{{cite book|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=_oEfAAAAYAAJ|title=Nihongi: Chronicles of Japan from the Earliest Times to A.D. 697, Volume 2|author=Aston, William George.|date=1896|publisher=The Japan Society London|isbn=9780524053478|pages=150–164|author-link=William George Aston}} These efforts still did not alleviate the ongoing plague, so Sujin decreed that a [[divination]] be performed sometime during the 7th year of his reign, that would involve him making a trip to the plain of Kami-asaji, and invoking the [[Yaoyorozu no Kami|eighty myriad deities]]. After the divination, {{ill|Ichishi no Nagaochi|ja|市磯長尾市|fr}}, a descendant of {{ill|Saonetsuhiko|ja|椎根津彦|fr}} would conduct the rites pertaining to Okunitama, replacing the emaciated Nunaki-iri-hime. {{ill|Ichishi no Nagaochi|ja|市磯長尾市|fr}} would be the ancestor of the Yamato no Kuni no Miyatsuko.{{Cite web|title=Page:Nihongi by Aston.djvu/208|url=https://en.wikisource.org/wiki/Page:Nihongi_by_Aston.djvu/208|access-date=2023-10-24|website=en.wikisource.org|language=en}} {{ill|Yamato no Agoko|lt=Agoko no Sukune|ja|倭吾子籠}} was a notable member of the clan and governor of Yamato Province{{Cite web|date=April 2022|title=Episode 61: Bad Behavior and the People that Excuse It|url=https://sengokudaimyo.com/podcast/episode-61|access-date=2023-05-04|website=Sengoku Daimyo|language=en-US}} == record == By the way, in the twelfth volume of the "Nihon Shoki," [[Emperor Richū|Emperor Richu]] floats a two-pronged boat on Iware City Isoike Pond. 『日本書紀』履中天皇3年11月6日条 === The Yamato military fields and warehouses === Similarly, Volume 11 of the "Shoki" tells the following story: This is the story of how Akokoro remade a giant tree that had washed up on the Oi River into a boat. At this time, Akokoro was called "Yamato Nao." The Crown Prince, who was filled with suspicion, became suspicious of Agogo's true intentions and tried to kill him. So Akokoro felt humbled and offered his younger sister, Hinohime, as a tribute, and was spared the death penalty. From this time on, Yamato Nao began to offer court ladies as tribute. 『日本書紀』履中天皇即位前紀条 According to Volume 12 of the "Shoki," Prince Sumiyoshi Nakatsu and Yamato Naokogo were on close terms. Therefore, when Prince Naka rebelled against the Crown Prince, Prince Izahowake (later Emperor Richu), presumably in the year 399, he tried to side with Prince Naka and gathered several hundred elite soldiers at a place called "Kakihami no Kurusu" (said to be Kurusu-go, {{ill|10=ja|11=忍海郡|Oshikai County}} ) and waited for the Crown Prince. However, when he realized that the Crown Prince's troops were more numerous than he had expected, he changed his attitude. === Driftwood of the Oi River === Another part of the Richū Sokui Chronicle states that the Crown Prince, on his way to [[Isonokami Shrine]], encounters a young girl at the foot of Mt. Asuka and asks her about the safety of the journey.{{Quote frame|六十二年の夏五月（推定[[374年]]）に、[[遠淡海国造|遠江国司]]（とほつあふみのくに の みこともち）表上言（まう）さく、「大（おほ）きなる樹（き）有りて、[[大井川|大井河]]（おほゐがは）より流れて、河（かは）曲（くま）り停（とどま）れり。其大きさ十囲（とうだき＝30尺、およそ300メートル）。本（もと）は壱（ひとつ）にして末は両（またまた）なり」とまうす。時に倭直吾子籠（やまとのあたひあごこ）を遣（つかは）して船に造らしむ。而（しかう）して南海（みなみのみち）より運（めぐら）して、難波津（なにはのつ）に将（ゐ）て来（きた）りて、御船（みふね）に充（あ）てつ。『日本書紀』仁徳天皇62年5月条}}There are also situations where you are advised to do so. This shows that the Yamato Naochou clan was familiar with the geography of the surrounding area, to the extent that they were able to set up ambushes. "The mountains are filled with many soldiers. Please go around and cross the Tagima Pass." === Prince Sumiyoshi's Rebellion === The fourteenth volume of the "Shoki" tells the story of Emperor Yuryaku, who, in a fit of rage after a hunt at Mimase, killed Otsu no Umakai with the sword, and his mother, Empress {{ill|Oshisaka no Ōnakatsuhime|en}}, presenting the Wa court lady "Hinohime" to settle the matter. This conversation led to the establishment of {{ill|10=ja|11=宍人部|the Shishihitobe}} (the branch of the Shishihito clan), and the appointment of three members, including Kashiwadeno no Omi Nagano. In addition, the “Oyamato no Kuni no Miyatsuko Agogo no Sukune” presented Sahonoko Toriwake to the Shishihitobe, and “the Ministers of the Imperial Court, Tomo no Miyatsuko and Kuni no Miyatsuko, followed suit and continued to offer tribute.” 『日本書紀』雄略天皇2年10月6日条{{Quote frame|「伝（つて）に聞く、皇太子（ひつぎのみこ）、非常之事（おもほえぬこと）有（ま）しますと。助けまつらむとして兵（つはもの）を備（そな）へて待ちたてまつる」}}As a character in the " [[Nihon Shoki]] ," he appears in relatively many places. Volume 11 of the Nihon Shoki records a dispute over the Yamato military fields and warehouses between {{ill|10=ja|11=額田大中彦皇子|Prince Nukata no}} {{ill|10=ja|11=屯田|Onakahiko}} and the Military Field Commander, {{ill|10=ja|11=淤宇宿禰|Ounosukune}}, which took place after the death of the Emperor in what is [[Emperor Ōjin|believed]] to be 310 (the 41st year of the reign of Emperor Ojin) and {{ill|10=ja|11=屯倉|the Imperial Throne}} was in a state of uncertainty. When Prince Nukata no Oonakahiko unilaterally confiscated his land, Ousukune appealed to Uji no Wakairoko and then to Osazaki no Mikoto (later [[Emperor Nintoku]] ), and it was discovered that Agoko, who was currently stationed in Karakuni, knew about the Wa military fields and military storehouses. Following the advice of Ootori-no-Mikoto, Ousukune traveled day and night to Korea with Awaji fishermen and returned with the child's basket. Akogo testified that the "Tonden and Tonkura of Wa" were passed down to Emperor Keikō, who was [[Emperor Keikō|the crown prince]] during the reign of [[Emperor Suinin]], saying, "Generally, the Tonden of Wa are the Tonden of the current emperor. Even if one is the son of the emperor, he cannot be in charge unless he is the emperor's son," and that they were under the control of the emperor of the time. This caused Prince Nukata-Onakahiko to reflect on his actions, and the land management issue was resolved in Ousukune's favor. The [[Kojiki]] makes no mention of such circumstances. === Presentation from the Shishitobe === It is said that the Hihime who appears here and Sumiyoshi's younger sister, Hinohime, are the same person, and that there may be some confusion in the legends. There is no mention of him in the [[Kojiki]] . == Origin == {{Short description|Japanese noble family}}{{Infobox Japanese clan|province of origin=[[Yamato Province]]|home province=[[Yamato Province]]|image=Ohyamato-jinja Haiden.jpg|image caption=Oyamato Shrine, their main shrine|founder={{ill|Shinetsuhiko|ja|椎根津彦}},

Their [[Ujigami]] or clan god is [[Yamato Okunitama]] of [[Ōyamato Shrine]]{{Cite web|title=International Symposium "Perspectives on Japanese history and literature from ancient historical records"|url=https://www.waseda.jp/inst/sgu/news-en/2019/04/12/5171|access-date=2023-05-04|website=Top Global University Project: Waseda Goes Global|language=en}} Some scholars interpret the ''kami'' 1|access-date=2023-05-04}} [[ja:倭吾子籠]] [[en:draft:Yamato no Agoko]] == History == [[File:Hibara-jinja,_torii_closeup.jpg|thumb|240x240px|[[Hibara Shrine]], at the foot of [[Mount Miwa]] in [[Sakurai, Nara]], identified as the place where the Yata-no-Kagami and the Kusanagi-no-Tsurugi were first enshrined after their removal from the imperial palace.]] During [[Jimmu's Eastern Expedition]] {{ill|Saonetsuhiko|ja|椎根津彦|fr}} was given the position of governor of [[Yamato Province]] by [[Emperor Jimmu]].{{Cite web|title=Friday: Kojiki (「乞食」ではなく『古事記』ですヨ！！) #26|url=https://japaneseexperts.net/972/|access-date=2023-05-04|website=Japanese Experts Net|language=en-US}} And Saonetsuhiko became their ancestor.{{Cite web|date=2023-10-26|title=Saonetsuhiko {{!}} 國學院大學デジタルミュージアム|url=https://d-museum.kokugakuin.ac.jp/eos/detail/id=9159|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20231026183115/https://d-museum.kokugakuin.ac.jp/eos/detail/id=9159|archive-date=2023-10-26|access-date=2023-12-04}} There is a complex myth about the reign of [[Emperor Sujin]] and its link to the worship of [[Yamato Okunitama]] and [[Amaterasu]]. There was a crisis during his reign and eventually the worship of [[Amaterasu]] and [[Yamato Okunitama]] were moved out of the imperial palace to separate shrines. Worship of Amaterasu moved to [[Hibara Shrine]] and then many other shrines called {{ill|Moto-Ise Shrines|lt=|ja|元伊勢}} until eventually reaching [[Ise Jingu]]. By contrast the worship of [[Yamato Okunitama]] moved to [[Oyamato Shrine]], near [[Hibara Shrine]] and [[Omiwa Shrine]]. Yamato Okunitama was first entrusted to a daughter of [[Emperor Sujin]] named {{Ill|Nunaki-iri-hime|ja|渟名城入姫命|fr}}, but shortly afterwards, her health began to fail. It is recorded that she became emaciated and lost all of her hair, which rendered her unable to perform her duties.{{cite book|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=_oEfAAAAYAAJ|title=Nihongi: Chronicles of Japan from the Earliest Times to A.D. 697, Volume 2|author=Aston, William George.|date=1896|publisher=The Japan Society London|isbn=9780524053478|pages=150–164|author-link=William George Aston}} These efforts still did not alleviate the ongoing plague, so Sujin decreed that a [[divination]] be performed sometime during the 7th year of his reign, that would involve him making a trip to the plain of Kami-asaji, and invoking the [[Yaoyorozu no Kami|eighty myriad deities]]. After the divination, {{ill|Ichishi no Nagaochi|ja|市磯長尾市|fr}}, a descendant of {{ill|Saonetsuhiko|ja|椎根津彦|fr}} would conduct the rites pertaining to Okunitama, replacing the emaciated Nunaki-iri-hime. {{ill|Ichishi no Nagaochi|ja|市磯長尾市|fr}} would be the ancestor of the Yamato no Kuni no Miyatsuko.{{Cite web|title=Page:Nihongi by Aston.djvu/208|url=https://en.wikisource.org/wiki/Page:Nihongi_by_Aston.djvu/208|access-date=2023-10-24|website=en.wikisource.org|language=en}} {{ill|Yamato no Agoko|lt=Agoko no Sukune|ja|倭吾子籠}} was a notable member of the clan and governor of Yamato Province{{Cite web|date=April 2022|title=Episode 61: Bad Behavior and the People that Excuse It|url=https://sengokudaimyo.com/podcast/episode-61|access-date=2023-05-04|website=Sengoku Daimyo|language=en-US}} == record == By the way, in the twelfth volume of the "Nihon Shoki," [[Emperor Richū|Emperor Richu]] floats a two-pronged boat on Iware City Isoike Pond. 『日本書紀』履中天皇3年11月6日条 === The Yamato military fields and warehouses === Similarly, Volume 11 of the "Shoki" tells the following story: This is the story of how Akokoro remade a giant tree that had washed up on the Oi River into a boat. At this time, Akokoro was called "Yamato Nao." The Crown Prince, who was filled with suspicion, became suspicious of Agogo's true intentions and tried to kill him. So Akokoro felt humbled and offered his younger sister, Hinohime, as a tribute, and was spared the death penalty. From this time on, Yamato Nao began to offer court ladies as tribute. 『日本書紀』履中天皇即位前紀条 According to Volume 12 of the "Shoki," Prince Sumiyoshi Nakatsu and Yamato Naokogo were on close terms. Therefore, when Prince Naka rebelled against the Crown Prince, Prince Izahowake (later Emperor Richu), presumably in the year 399, he tried to side with Prince Naka and gathered several hundred elite soldiers at a place called "Kakihami no Kurusu" (said to be Kurusu-go, {{ill|10=ja|11=忍海郡|Oshikai County}} ) and waited for the Crown Prince. However, when he realized that the Crown Prince's troops were more numerous than he had expected, he changed his attitude. === Driftwood of the Oi River === Another part of the Richū Sokui Chronicle states that the Crown Prince, on his way to [[Isonokami Shrine]], encounters a young girl at the foot of Mt. Asuka and asks her about the safety of the journey.{{Quote frame|六十二年の夏五月（推定[[374年]]）に、[[遠淡海国造|遠江国司]]（とほつあふみのくに の みこともち）表上言（まう）さく、「大（おほ）きなる樹（き）有りて、[[大井川|大井河]]（おほゐがは）より流れて、河（かは）曲（くま）り停（とどま）れり。其大きさ十囲（とうだき＝30尺、およそ300メートル）。本（もと）は壱（ひとつ）にして末は両（またまた）なり」とまうす。時に倭直吾子籠（やまとのあたひあごこ）を遣（つかは）して船に造らしむ。而（しかう）して南海（みなみのみち）より運（めぐら）して、難波津（なにはのつ）に将（ゐ）て来（きた）りて、御船（みふね）に充（あ）てつ。『日本書紀』仁徳天皇62年5月条}}There are also situations where you are advised to do so. This shows that the Yamato Naochou clan was familiar with the geography of the surrounding area, to the extent that they were able to set up ambushes. "The mountains are filled with many soldiers. Please go around and cross the Tagima Pass." === Prince Sumiyoshi's Rebellion === The fourteenth volume of the "Shoki" tells the story of Emperor Yuryaku, who, in a fit of rage after a hunt at Mimase, killed Otsu no Umakai with the sword, and his mother, Empress {{ill|Oshisaka no Ōnakatsuhime|en}}, presenting the Wa court lady "Hinohime" to settle the matter. This conversation led to the establishment of {{ill|10=ja|11=宍人部|the Shishihitobe}} (the branch of the Shishihito clan), and the appointment of three members, including Kashiwadeno no Omi Nagano. In addition, the “Oyamato no Kuni no Miyatsuko Agogo no Sukune” presented Sahonoko Toriwake to the Shishihitobe, and “the Ministers of the Imperial Court, Tomo no Miyatsuko and Kuni no Miyatsuko, followed suit and continued to offer tribute.” 『日本書紀』雄略天皇2年10月6日条{{Quote frame|「伝（つて）に聞く、皇太子（ひつぎのみこ）、非常之事（おもほえぬこと）有（ま）しますと。助けまつらむとして兵（つはもの）を備（そな）へて待ちたてまつる」}}As a character in the " [[Nihon Shoki]] ," he appears in relatively many places. Volume 11 of the Nihon Shoki records a dispute over the Yamato military fields and warehouses between {{ill|10=ja|11=額田大中彦皇子|Prince Nukata no}} {{ill|10=ja|11=屯田|Onakahiko}} and the Military Field Commander, {{ill|10=ja|11=淤宇宿禰|Ounosukune}}, which took place after the death of the Emperor in what is [[Emperor Ōjin|believed]] to be 310 (the 41st year of the reign of Emperor Ojin) and {{ill|10=ja|11=屯倉|the Imperial Throne}} was in a state of uncertainty. When Prince Nukata no Oonakahiko unilaterally confiscated his land, Ousukune appealed to Uji no Wakairoko and then to Osazaki no Mikoto (later [[Emperor Nintoku]] ), and it was discovered that Agoko, who was currently stationed in Karakuni, knew about the Wa military fields and military storehouses. Following the advice of Ootori-no-Mikoto, Ousukune traveled day and night to Korea with Awaji fishermen and returned with the child's basket. Akogo testified that the "Tonden and Tonkura of Wa" were passed down to Emperor Keikō, who was [[Emperor Keikō|the crown prince]] during the reign of [[Emperor Suinin]], saying, "Generally, the Tonden of Wa are the Tonden of the current emperor. Even if one is the son of the emperor, he cannot be in charge unless he is the emperor's son," and that they were under the control of the emperor of the time. This caused Prince Nukata-Onakahiko to reflect on his actions, and the land management issue was resolved in Ousukune's favor. The [[Kojiki]] makes no mention of such circumstances. === Presentation from the Shishitobe === It is said that the Hihime who appears here and Sumiyoshi's younger sister, Hinohime, are the same person, and that there may be some confusion in the legends. The above description needs to be considered in conjunction with historical facts uncovered by archaeology, which show that the chiefs who became the ancestors of the Izumo no Omi clan in the first half of the 5th century were deeply involved with the Yamato government and engaged in negotiations with the Korean Peninsula. Furthermore, it is necessary to look at the connections with {{ill|10=ja|11=淡路島|the Awaji Island}} fishermen group and the relationship with the {{ill|Nomi no Sukune|en}} legend. == Research == A group of fishermen from Awaji Island appears frequently in the aforementioned story; sailors from this group were active when Ousukune went to retrieve the Akoko basket from Korea; and in the legend of Prince Sumiyoshi Nakatsu, "fishermen from Nojima on Awaji" are secretly active, led by {{ill|10=ja|11=阿曇浜子|Azumi no Muraji Hamako}}. Many artifacts indicating connections to the peninsula and Izumo have been excavated from the Kidohara and Uryu ruins on Awaji Island. Jasper rough stones from {{ill|10=ja|11=玉湯町|Kasenyama}} in Tamayu-cho, [[Matsue|Matsue City]] have been excavated from jade-making sites in the Kinai region, such as the Soga Site, Furu {{ill|10=ja|11=布留遺跡|Site}}, and Nagahara Site. In particular, jade-making sites using Izumo-style stone materials such as jasper and quartz have been found at the Tani Site near Ise, the base of the Yamato {{ill|10=ja|11=磯城|Nao}} clan. Outside the Nara Basin, small amounts of remains have been excavated from the Nagahara ruins in Kawachi Province. In addition to Yayoi period ruins, the remains of a jade-making workshop thought to date from the end of the 4th century to the beginning of the 5th century have been discovered along the coasts of Lake Shinji and Lake Nakaumi, and whetstones made from crystalline schist mined in {{ill|10=ja|11=紀の川|the Yoshino River}} and {{ill|10=ja|11=紀の川|Kino River}} basins in Nara Prefecture were used. {{ill|Ichishi no Nagaochi|fr}}, an ancestor of Yamato Nao, appears in the legends of {{ill|Amenohiboko|en}} and is also said to have gone to Izumo to welcome Nomi no Sukune. Nomi no Sukune was famous for his {{ill|10=ja|11=当麻蹴速|sumo}} match with Tagima no Kehaya, and according to Kikuchi Teruo, this story is the origin of the rice farming ritual in which the spirits of the earth are calmed by sumo. In this story, the land of Tagima that Nomi no Sukune acquired was located at the point where the Nara Basin emerges from [[Osaka Bay|Osaka]] Bay via Takenouchi {{ill|10=ja|11=竹内峠|Pass}}, where Sugawara Shrine is located, and it was a strategic transportation hub that also leads to {{ill|10=ja|11=葛城|Katsuragi}} to the south. The nearby Ota ruins are the remains of a settlement from the early Kofun period, and pottery from {{ill|10=ja|11=山陰地方|the San'in}} region estimated to date to the first half of the 4th century has also been excavated. This suggests that there was evidence of a connection with the San'in region around the "Tagima Path" from the time of Nomi no Sukune. As described above, the relationship between Yamato Nao, the Izumo forces, and the fishermen of Awaji Island in the Agokoro legend conveys some historical fact, and it is highly likely that these were condensed and linked together in one person called Waagokoro. == Family tree == Many clans may be descendants of Furutama no Mikoto. This includes the {{ill|Owari clan|ja|尾張氏|en}} and [[Yamato no Kuni no Miyatsuko]]. 1|access-date=2023-05-04}} [[ja:倭吾子籠]] [[en:draft:Yamato no Agoko]] == History == [[File:Hibara-jinja,_torii_closeup.jpg|thumb|240x240px|[[Hibara Shrine]], at the foot of [[Mount Miwa]] in [[Sakurai, Nara]], identified as the place where the Yata-no-Kagami and the Kusanagi-no-Tsurugi were first enshrined after their removal from the imperial palace.]] During [[Jimmu's Eastern Expedition]] {{ill|Saonetsuhiko|ja|椎根津彦|fr}} was given the position of governor of [[Yamato Province]] by [[Emperor Jimmu]].{{Cite web|title=Friday: Kojiki (「乞食」ではなく『古事記』ですヨ！！) #26|url=https://japaneseexperts.net/972/|access-date=2023-05-04|website=Japanese Experts Net|language=en-US}} And Saonetsuhiko became their ancestor.{{Cite web|date=2023-10-26|title=Saonetsuhiko {{!}} 國學院大學デジタルミュージアム|url=https://d-museum.kokugakuin.ac.jp/eos/detail/id=9159|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20231026183115/https://d-museum.kokugakuin.ac.jp/eos/detail/id=9159|archive-date=2023-10-26|access-date=2023-12-04}} There is a complex myth about the reign of [[Emperor Sujin]] and its link to the worship of [[Yamato Okunitama]] and [[Amaterasu]]. There was a crisis during his reign and eventually the worship of [[Amaterasu]] and [[Yamato Okunitama]] were moved out of the imperial palace to separate shrines. Worship of Amaterasu moved to [[Hibara Shrine]] and then many other shrines called {{ill|Moto-Ise Shrines|lt=|ja|元伊勢}} until eventually reaching [[Ise Jingu]]. By contrast the worship of [[Yamato Okunitama]] moved to [[Oyamato Shrine]], near [[Hibara Shrine]] and [[Omiwa Shrine]]. Yamato Okunitama was first entrusted to a daughter of [[Emperor Sujin]] named {{Ill|Nunaki-iri-hime|ja|渟名城入姫命|fr}}, but shortly afterwards, her health began to fail. It is recorded that she became emaciated and lost all of her hair, which rendered her unable to perform her duties.{{cite book|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=_oEfAAAAYAAJ|title=Nihongi: Chronicles of Japan from the Earliest Times to A.D. 697, Volume 2|author=Aston, William George.|date=1896|publisher=The Japan Society London|isbn=9780524053478|pages=150–164|author-link=William George Aston}} These efforts still did not alleviate the ongoing plague, so Sujin decreed that a [[divination]] be performed sometime during the 7th year of his reign, that would involve him making a trip to the plain of Kami-asaji, and invoking the [[Yaoyorozu no Kami|eighty myriad deities]]. After the divination, {{ill|Ichishi no Nagaochi|ja|市磯長尾市|fr}}, a descendant of {{ill|Saonetsuhiko|ja|椎根津彦|fr}} would conduct the rites pertaining to Okunitama, replacing the emaciated Nunaki-iri-hime. {{ill|Ichishi no Nagaochi|ja|市磯長尾市|fr}} would be the ancestor of the Yamato no Kuni no Miyatsuko.{{Cite web|title=Page:Nihongi by Aston.djvu/208|url=https://en.wikisource.org/wiki/Page:Nihongi_by_Aston.djvu/208|access-date=2023-10-24|website=en.wikisource.org|language=en}} {{ill|Yamato no Agoko|lt=Agoko no Sukune|ja|倭吾子籠}} was a notable member of the clan and governor of Yamato Province{{Cite web|date=April 2022|title=Episode 61: Bad Behavior and the People that Excuse It|url=https://sengokudaimyo.com/podcast/episode-61|access-date=2023-05-04|website=Sengoku Daimyo|language=en-US}} == record == By the way, in the twelfth volume of the "Nihon Shoki," [[Emperor Richū|Emperor Richu]] floats a two-pronged boat on Iware City Isoike Pond. 『日本書紀』履中天皇3年11月6日条 === The Yamato military fields and warehouses === Similarly, Volume 11 of the "Shoki" tells the following story: This is the story of how Akokoro remade a giant tree that had washed up on the Oi River into a boat. At this time, Akokoro was called "Yamato Nao." The Crown Prince, who was filled with suspicion, became suspicious of Agogo's true intentions and tried to kill him. So Akokoro felt humbled and offered his younger sister, Hinohime, as a tribute, and was spared the death penalty. From this time on, Yamato Nao began to offer court ladies as tribute. 『日本書紀』履中天皇即位前紀条 According to Volume 12 of the "Shoki," Prince Sumiyoshi Nakatsu and Yamato Naokogo were on close terms. Therefore, when Prince Naka rebelled against the Crown Prince, Prince Izahowake (later Emperor Richu), presumably in the year 399, he tried to side with Prince Naka and gathered several hundred elite soldiers at a place called "Kakihami no Kurusu" (said to be Kurusu-go, {{ill|10=ja|11=忍海郡|Oshikai County}} ) and waited for the Crown Prince. However, when he realized that the Crown Prince's troops were more numerous than he had expected, he changed his attitude. === Driftwood of the Oi River === Another part of the Richū Sokui Chronicle states that the Crown Prince, on his way to [[Isonokami Shrine]], encounters a young girl at the foot of Mt. Asuka and asks her about the safety of the journey.{{Quote frame|六十二年の夏五月（推定[[374年]]）に、[[遠淡海国造|遠江国司]]（とほつあふみのくに の みこともち）表上言（まう）さく、「大（おほ）きなる樹（き）有りて、[[大井川|大井河]]（おほゐがは）より流れて、河（かは）曲（くま）り停（とどま）れり。其大きさ十囲（とうだき＝30尺、およそ300メートル）。本（もと）は壱（ひとつ）にして末は両（またまた）なり」とまうす。時に倭直吾子籠（やまとのあたひあごこ）を遣（つかは）して船に造らしむ。而（しかう）して南海（みなみのみち）より運（めぐら）して、難波津（なにはのつ）に将（ゐ）て来（きた）りて、御船（みふね）に充（あ）てつ。『日本書紀』仁徳天皇62年5月条}}There are also situations where you are advised to do so. This shows that the Yamato Naochou clan was familiar with the geography of the surrounding area, to the extent that they were able to set up ambushes. "The mountains are filled with many soldiers. Please go around and cross the Tagima Pass." === Prince Sumiyoshi's Rebellion === The fourteenth volume of the "Shoki" tells the story of Emperor Yuryaku, who, in a fit of rage after a hunt at Mimase, killed Otsu no Umakai with the sword, and his mother, Empress {{ill|Oshisaka no Ōnakatsuhime|en}}, presenting the Wa court lady "Hinohime" to settle the matter. This conversation led to the establishment of {{ill|10=ja|11=宍人部|the Shishihitobe}} (the branch of the Shishihito clan), and the appointment of three members, including Kashiwadeno no Omi Nagano. In addition, the “Oyamato no Kuni no Miyatsuko Agogo no Sukune” presented Sahonoko Toriwake to the Shishihitobe, and “the Ministers of the Imperial Court, Tomo no Miyatsuko and Kuni no Miyatsuko, followed suit and continued to offer tribute.” 『日本書紀』雄略天皇2年10月6日条{{Quote frame|「伝（つて）に聞く、皇太子（ひつぎのみこ）、非常之事（おもほえぬこと）有（ま）しますと。助けまつらむとして兵（つはもの）を備（そな）へて待ちたてまつる」}}As a character in the " [[Nihon Shoki]] ," he appears in relatively many places. Volume 11 of the Nihon Shoki records a dispute over the Yamato military fields and warehouses between {{ill|10=ja|11=額田大中彦皇子|Prince Nukata no}} {{ill|10=ja|11=屯田|Onakahiko}} and the Military Field Commander, {{ill|10=ja|11=淤宇宿禰|Ounosukune}}, which took place after the death of the Emperor in what is [[Emperor Ōjin|believed]] to be 310 (the 41st year of the reign of Emperor Ojin) and {{ill|10=ja|11=屯倉|the Imperial Throne}} was in a state of uncertainty. When Prince Nukata no Oonakahiko unilaterally confiscated his land, Ousukune appealed to Uji no Wakairoko and then to Osazaki no Mikoto (later [[Emperor Nintoku]] ), and it was discovered that Agoko, who was currently stationed in Karakuni, knew about the Wa military fields and military storehouses. Following the advice of Ootori-no-Mikoto, Ousukune traveled day and night to Korea with Awaji fishermen and returned with the child's basket. Akogo testified that the "Tonden and Tonkura of Wa" were passed down to Emperor Keikō, who was [[Emperor Keikō|the crown prince]] during the reign of [[Emperor Suinin]], saying, "Generally, the Tonden of Wa are the Tonden of the current emperor. Even if one is the son of the emperor, he cannot be in charge unless he is the emperor's son," and that they were under the control of the emperor of the time. This caused Prince Nukata-Onakahiko to reflect on his actions, and the land management issue was resolved in Ousukune's favor. The [[Kojiki]] makes no mention of such circumstances. === Presentation from the Shishitobe === It is said that the Hihime who appears here and Sumiyoshi's younger sister, Hinohime, are the same person, and that there may be some confusion in the legends. The above description needs to be considered in conjunction with historical facts uncovered by archaeology, which show that the chiefs who became the ancestors of the Izumo no Omi clan in the first half of the 5th century were deeply involved with the Yamato government and engaged in negotiations with the Korean Peninsula. Furthermore, it is necessary to look at the connections with {{ill|10=ja|11=淡路島|the Awaji Island}} fishermen group and the relationship with the {{ill|Nomi no Sukune|en}} legend. == Research == A group of fishermen from Awaji Island appears frequently in the aforementioned story; sailors from this group were active when Ousukune went to retrieve the Akoko basket from Korea; and in the legend of Prince Sumiyoshi Nakatsu, "fishermen from Nojima on Awaji" are secretly active, led by {{ill|10=ja|11=阿曇浜子|Azumi no Muraji Hamako}}. Many artifacts indicating connections to the peninsula and Izumo have been excavated from the Kidohara and Uryu ruins on Awaji Island. Jasper rough stones from {{ill|10=ja|11=玉湯町|Kasenyama}} in Tamayu-cho, [[Matsue|Matsue City]] have been excavated from jade-making sites in the Kinai region, such as the Soga Site, Furu {{ill|10=ja|11=布留遺跡|Site}}, and Nagahara Site. In particular, jade-making sites using Izumo-style stone materials such as jasper and quartz have been found at the Tani Site near Ise, the base of the Yamato {{ill|10=ja|11=磯城|Nao}} clan. Outside the Nara Basin, small amounts of remains have been excavated from the Nagahara ruins in Kawachi Province. In addition to Yayoi period ruins, the remains of a jade-making workshop thought to date from the end of the 4th century to the beginning of the 5th century have been discovered along the coasts of Lake Shinji and Lake Nakaumi, and whetstones made from crystalline schist mined in {{ill|10=ja|11=紀の川|the Yoshino River}} and {{ill|10=ja|11=紀の川|Kino River}} basins in Nara Prefecture were used. {{ill|Ichishi no Nagaochi|fr}}, an ancestor of Yamato Nao, appears in the legends of {{ill|Amenohiboko|en}} and is also said to have gone to Izumo to welcome Nomi no Sukune. Nomi no Sukune was famous for his {{ill|10=ja|11=当麻蹴速|sumo}} match with Tagima no Kehaya, and according to Kikuchi Teruo, this story is the origin of the rice farming ritual in which the spirits of the earth are calmed by sumo. In this story, the land of Tagima that Nomi no Sukune acquired was located at the point where the Nara Basin emerges from [[Osaka Bay|Osaka]] Bay via Takenouchi {{ill|10=ja|11=竹内峠|Pass}}, where Sugawara Shrine is located, and it was a strategic transportation hub that also leads to {{ill|10=ja|11=葛城|Katsuragi}} to the south. The nearby Ota ruins are the remains of a settlement from the early Kofun period, and pottery from {{ill|10=ja|11=山陰地方|the San'in}} region estimated to date to the first half of the 4th century has also been excavated. This suggests that there was evidence of a connection with the San'in region around the "Tagima Path" from the time of Nomi no Sukune. As described above, the relationship between Yamato Nao, the Izumo forces, and the fishermen of Awaji Island in the Agokoro legend conveys some historical fact, and it is highly likely that these were condensed and linked together in one person called Waagokoro. == Family tree == Many clans may be descendants of Furutama no Mikoto. This includes the {{ill|Owari clan|ja|尾張氏|en}} and [[Yamato no Kuni no Miyatsuko]]. This is a subject of debate.{{Cite web|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160422190938/http://wwr2.ucom.ne.jp/hetoyc15/keihu/amabe/amabe-k2.htm|access-date=2023-12-13|website=web.archive.org}} {{User:Immanuelle/Generations of Watatsumi}} == See also == * {{ill|Yamato Okunitama Shrine|ja|大和大国魂神社|simple}} * [[Kuni no miyatsuko]] * {{ill|Princess Yamato Totohi Momoso|en||fr|Yamatototohimomoso-hime}} * {{ill|10=ja|11=飛鳥時代以前の人物一覧|List of people before the Asuka period}} * {{ill|10=ja|11=倭の六県|The Six Prefectures of Wa}} * {{ill|10=ja|11=葛城|Katsuragi}} * {{ill|10=ja|11=大山守皇子|Prince Oyamamori}} * {{ill|10=ja|11=菟道稚郎子|Ujichi Wakako}} * {{ill|10=ja|11=住吉仲皇子|Prince Sumiyoshi}} * {{ill|10=ja|11=阿曇浜子|Azumi Hamako}} * {{ill|Ichishi no Nagaochi|fr}} == footnote == {{脚注ヘルプ}} == References == * Complete translation of the Kojiki: Japanese Classics 1, Shogakukan, 1983 * "Nihon Shoki" (vol. 2 and 3), Iwanami Bunko, 1994 * "Nihon Shoki" Complete Modern Japanese Translation (Vol. 1 and 2), Kodansha Academic Library, Translated by Ujitani Takeshi, 1988 == Notes == {{notelist}} === References === {{reflist}} === Bibliography === {{Refbegin}} ====''Nihon Shoki''==== ''See the references under {{Lang|ja-latn|[[Nihon Shoki]]}} for an extended bibliography'' *{{cite book|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=1IJrNAKBpycC&pg=PA299|title=Nihongi: Chronicles of Japan from the Earliest Times to A.D. 697|last=Aston|first=William George|publisher=Kegan Paul, Trench, Trubner (for the Japan Society of London)|year=1896|isbn=9780524053478|volume=1|place=London|oclc=448337491|author-link=William George Aston}}, [https://books.google.com/books?id=_oEfAAAAYAAJ alt-link] English translation * {{cite web|author=JHTI|year=2002|title=Nihon Shoki|url=https://jhti.berkeley.edu/Nihon%20shoki.html|access-date=2019-08-23|work=[[Japanese Historical Text Initiative]] (JHTI)|publisher=UC Berkeley}}, searchtext resource to retrieve kanbun text vs. English tr. 1|access-date=2023-05-04}} [[ja:倭吾子籠]] [[en:draft:Yamato no Agoko]] == History == [[File:Hibara-jinja,_torii_closeup.jpg|thumb|240x240px|[[Hibara Shrine]], at the foot of [[Mount Miwa]] in [[Sakurai, Nara]], identified as the place where the Yata-no-Kagami and the Kusanagi-no-Tsurugi were first enshrined after their removal from the imperial palace.]] During [[Jimmu's Eastern Expedition]] {{ill|Saonetsuhiko|ja|椎根津彦|fr}} was given the position of governor of [[Yamato Province]] by [[Emperor Jimmu]].{{Cite web|title=Friday: Kojiki (「乞食」ではなく『古事記』ですヨ！！) #26|url=https://japaneseexperts.net/972/|access-date=2023-05-04|website=Japanese Experts Net|language=en-US}} And Saonetsuhiko became their ancestor.{{Cite web|date=2023-10-26|title=Saonetsuhiko {{!}} 國學院大學デジタルミュージアム|url=https://d-museum.kokugakuin.ac.jp/eos/detail/id=9159|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20231026183115/https://d-museum.kokugakuin.ac.jp/eos/detail/id=9159|archive-date=2023-10-26|access-date=2023-12-04}} There is a complex myth about the reign of [[Emperor Sujin]] and its link to the worship of [[Yamato Okunitama]] and [[Amaterasu]]. There was a crisis during his reign and eventually the worship of [[Amaterasu]] and [[Yamato Okunitama]] were moved out of the imperial palace to separate shrines. Worship of Amaterasu moved to [[Hibara Shrine]] and then many other shrines called {{ill|Moto-Ise Shrines|lt=|ja|元伊勢}} until eventually reaching [[Ise Jingu]]. By contrast the worship of [[Yamato Okunitama]] moved to [[Oyamato Shrine]], near [[Hibara Shrine]] and [[Omiwa Shrine]]. Yamato Okunitama was first entrusted to a daughter of [[Emperor Sujin]] named {{Ill|Nunaki-iri-hime|ja|渟名城入姫命|fr}}, but shortly afterwards, her health began to fail. It is recorded that she became emaciated and lost all of her hair, which rendered her unable to perform her duties.{{cite book|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=_oEfAAAAYAAJ|title=Nihongi: Chronicles of Japan from the Earliest Times to A.D. 697, Volume 2|author=Aston, William George.|date=1896|publisher=The Japan Society London|isbn=9780524053478|pages=150–164|author-link=William George Aston}} These efforts still did not alleviate the ongoing plague, so Sujin decreed that a [[divination]] be performed sometime during the 7th year of his reign, that would involve him making a trip to the plain of Kami-asaji, and invoking the [[Yaoyorozu no Kami|eighty myriad deities]]. After the divination, {{ill|Ichishi no Nagaochi|ja|市磯長尾市|fr}}, a descendant of {{ill|Saonetsuhiko|ja|椎根津彦|fr}} would conduct the rites pertaining to Okunitama, replacing the emaciated Nunaki-iri-hime. {{ill|Ichishi no Nagaochi|ja|市磯長尾市|fr}} would be the ancestor of the Yamato no Kuni no Miyatsuko.{{Cite web|title=Page:Nihongi by Aston.djvu/208|url=https://en.wikisource.org/wiki/Page:Nihongi_by_Aston.djvu/208|access-date=2023-10-24|website=en.wikisource.org|language=en}} {{ill|Yamato no Agoko|lt=Agoko no Sukune|ja|倭吾子籠}} was a notable member of the clan and governor of Yamato Province{{Cite web|date=April 2022|title=Episode 61: Bad Behavior and the People that Excuse It|url=https://sengokudaimyo.com/podcast/episode-61|access-date=2023-05-04|website=Sengoku Daimyo|language=en-US}} == record == By the way, in the twelfth volume of the "Nihon Shoki," [[Emperor Richū|Emperor Richu]] floats a two-pronged boat on Iware City Isoike Pond. 『日本書紀』履中天皇3年11月6日条 === The Yamato military fields and warehouses === Similarly, Volume 11 of the "Shoki" tells the following story: This is the story of how Akokoro remade a giant tree that had washed up on the Oi River into a boat. At this time, Akokoro was called "Yamato Nao." The Crown Prince, who was filled with suspicion, became suspicious of Agogo's true intentions and tried to kill him. So Akokoro felt humbled and offered his younger sister, Hinohime, as a tribute, and was spared the death penalty. From this time on, Yamato Nao began to offer court ladies as tribute. 『日本書紀』履中天皇即位前紀条 According to Volume 12 of the "Shoki," Prince Sumiyoshi Nakatsu and Yamato Naokogo were on close terms. Therefore, when Prince Naka rebelled against the Crown Prince, Prince Izahowake (later Emperor Richu), presumably in the year 399, he tried to side with Prince Naka and gathered several hundred elite soldiers at a place called "Kakihami no Kurusu" (said to be Kurusu-go, {{ill|10=ja|11=忍海郡|Oshikai County}} ) and waited for the Crown Prince. However, when he realized that the Crown Prince's troops were more numerous than he had expected, he changed his attitude. === Driftwood of the Oi River === Another part of the Richū Sokui Chronicle states that the Crown Prince, on his way to [[Isonokami Shrine]], encounters a young girl at the foot of Mt. Asuka and asks her about the safety of the journey.{{Quote frame|六十二年の夏五月（推定[[374年]]）に、[[遠淡海国造|遠江国司]]（とほつあふみのくに の みこともち）表上言（まう）さく、「大（おほ）きなる樹（き）有りて、[[大井川|大井河]]（おほゐがは）より流れて、河（かは）曲（くま）り停（とどま）れり。其大きさ十囲（とうだき＝30尺、およそ300メートル）。本（もと）は壱（ひとつ）にして末は両（またまた）なり」とまうす。時に倭直吾子籠（やまとのあたひあごこ）を遣（つかは）して船に造らしむ。而（しかう）して南海（みなみのみち）より運（めぐら）して、難波津（なにはのつ）に将（ゐ）て来（きた）りて、御船（みふね）に充（あ）てつ。『日本書紀』仁徳天皇62年5月条}}There are also situations where you are advised to do so. This shows that the Yamato Naochou clan was familiar with the geography of the surrounding area, to the extent that they were able to set up ambushes. "The mountains are filled with many soldiers. Please go around and cross the Tagima Pass." === Prince Sumiyoshi's Rebellion === The fourteenth volume of the "Shoki" tells the story of Emperor Yuryaku, who, in a fit of rage after a hunt at Mimase, killed Otsu no Umakai with the sword, and his mother, Empress {{ill|Oshisaka no Ōnakatsuhime|en}}, presenting the Wa court lady "Hinohime" to settle the matter. This conversation led to the establishment of {{ill|10=ja|11=宍人部|the Shishihitobe}} (the branch of the Shishihito clan), and the appointment of three members, including Kashiwadeno no Omi Nagano. In addition, the “Oyamato no Kuni no Miyatsuko Agogo no Sukune” presented Sahonoko Toriwake to the Shishihitobe, and “the Ministers of the Imperial Court, Tomo no Miyatsuko and Kuni no Miyatsuko, followed suit and continued to offer tribute.” 『日本書紀』雄略天皇2年10月6日条{{Quote frame|「伝（つて）に聞く、皇太子（ひつぎのみこ）、非常之事（おもほえぬこと）有（ま）しますと。助けまつらむとして兵（つはもの）を備（そな）へて待ちたてまつる」}}As a character in the " [[Nihon Shoki]] ," he appears in relatively many places. Volume 11 of the Nihon Shoki records a dispute over the Yamato military fields and warehouses between {{ill|10=ja|11=額田大中彦皇子|Prince Nukata no}} {{ill|10=ja|11=屯田|Onakahiko}} and the Military Field Commander, {{ill|10=ja|11=淤宇宿禰|Ounosukune}}, which took place after the death of the Emperor in what is [[Emperor Ōjin|believed]] to be 310 (the 41st year of the reign of Emperor Ojin) and {{ill|10=ja|11=屯倉|the Imperial Throne}} was in a state of uncertainty. When Prince Nukata no Oonakahiko unilaterally confiscated his land, Ousukune appealed to Uji no Wakairoko and then to Osazaki no Mikoto (later [[Emperor Nintoku]] ), and it was discovered that Agoko, who was currently stationed in Karakuni, knew about the Wa military fields and military storehouses. Following the advice of Ootori-no-Mikoto, Ousukune traveled day and night to Korea with Awaji fishermen and returned with the child's basket. Akogo testified that the "Tonden and Tonkura of Wa" were passed down to Emperor Keikō, who was [[Emperor Keikō|the crown prince]] during the reign of [[Emperor Suinin]], saying, "Generally, the Tonden of Wa are the Tonden of the current emperor. Even if one is the son of the emperor, he cannot be in charge unless he is the emperor's son," and that they were under the control of the emperor of the time. This caused Prince Nukata-Onakahiko to reflect on his actions, and the land management issue was resolved in Ousukune's favor. The [[Kojiki]] makes no mention of such circumstances. === Presentation from the Shishitobe === It is said that the Hihime who appears here and Sumiyoshi's younger sister, Hinohime, are the same person, and that there may be some confusion in the legends. The above description needs to be considered in conjunction with historical facts uncovered by archaeology, which show that the chiefs who became the ancestors of the Izumo no Omi clan in the first half of the 5th century were deeply involved with the Yamato government and engaged in negotiations with the Korean Peninsula. Furthermore, it is necessary to look at the connections with {{ill|10=ja|11=淡路島|the Awaji Island}} fishermen group and the relationship with the {{ill|Nomi no Sukune|en}} legend. == Research == A group of fishermen from Awaji Island appears frequently in the aforementioned story; sailors from this group were active when Ousukune went to retrieve the Akoko basket from Korea; and in the legend of Prince Sumiyoshi Nakatsu, "fishermen from Nojima on Awaji" are secretly active, led by {{ill|10=ja|11=阿曇浜子|Azumi no Muraji Hamako}}. Many artifacts indicating connections to the peninsula and Izumo have been excavated from the Kidohara and Uryu ruins on Awaji Island. Jasper rough stones from {{ill|10=ja|11=玉湯町|Kasenyama}} in Tamayu-cho, [[Matsue|Matsue City]] have been excavated from jade-making sites in the Kinai region, such as the Soga Site, Furu {{ill|10=ja|11=布留遺跡|Site}}, and Nagahara Site. In particular, jade-making sites using Izumo-style stone materials such as jasper and quartz have been found at the Tani Site near Ise, the base of the Yamato {{ill|10=ja|11=磯城|Nao}} clan. Outside the Nara Basin, small amounts of remains have been excavated from the Nagahara ruins in Kawachi Province. In addition to Yayoi period ruins, the remains of a jade-making workshop thought to date from the end of the 4th century to the beginning of the 5th century have been discovered along the coasts of Lake Shinji and Lake Nakaumi, and whetstones made from crystalline schist mined in {{ill|10=ja|11=紀の川|the Yoshino River}} and {{ill|10=ja|11=紀の川|Kino River}} basins in Nara Prefecture were used. {{ill|Ichishi no Nagaochi|fr}}, an ancestor of Yamato Nao, appears in the legends of {{ill|Amenohiboko|en}} and is also said to have gone to Izumo to welcome Nomi no Sukune. Nomi no Sukune was famous for his {{ill|10=ja|11=当麻蹴速|sumo}} match with Tagima no Kehaya, and according to Kikuchi Teruo, this story is the origin of the rice farming ritual in which the spirits of the earth are calmed by sumo. In this story, the land of Tagima that Nomi no Sukune acquired was located at the point where the Nara Basin emerges from [[Osaka Bay|Osaka]] Bay via Takenouchi {{ill|10=ja|11=竹内峠|Pass}}, where Sugawara Shrine is located, and it was a strategic transportation hub that also leads to {{ill|10=ja|11=葛城|Katsuragi}} to the south. The nearby Ota ruins are the remains of a settlement from the early Kofun period, and pottery from {{ill|10=ja|11=山陰地方|the San'in}} region estimated to date to the first half of the 4th century has also been excavated. This suggests that there was evidence of a connection with the San'in region around the "Tagima Path" from the time of Nomi no Sukune. As described above, the relationship between Yamato Nao, the Izumo forces, and the fishermen of Awaji Island in the Agokoro legend conveys some historical fact, and it is highly likely that these were condensed and linked together in one person called Waagokoro. == Family tree == Many clans may be descendants of Furutama no Mikoto. This includes the {{ill|Owari clan|ja|尾張氏|en}} and [[Yamato no Kuni no Miyatsuko]]. This is a subject of debate.{{Cite web|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160422190938/http://wwr2.ucom.ne.jp/hetoyc15/keihu/amabe/amabe-k2.htm|access-date=2023-12-13|website=web.archive.org}} {{User:Immanuelle/Generations of Watatsumi}} == See also == * {{ill|Yamato Okunitama Shrine|ja|大和大国魂神社|simple}} * [[Kuni no miyatsuko]] * {{ill|Princess Yamato Totohi Momoso|en||fr|Yamatototohimomoso-hime}} * {{ill|10=ja|11=飛鳥時代以前の人物一覧|List of people before the Asuka period}} * {{ill|10=ja|11=倭の六県|The Six Prefectures of Wa}} * {{ill|10=ja|11=葛城|Katsuragi}} * {{ill|10=ja|11=大山守皇子|Prince Oyamamori}} * {{ill|10=ja|11=菟道稚郎子|Ujichi Wakako}} * {{ill|10=ja|11=住吉仲皇子|Prince Sumiyoshi}} * {{ill|10=ja|11=阿曇浜子|Azumi Hamako}} * {{ill|Ichishi no Nagaochi|fr}} == footnote == {{脚注ヘルプ}} == References == * Complete translation of the Kojiki: Japanese Classics 1, Shogakukan, 1983 * "Nihon Shoki" (vol. 2 and 3), Iwanami Bunko, 1994 * "Nihon Shoki" Complete Modern Japanese Translation (Vol. 1 and 2), Kodansha Academic Library, Translated by Ujitani Takeshi, 1988 == Notes == {{notelist}} === References === {{reflist}} === Bibliography === {{Refbegin}} ====''Nihon Shoki''==== ''See the references under {{Lang|ja-latn|[[Nihon Shoki]]}} for an extended bibliography'' *{{cite book|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=1IJrNAKBpycC&pg=PA299|title=Nihongi: Chronicles of Japan from the Earliest Times to A.D. 697|last=Aston|first=William George|publisher=Kegan Paul, Trench, Trubner (for the Japan Society of London)|year=1896|isbn=9780524053478|volume=1|place=London|oclc=448337491|author-link=William George Aston}}, [https://books.google.com/books?id=_oEfAAAAYAAJ alt-link] English translation * {{cite web|author=JHTI|year=2002|title=Nihon Shoki|url=https://jhti.berkeley.edu/Nihon%20shoki.html|access-date=2019-08-23|work=[[Japanese Historical Text Initiative]] (JHTI)|publisher=UC Berkeley}}, searchtext resource to retrieve kanbun text vs. English tr.
