{{draft}} {{Promising draft|reason=the high amount of work put into it over a long time, see edit history}} {{infobox deity|氏名=倭吾子籠|image=|imageサイズ=|image説明=|時代=[[古墳時代]]|生誕=不明|死没=不明|改名=|alternative names=|諡号=|神号=|戒名=|墓所=|官位=|主君=[[仁徳天皇]]、[[履中天皇]]、[[Emperor Yūryaku]]|氏族=[[倭氏|倭直]]（[[倭国造]]）|父母=|兄弟=|妻=|子=|特記事項=|image=Ohyamato-jinja Haiden.jpg|image caption=Oyamato Shrine, the main shrine of the {{ill|clan Yamato|en|Yamato no Kuni no Miyatsuko|12=draft}}|caption=[[Ōyamato Shrine]], the main shrine of the [[Yamato no Kuni no Miyatsuko]]|province of origin=[[Yamato Province]]|home province=[[Yamato Province]]|founder={{ill|Saonetsuhiko|ja|椎根津彦|12=draft}},
{{ill|Ichishi no Nagaochi|ja|市磯長尾市|12=draft}}|father='''{{ill|Naruko no Sukune|ja|鳴子宿祢|12=draft}}'''|siblings={{ill|Maro no Sukune|ja|麻呂宿祢|12=draft}}, {{ill|Hinohime|ja|日之媛|complete=true|12=draft}}}} {{complex}} '''Yamato''' no Agoko (years of birth and death unknown) was a {{ill|Gōzoku|lt=powerful|en|12=draft}} clan leader of ancient Japan mentioned in the " [[Nihon Shoki]] " and other sources. Ancestor of [[Yamato no Kuni no Miyatsuko|the Yamato]] no Kuni no Miyatsuko. There is no mention of him in the [[Kojiki]] . He served under [[Emperor Nintoku]] , [[Emperor Richū|Emperor Richu]] , and [[Emperor Yūryaku|Emperor Yuryaku]] == Origin == {{Short description|Japanese noble family}} Yamato no Agoko came from the [[Yamato no Kuni no Miyatsuko|Yamato no Atai clan]]. Their [[Ujigami]] or clan god is [[Yamato Okunitama]] of [[Ōyamato Shrine]]{{Cite web|title=International Symposium "Perspectives on Japanese history and literature from ancient historical records"|url=https://www.waseda.jp/inst/sgu/news-en/2019/04/12/5171|access-date=2023-05-04|website=Top Global University Project: Waseda Goes Global|language=en}} Some scholars interpret the ''kami'' as being a variant or epithet of [[Ōmononushi]] who has much more widespread worship.{{Cite journal|last=Ellwood|first=Robert S.|date=1990|title=The Sujin Religious Revolution|journal=Japanese Journal of Religious Studies|volume=17|issue=2/3|pages=199–217|doi=10.18874/jjrs.17.2-3.1990.199-217|issn=0304-1042|jstor=30234018|doi-access=free}}{{Cite book|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=_Q81DQAAQBAJ|title=Shinto: A History|last=Hardacre|first=Helen|date=2017|publisher=Oxford University Press|isbn=978-0-19-062171-1|language=en}}{{rp|22}} There is a complex myth about the origins of modern worship of [[Yamato Okunitama]] during the reign of [[Emperor Sujin]].{{Cite web|last=D|first=John|date=2012-11-10|title=Teeuwen on Shinto|url=https://www.greenshinto.com/2012/11/10/teeuwen-on-shinto/|access-date=2023-05-04|website=Green Shinto|language=en-GB}}https://www.japanpolicyforum.jp/pdf/2016/no35/DJweb_35_cul_02.pdfhttps://freidok.uni-freiburg.de/fedora/objects/freidok:4635/datastreams/FILE1/content{{Citation|title=Book V|url=https://en.wikisource.org/wiki/Nihongi:_Chronicles_of_Japan_from_the_Earliest_Times_to_A.D._697/Book_V|work=Nihongi: Chronicles of Japan from the Earliest Times to A.D. 697, Volume 1|access-date=2023-05-04}} [[File:Hibara-jinja,_torii_closeup.jpg|thumb|240x240px|Hibara Shrine, at the foot of [[Mount Miwa]] in [[Sakurai, Nara]], identified as the place where the Yata-no-Kagami and the Kusanagi-no-Tsurugi were first enshrined after their removal from the imperial palace.]] During {{ill|Jimmu%27s Eastern Expedition|en}} {{ill|Saonetsuhiko|ja|椎根津彦|fr|12=draft}} was given the position of governor of [[Yamato Province]] by [[Emperor Jimmu]].{{Cite web|title=Friday: Kojiki (「乞食」ではなく『古事記』ですヨ！！) #26|url=https://japaneseexperts.net/972/|access-date=2023-05-04|website=Japanese Experts Net|language=en-US}} And Saonetsuhiko became their ancestor.{{Cite web|date=2023-10-26|title=Saonetsuhiko {{!}} 國學院大學デジタルミュージアム|url=https://d-museum.kokugakuin.ac.jp/eos/detail/id=9159|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20231026183115/https://d-museum.kokugakuin.ac.jp/eos/detail/id=9159|archive-date=2023-10-26|access-date=2023-12-04}} After the divination, {{ill|Ichishi no Nagaochi|ja|市磯長尾市|fr|12=draft}}, a descendant of {{ill|Saonetsuhiko|ja|椎根津彦|fr|12=draft}} would conduct the rites pertaining to Okunitama, replacing the emaciated Nunaki-iri-hime. {{ill|Ichishi no Nagaochi|ja|市磯長尾市|fr|12=draft}} would be the ancestor of the Yamato no Kuni no Miyatsuko.{{Cite web|title=Page:Nihongi by Aston.djvu/208|url=https://en.wikisource.org/wiki/Page:Nihongi_by_Aston.djvu/208|access-date=2023-10-24|website=en.wikisource.org|language=en}} == Historical record == By the way, in the twelfth volume of the "Nihon Shoki," [[Emperor Richū|Emperor Richu]] floats a two-pronged boat on Iware City Isoike Pond. 『日本書紀』履中天皇3rd year 11月6日条 === The Yamato military fields and warehouses === Similarly, Volume 11 of the "Shoki" tells the following story: This is the story of how Agoko remade a giant tree that had washed up on the Oi River into a boat. At this time, Agoko was called "Yamato no Agoko." The Crown Prince, who was filled with suspicion, became suspicious of Agogo's true intentions and tried to kill him. So Agoko felt humbled and offered his younger sister, Hinohime, as a tribute, and was spared the death penalty. From this time on, Yamato no Agoko began to offer court ladies as tribute. 『日本書紀』履中天皇即位前紀条 According to Volume 12 of the "Shoki," Prince Sumiyoshi Nakatsu and Yamato Naokogo were on close terms. Therefore, when Prince Naka rebelled against the Crown Prince, Prince Izahowake (later Emperor Richu), presumably in the year 399, he tried to side with Prince Naka and gathered several hundred elite soldiers at a place called "Kakihami no Kurusu" (said to be Kurusu-go, {{ill|10=ja|11=忍海郡|Oshikai county|12=draft}} ) and waited for the Crown Prince. However, when he realized that the Crown Prince's troops were more numerous than he had expected, he changed his attitude. === Driftwood of the Oi River === Another part of the Richū Sokui Chronicle states that the Crown Prince, on his way to {{Interlanguage link|12=draft|Isonokami Shrine|en|Isonokami Shrine}}, encounters a young girl at the foot of Mt. Asuka and asks her about the safety of the journey.{{Quote frame|In the summer of May of the 62nd year (estimated to be 374 AD), the governor of Tōtōmi Province reported, "There is a large tree that flowed from the {{ill|Ōi River|en}}, bending and stopping at the river's curve. Its size is around ten tōdaki (approximately 300 meters). Initially singular, it splits into two at the ends." At that time, Yamato no Ataī Agoko was dispatched to construct a ship from it. Thus, navigating from the Southern Sea, it arrived at Naniwa Port, where it was dedicated as a royal ship.『日本書紀』仁徳天皇62nd year 5月条|12=draft}}This episode is about a massive log that had drifted to the Ōigawa River, which Agoko then remade into a ship. At this time, Agoko was referred to as "Yamato no Atai." Incidentally, in Volume 12 of the "Nihon Shoki," it is mentioned that Emperor Nintoku floated a bifurcated boat (a boat split into two parts) in the Iware Market Isopond. === Prince Sumiyoshi's Rebellion === The fourteenth volume of the "Shoki" tells the story of Emperor Yuryaku, who, in a fit of rage after a hunt at Mimase, killed Otsu no Umakai with the sword, and his mother, Empress {{ill|Oshisaka no Ōnakatsuhime|en}}, presenting the Wa court lady "Hinohime" to settle the matter. This conversation led to the establishment of the {{ill|10=ja|11=宍人部|Shishihitobe|12=draft}} (the branch of the Shishihito clan), and the appointment of three members, including Kashiwadeno no Omi Nagano. In addition, the “Oyamato no Kuni no Miyatsuko Agoko no Sukune” presented Sahonoko Toriwake to the Shishihitobe, and “the Ministers of the Imperial Court, Tomo no Miyatsuko and Kuni no Miyatsuko, followed suit and continued to offer tribute.” 『日本書紀』雄略天皇2nd year 10月6日条{{Quote frame|"I hear through the grapevine that an extraordinary event has occurred to the Crown Prince. Preparing soldiers, we stand ready to offer assistance."}}As a character in the " [[Nihon Shoki]] ," he appears in relatively many places. Volume 11 of the Nihon Shoki records a dispute over the Yamato military fields and warehouses between {{ill|10=ja|11=額田大中彦皇子|Prince Nukata no Onakahiko|12=draft}} and the {{ill|Tuntian|lt=military farm|en|10=ja|11=屯田|12=draft}} administrator, {{ill|10=ja|11=淤宇宿禰|Ounosukune|12=draft}}, which took place after the death of the Emperor in what is [[Emperor Ōjin|believed]] to be 310 (the 41st year of the reign of Emperor Ojin) and {{ill|10=ja|11=屯倉|the Imperial Throne|12=draft}} was in a state of uncertainty. When Prince Nukata no Oonakahiko unilaterally confiscated his land, Ousukune appealed to Uji no Wakairoko and then to Osazaki no Mikoto (later [[Emperor Nintoku]] ), and it was discovered that Agoko, who was currently stationed in Karakuni, knew about the Wa military fields and military storehouses. Following the advice of Ootori-no-Mikoto, Ousukune traveled day and night to Korea with Awaji fishermen and returned with the child's basket. Akogo testified that the "{{ill|Tuntian|lt=military farms|en|10=ja|11=屯田|12=draft}} (屯田) and {{ill|military granary|lt=granaries|ja|屯倉|12=draft}} (屯倉) of Wa" were passed down to Emperor Keikō, who was [[Emperor Keikō|the crown prince]] during the reign of [[Emperor Suinin]], saying, "Generally, the {{ill|Tuntian|lt=military farms|en|10=ja|11=屯田|12=draft}} (屯田) of Yamato are the military farms (屯田) of the current emperor. Even if one is the son of the emperor, he cannot be in charge unless he is the emperor's son," and that they were under the control of the emperor of the time. This caused Prince Nukata-Onakahiko to reflect on his actions, and the land management issue was resolved in Ousukune's favor. The [[Kojiki]] makes no mention of such circumstances. === Presentation from the Shishitobe === It is said that the Hihime who appears here and Sumiyoshi's younger sister, Hinohime, are the same person, and that there may be some confusion in the legends. The above description needs to be considered in conjunction with historical facts uncovered by archaeology, which show that the chiefs who became the ancestors of the Izumo no Omi clan in the first half of the 5th century were deeply involved with the Yamato government and engaged in negotiations with the Korean Peninsula. Furthermore, it is necessary to look at the connections with the {{ill|10=ja|11=淡路島|Awaji Island|12=draft}} fishermen group and the relationship with the {{ill|Nomi no Sukune|en}} legend. == Research == A group of fishermen from Awaji Island appears frequently in the aforementioned story; sailors from this group were active when Ousukune went to retrieve the Akoko basket from Korea; and in the legend of Prince Sumiyoshi Nakatsu, "fishermen from Nojima on Awaji" are secretly active, led by {{ill|10=ja|11=阿曇浜子|Azumi no Muraji Hamako|12=draft}}. Many artifacts indicating connections to the peninsula and Izumo have been excavated from the Kidohara and Uryu ruins on Awaji Island. Jasper rough stones from {{ill|10=ja|11=玉湯町|Kasenyama|12=draft}} in Tamayu-cho, [[Matsue|Matsue City]] have been excavated from jade-making sites in the Kinai region, such as the Soga Site, Furu {{ill|10=ja|11=布留遺跡|Site|12=draft}}, and Nagahara Site. In particular, jade-making sites using Izumo-style stone materials such as jasper and quartz have been found at the Tani Site near Ise, the base of the Yamato no Agoko clan. Outside the Nara Basin, small amounts of remains have been excavated from the Nagahara ruins in Kawachi Province. In addition to Yayoi period ruins, the remains of a jade-making workshop thought to date from the end of the 4th century to the beginning of the 5th century have been discovered along the coasts of Lake Shinji and Lake Nakaumi, and whetstones made from crystalline schist mined in the {{ill|10=ja|11=紀の川|Yoshino River|lt=Yoshino River|en|12=draft}} and {{ill|10=ja|11=紀の川|Kinokawa_River|lt=Kino River|en|12=draft}} basins in Nara Prefecture were used. {{ill|Ichishi no Nagaochi|fr}}, an ancestor of Yamato no Agoko, appears in the legends of {{ill|Amenohiboko|en|12=draft}} and is also said to have gone to Izumo to welcome Nomi no Sukune. Nomi no Sukune was famous for his {{ill|10=ja|11=当麻蹴速|sumo|12=draft}} match with Tagima no Kehaya, and according to Kikuchi Teruo, this story is the origin of the rice farming ritual in which the spirits of the earth are calmed by sumo. In this story, the land of Tagima that Nomi no Sukune acquired was located at the point where the Nara Basin emerges from [[Osaka Bay|Osaka]] Bay via {{ill|Takeuchi Pass|ja|竹内峠|12=draft}}, where Sugawara Shrine is located, and it was a strategic transportation hub that also leads to {{ill|10=ja|11=葛城|Katsuragi|4=en|12=draft}} to the south. The nearby Ota ruins are the remains of a settlement from the early Kofun period, and pottery from the {{ill|San'in region|en}} estimated to date to the first half of the 4th century has also been excavated. This suggests that there was evidence of a connection with the San'in region around the "Tagima Path" from the time of Nomi no Sukune. As described above, the relationship between the [[Yamato no Kuni no Miyatsuko|Yamato clan]] troops, the Izumo forces, and the fishermen of Awaji Island in the Agokoro legend conveys some historical fact, and it is highly likely that these were condensed and linked together in one person called Yamato no Agoko. == Family tree == Many clans may be descendants of Furutama no Mikoto. This includes the {{ill|Owari clan|ja|尾張氏|en|12=draft}} and [[Yamato no Kuni no Miyatsuko]]. This is a subject of debate.{{Cite web|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160422190938/http://wwr2.ucom.ne.jp/hetoyc15/keihu/amabe/amabe-k2.htm|access-date=2023-12-13|website=web.archive.org}} Tehiko|lt2=手彦|complete=true|en:draft|12=draft}}''' * '''{{ill|Yamato no Iotari|ja|大倭五百足|simple|User:Immanuelle/Yamato no Iotari|fr|User:Immanuelle/Yamato no Iotari|lt1=Yamato no Ancestor of [[Yamato no Kuni no Miyatsuko|the Yamato]] no Kuni no Miyatsuko. There is no mention of him in the [[Kojiki]] . He served under [[Emperor Nintoku]] , [[Emperor Richū|Emperor Richu]] , and [[Emperor Yūryaku|Emperor Yuryaku]] == Origin == {{Short description|Japanese noble family}} Yamato no Agoko came from the [[Yamato no Kuni no Miyatsuko|Yamato no Atai clan]]. Their [[Ujigami]] or clan god is [[Yamato Okunitama]] of [[Ōyamato Shrine]]{{Cite web|title=International Symposium "Perspectives on Japanese history and literature from ancient historical records"|url=https://www.waseda.jp/inst/sgu/news-en/2019/04/12/5171|access-date=2023-05-04|website=Top Global University Project: Waseda Goes Global|language=en}} Some scholars interpret the ''kami'' as being a variant or epithet of [[Ōmononushi]] who has much more widespread worship.{{Cite journal|last=Ellwood|first=Robert S.|date=1990|title=The Sujin Religious Revolution|journal=Japanese Journal of Religious Studies|volume=17|issue=2/3|pages=199–217|doi=10.18874/jjrs.17.2-3.1990.199-217|issn=0304-1042|jstor=30234018|doi-access=free}}{{Cite book|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=_Q81DQAAQBAJ|title=Shinto: A History|last=Hardacre|first=Helen|date=2017|publisher=Oxford University Press|isbn=978-0-19-062171-1|language=en}}{{rp|22}} There is a complex myth about the origins of modern worship of [[Yamato Okunitama]] during the reign of [[Emperor Sujin]].{{Cite web|last=D|first=John|date=2012-11-10|title=Teeuwen on Shinto|url=https://www.greenshinto.com/2012/11/10/teeuwen-on-shinto/|access-date=2023-05-04|website=Green Shinto|language=en-GB}}https://www.japanpolicyforum.jp/pdf/2016/no35/DJweb_35_cul_02.pdfhttps://freidok.uni-freiburg.de/fedora/objects/freidok:4635/datastreams/FILE1/content{{Citation|title=Book V|url=https://en.wikisource.org/wiki/Nihongi:_Chronicles_of_Japan_from_the_Earliest_Times_to_A.D._697/Book_V|work=Nihongi: Chronicles of Japan from the Earliest Times to A.D. 697, Volume 1|access-date=2023-05-04}} [[File:Hibara-jinja,_torii_closeup.jpg|thumb|240x240px|Hibara Shrine, at the foot of [[Mount Miwa]] in [[Sakurai, Nara]], identified as the place where the Yata-no-Kagami and the Kusanagi-no-Tsurugi were first enshrined after their removal from the imperial palace.]] During {{ill|Jimmu%27s Eastern Expedition|en}} {{ill|Saonetsuhiko|ja|椎根津彦|fr|12=draft}} was given the position of governor of [[Yamato Province]] by [[Emperor Jimmu]].{{Cite web|title=Friday: Kojiki (「乞食」ではなく『古事記』ですヨ！！) #26|url=https://japaneseexperts.net/972/|access-date=2023-05-04|website=Japanese Experts Net|language=en-US}} And Saonetsuhiko became their ancestor.{{Cite web|date=2023-10-26|title=Saonetsuhiko {{!}} 國學院大學デジタルミュージアム|url=https://d-museum.kokugakuin.ac.jp/eos/detail/id=9159|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20231026183115/https://d-museum.kokugakuin.ac.jp/eos/detail/id=9159|archive-date=2023-10-26|access-date=2023-12-04}} After the divination, {{ill|Ichishi no Nagaochi|ja|市磯長尾市|fr|12=draft}}, a descendant of {{ill|Saonetsuhiko|ja|椎根津彦|fr|12=draft}} would conduct the rites pertaining to Okunitama, replacing the emaciated Nunaki-iri-hime. {{ill|Ichishi no Nagaochi|ja|市磯長尾市|fr|12=draft}} would be the ancestor of the Yamato no Kuni no Miyatsuko.{{Cite web|title=Page:Nihongi by Aston.djvu/208|url=https://en.wikisource.org/wiki/Page:Nihongi_by_Aston.djvu/208|access-date=2023-10-24|website=en.wikisource.org|language=en}} == Historical record == By the way, in the twelfth volume of the "Nihon Shoki," [[Emperor Richū|Emperor Richu]] floats a two-pronged boat on Iware City Isoike Pond. 『日本書紀』履中天皇3rd year 11月6日条 === The Yamato military fields and warehouses === Similarly, Volume 11 of the "Shoki" tells the following story: This is the story of how Agoko remade a giant tree that had washed up on the Oi River into a boat. At this time, Agoko was called "Yamato no Agoko." The Crown Prince, who was filled with suspicion, became suspicious of Agogo's true intentions and tried to kill him. So Agoko felt humbled and offered his younger sister, Hinohime, as a tribute, and was spared the death penalty. From this time on, Yamato no Agoko began to offer court ladies as tribute. 『日本書紀』履中天皇即位前紀条 According to Volume 12 of the "Shoki," Prince Sumiyoshi Nakatsu and Yamato Naokogo were on close terms. Therefore, when Prince Naka rebelled against the Crown Prince, Prince Izahowake (later Emperor Richu), presumably in the year 399, he tried to side with Prince Naka and gathered several hundred elite soldiers at a place called "Kakihami no Kurusu" (said to be Kurusu-go, {{ill|10=ja|11=忍海郡|Oshikai county|12=draft}} ) and waited for the Crown Prince. However, when he realized that the Crown Prince's troops were more numerous than he had expected, he changed his attitude. === Driftwood of the Oi River === Another part of the Richū Sokui Chronicle states that the Crown Prince, on his way to {{Interlanguage link|12=draft|Isonokami Shrine|en|Isonokami Shrine}}, encounters a young girl at the foot of Mt. Asuka and asks her about the safety of the journey.{{Quote frame|In the summer of May of the 62nd year (estimated to be 374 AD), the governor of Tōtōmi Province reported, "There is a large tree that flowed from the {{ill|Ōi River|en}}, bending and stopping at the river's curve. Its size is around ten tōdaki (approximately 300 meters). Initially singular, it splits into two at the ends." At that time, Yamato no Ataī Agoko was dispatched to construct a ship from it. Thus, navigating from the Southern Sea, it arrived at Naniwa Port, where it was dedicated as a royal ship.『日本書紀』仁徳天皇62nd year 5月条|12=draft}}This episode is about a massive log that had drifted to the Ōigawa River, which Agoko then remade into a ship. At this time, Agoko was referred to as "Yamato no Atai." Incidentally, in Volume 12 of the "Nihon Shoki," it is mentioned that Emperor Nintoku floated a bifurcated boat (a boat split into two parts) in the Iware Market Isopond. === Prince Sumiyoshi's Rebellion === The fourteenth volume of the "Shoki" tells the story of Emperor Yuryaku, who, in a fit of rage after a hunt at Mimase, killed Otsu no Umakai with the sword, and his mother, Empress {{ill|Oshisaka no Ōnakatsuhime|en}}, presenting the Wa court lady "Hinohime" to settle the matter. This conversation led to the establishment of the {{ill|10=ja|11=宍人部|Shishihitobe|12=draft}} (the branch of the Shishihito clan), and the appointment of three members, including Kashiwadeno no Omi Nagano. In addition, the “Oyamato no Kuni no Miyatsuko Agoko no Sukune” presented Sahonoko Toriwake to the Shishihitobe, and “the Ministers of the Imperial Court, Tomo no Miyatsuko and Kuni no Miyatsuko, followed suit and continued to offer tribute.” 『日本書紀』雄略天皇2nd year 10月6日条{{Quote frame|"I hear through the grapevine that an extraordinary event has occurred to the Crown Prince. Preparing soldiers, we stand ready to offer assistance."}}As a character in the " [[Nihon Shoki]] ," he appears in relatively many places. Volume 11 of the Nihon Shoki records a dispute over the Yamato military fields and warehouses between {{ill|10=ja|11=額田大中彦皇子|Prince Nukata no Onakahiko|12=draft}} and the {{ill|Tuntian|lt=military farm|en|10=ja|11=屯田|12=draft}} administrator, {{ill|10=ja|11=淤宇宿禰|Ounosukune|12=draft}}, which took place after the death of the Emperor in what is [[Emperor Ōjin|believed]] to be 310 (the 41st year of the reign of Emperor Ojin) and {{ill|10=ja|11=屯倉|the Imperial Throne|12=draft}} was in a state of uncertainty. When Prince Nukata no Oonakahiko unilaterally confiscated his land, Ousukune appealed to Uji no Wakairoko and then to Osazaki no Mikoto (later [[Emperor Nintoku]] ), and it was discovered that Agoko, who was currently stationed in Karakuni, knew about the Wa military fields and military storehouses. Following the advice of Ootori-no-Mikoto, Ousukune traveled day and night to Korea with Awaji fishermen and returned with the child's basket. Akogo testified that the "{{ill|Tuntian|lt=military farms|en|10=ja|11=屯田|12=draft}} (屯田) and {{ill|military granary|lt=granaries|ja|屯倉|12=draft}} (屯倉) of Wa" were passed down to Emperor Keikō, who was [[Emperor Keikō|the crown prince]] during the reign of [[Emperor Suinin]], saying, "Generally, the {{ill|Tuntian|lt=military farms|en|10=ja|11=屯田|12=draft}} (屯田) of Yamato are the military farms (屯田) of the current emperor. Even if one is the son of the emperor, he cannot be in charge unless he is the emperor's son," and that they were under the control of the emperor of the time. This caused Prince Nukata-Onakahiko to reflect on his actions, and the land management issue was resolved in Ousukune's favor. The [[Kojiki]] makes no mention of such circumstances. === Presentation from the Shishitobe === It is said that the Hihime who appears here and Sumiyoshi's younger sister, Hinohime, are the same person, and that there may be some confusion in the legends. The above description needs to be considered in conjunction with historical facts uncovered by archaeology, which show that the chiefs who became the ancestors of the Izumo no Omi clan in the first half of the 5th century were deeply involved with the Yamato government and engaged in negotiations with the Korean Peninsula. Furthermore, it is necessary to look at the connections with the {{ill|10=ja|11=淡路島|Awaji Island|12=draft}} fishermen group and the relationship with the {{ill|Nomi no Sukune|en}} legend. == Research == A group of fishermen from Awaji Island appears frequently in the aforementioned story; sailors from this group were active when Ousukune went to retrieve the Akoko basket from Korea; and in the legend of Prince Sumiyoshi Nakatsu, "fishermen from Nojima on Awaji" are secretly active, led by {{ill|10=ja|11=阿曇浜子|Azumi no Muraji Hamako|12=draft}}. Many artifacts indicating connections to the peninsula and Izumo have been excavated from the Kidohara and Uryu ruins on Awaji Island. Jasper rough stones from {{ill|10=ja|11=玉湯町|Kasenyama|12=draft}} in Tamayu-cho, [[Matsue|Matsue City]] have been excavated from jade-making sites in the Kinai region, such as the Soga Site, Furu {{ill|10=ja|11=布留遺跡|Site|12=draft}}, and Nagahara Site. In particular, jade-making sites using Izumo-style stone materials such as jasper and quartz have been found at the Tani Site near Ise, the base of the Yamato no Agoko clan. Outside the Nara Basin, small amounts of remains have been excavated from the Nagahara ruins in Kawachi Province. In addition to Yayoi period ruins, the remains of a jade-making workshop thought to date from the end of the 4th century to the beginning of the 5th century have been discovered along the coasts of Lake Shinji and Lake Nakaumi, and whetstones made from crystalline schist mined in the {{ill|10=ja|11=紀の川|Yoshino River|lt=Yoshino River|en|12=draft}} and {{ill|10=ja|11=紀の川|Kinokawa_River|lt=Kino River|en|12=draft}} basins in Nara Prefecture were used. {{ill|Ichishi no Nagaochi|fr}}, an ancestor of Yamato no Agoko, appears in the legends of {{ill|Amenohiboko|en|12=draft}} and is also said to have gone to Izumo to welcome Nomi no Sukune. Nomi no Sukune was famous for his {{ill|10=ja|11=当麻蹴速|sumo|12=draft}} match with Tagima no Kehaya, and according to Kikuchi Teruo, this story is the origin of the rice farming ritual in which the spirits of the earth are calmed by sumo. In this story, the land of Tagima that Nomi no Sukune acquired was located at the point where the Nara Basin emerges from [[Osaka Bay|Osaka]] Bay via {{ill|Takeuchi Pass|ja|竹内峠|12=draft}}, where Sugawara Shrine is located, and it was a strategic transportation hub that also leads to {{ill|10=ja|11=葛城|Katsuragi|4=en|12=draft}} to the south. The nearby Ota ruins are the remains of a settlement from the early Kofun period, and pottery from the {{ill|San'in region|en}} estimated to date to the first half of the 4th century has also been excavated. This suggests that there was evidence of a connection with the San'in region around the "Tagima Path" from the time of Nomi no Sukune. As described above, the relationship between the [[Yamato no Kuni no Miyatsuko|Yamato clan]] troops, the Izumo forces, and the fishermen of Awaji Island in the Agokoro legend conveys some historical fact, and it is highly likely that these were condensed and linked together in one person called Yamato no Agoko. == Family tree == Many clans may be descendants of Furutama no Mikoto. This includes the {{ill|Owari clan|ja|尾張氏|en|12=draft}} and [[Yamato no Kuni no Miyatsuko]]. This is a subject of debate.{{Cite web|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160422190938/http://wwr2.ucom.ne.jp/hetoyc15/keihu/amabe/amabe-k2.htm|access-date=2023-12-13|website=web.archive.org}} Tehiko|lt2=手彦|complete=true|en:draft|12=draft}}''' * '''{{ill|Yamato no Iotari|ja|大倭五百足|simple|User:Immanuelle/Yamato no Iotari|fr|User:Immanuelle/Yamato no Iotari|lt1=Yamato no emaciated Nunaki-iri-hime. {{ill|Ichishi no Nagaochi|ja|市磯長尾市|fr|12=draft}} would be the ancestor of the Yamato no Kuni no Miyatsuko.{{Cite web|title=Page:Nihongi by Aston.djvu/208|url=https://en.wikisource.org/wiki/Page:Nihongi_by_Aston.djvu/208|access-date=2023-10-24|website=en.wikisource.org|language=en}} == Historical record == By the way, in the twelfth volume of the "Nihon Shoki," [[Emperor Richū|Emperor Richu]] floats a two-pronged boat on Iware City Isoike Pond. 『日本書紀』履中天皇3rd year 11月6日条 === The Yamato military fields and warehouses === Similarly, Volume 11 of the "Shoki" tells the following story: This is the story of how Agoko remade a giant tree that had washed up on the Oi River into a boat. At this time, Agoko was called "Yamato no Agoko." The Crown Prince, who was filled with suspicion, became suspicious of Agogo's true intentions and tried to kill him. So Agoko felt humbled and offered his younger sister, Hinohime, as a tribute, and was spared the death penalty. From this time on, Yamato no Agoko began to offer court ladies as tribute. 『日本書紀』履中天皇即位前紀条 According to Volume 12 of the "Shoki," Prince Sumiyoshi Nakatsu and Yamato Naokogo were on close terms. Therefore, when Prince Naka rebelled against the Crown Prince, Prince Izahowake (later Emperor Richu), presumably in the year 399, he tried to side with Prince Naka and gathered several hundred elite soldiers at a place called "Kakihami no Kurusu" (said to be Kurusu-go, {{ill|10=ja|11=忍海郡|Oshikai county|12=draft}} ) and waited for the Crown Prince. However, when he realized that the Crown Prince's troops were more numerous than he had expected, he changed his attitude. === Driftwood of the Oi River === Another part of the Richū Sokui Chronicle states that the Crown Prince, on his way to {{Interlanguage link|12=draft|Isonokami Shrine|en|Isonokami Shrine}}, encounters a young girl at the foot of Mt. Asuka and asks her about the safety of the journey.{{Quote frame|In the summer of May of the 62nd year (estimated to be 374 AD), the governor of Tōtōmi Province reported, "There is a large tree that flowed from the {{ill|Ōi River|en}}, bending and stopping at the river's curve. Its size is around ten tōdaki (approximately 300 meters). Initially singular, it splits into two at the ends." At that time, Yamato no Ataī Agoko was dispatched to construct a ship from it. Thus, navigating from the Southern Sea, it arrived at Naniwa Port, where it was dedicated as a royal ship.『日本書紀』仁徳天皇62nd year 5月条|12=draft}}This episode is about a massive log that had drifted to the Ōigawa River, which Agoko then remade into a ship. At this time, Agoko was referred to as "Yamato no Atai." Incidentally, in Volume 12 of the "Nihon Shoki," it is mentioned that Emperor Nintoku floated a bifurcated boat (a boat split into two parts) in the Iware Market Isopond. === Prince Sumiyoshi's Rebellion === The fourteenth volume of the "Shoki" tells the story of Emperor Yuryaku, who, in a fit of rage after a hunt at Mimase, killed Otsu no Umakai with the sword, and his mother, Empress {{ill|Oshisaka no Ōnakatsuhime|en}}, presenting the Wa court lady "Hinohime" to settle the matter. This conversation led to the establishment of the {{ill|10=ja|11=宍人部|Shishihitobe|12=draft}} (the branch of the Shishihito clan), and the appointment of three members, including Kashiwadeno no Omi Nagano. In addition, the “Oyamato no Kuni no Miyatsuko Agoko no Sukune” presented Sahonoko Toriwake to the Shishihitobe, and “the Ministers of the Imperial Court, Tomo no Miyatsuko and Kuni no Miyatsuko, followed suit and continued to offer tribute.” 『日本書紀』雄略天皇2nd year 10月6日条{{Quote frame|"I hear through the grapevine that an extraordinary event has occurred to the Crown Prince. Preparing soldiers, we stand ready to offer assistance."}}As a character in the " [[Nihon Shoki]] ," he appears in relatively many places. Volume 11 of the Nihon Shoki records a dispute over the Yamato military fields and warehouses between {{ill|10=ja|11=額田大中彦皇子|Prince Nukata no Onakahiko|12=draft}} and the {{ill|Tuntian|lt=military farm|en|10=ja|11=屯田|12=draft}} administrator, {{ill|10=ja|11=淤宇宿禰|Ounosukune|12=draft}}, which took place after the death of the Emperor in what is [[Emperor Ōjin|believed]] to be 310 (the 41st year of the reign of Emperor Ojin) and {{ill|10=ja|11=屯倉|the Imperial Throne|12=draft}} was in a state of uncertainty. When Prince Nukata no Oonakahiko unilaterally confiscated his land, Ousukune appealed to Uji no Wakairoko and then to Osazaki no Mikoto (later [[Emperor Nintoku]] ), and it was discovered that Agoko, who was currently stationed in Karakuni, knew about the Wa military fields and military storehouses. Following the advice of Ootori-no-Mikoto, Ousukune traveled day and night to Korea with Awaji fishermen and returned with the child's basket. Akogo testified that the "{{ill|Tuntian|lt=military farms|en|10=ja|11=屯田|12=draft}} (屯田) and {{ill|military granary|lt=granaries|ja|屯倉|12=draft}} (屯倉) of Wa" were passed down to Emperor Keikō, who was [[Emperor Keikō|the crown prince]] during the reign of [[Emperor Suinin]], saying, "Generally, the {{ill|Tuntian|lt=military farms|en|10=ja|11=屯田|12=draft}} (屯田) of Yamato are the military farms (屯田) of the current emperor. Even if one is the son of the emperor, he cannot be in charge unless he is the emperor's son," and that they were under the control of the emperor of the time. This caused Prince Nukata-Onakahiko to reflect on his actions, and the land management issue was resolved in Ousukune's favor. The [[Kojiki]] makes no mention of such circumstances. === Presentation from the Shishitobe === It is said that the Hihime who appears here and Sumiyoshi's younger sister, Hinohime, are the same person, and that there may be some confusion in the legends. The above description needs to be considered in conjunction with historical facts uncovered by archaeology, which show that the chiefs who became the ancestors of the Izumo no Omi clan in the first half of the 5th century were deeply involved with the Yamato government and engaged in negotiations with the Korean Peninsula. Furthermore, it is necessary to look at the connections with the {{ill|10=ja|11=淡路島|Awaji Island|12=draft}} fishermen group and the relationship with the {{ill|Nomi no Sukune|en}} legend. == Research == A group of fishermen from Awaji Island appears frequently in the aforementioned story; sailors from this group were active when Ousukune went to retrieve the Akoko basket from Korea; and in the legend of Prince Sumiyoshi Nakatsu, "fishermen from Nojima on Awaji" are secretly active, led by {{ill|10=ja|11=阿曇浜子|Azumi no Muraji Hamako|12=draft}}. Many artifacts indicating connections to the peninsula and Izumo have been excavated from the Kidohara and Uryu ruins on Awaji Island. Jasper rough stones from {{ill|10=ja|11=玉湯町|Kasenyama|12=draft}} in Tamayu-cho, [[Matsue|Matsue City]] have been excavated from jade-making sites in the Kinai region, such as the Soga Site, Furu {{ill|10=ja|11=布留遺跡|Site|12=draft}}, and Nagahara Site. In particular, jade-making sites using Izumo-style stone materials such as jasper and quartz have been found at the Tani Site near Ise, the base of the Yamato no Agoko clan. Outside the Nara Basin, small amounts of remains have been excavated from the Nagahara ruins in Kawachi Province. In addition to Yayoi period ruins, the remains of a jade-making workshop thought to date from the end of the 4th century to the beginning of the 5th century have been discovered along the coasts of Lake Shinji and Lake Nakaumi, and whetstones made from crystalline schist mined in the {{ill|10=ja|11=紀の川|Yoshino River|lt=Yoshino River|en|12=draft}} and {{ill|10=ja|11=紀の川|Kinokawa_River|lt=Kino River|en|12=draft}} basins in Nara Prefecture were used. {{ill|Ichishi no Nagaochi|fr}}, an ancestor of Yamato no Agoko, appears in the legends of {{ill|Amenohiboko|en|12=draft}} and is also said to have gone to Izumo to welcome Nomi no Sukune. Nomi no Sukune was famous for his {{ill|10=ja|11=当麻蹴速|sumo|12=draft}} match with Tagima no Kehaya, and according to Kikuchi Teruo, this story is the origin of the rice farming ritual in which the spirits of the earth are calmed by sumo. In this story, the land of Tagima that Nomi no Sukune acquired was located at the point where the Nara Basin emerges from [[Osaka Bay|Osaka]] Bay via {{ill|Takeuchi Pass|ja|竹内峠|12=draft}}, where Sugawara Shrine is located, and it was a strategic transportation hub that also leads to {{ill|10=ja|11=葛城|Katsuragi|4=en|12=draft}} to the south. The nearby Ota ruins are the remains of a settlement from the early Kofun period, and pottery from the {{ill|San'in region|en}} estimated to date to the first half of the 4th century has also been excavated. This suggests that there was evidence of a connection with the San'in region around the "Tagima Path" from the time of Nomi no Sukune. As described above, the relationship between the [[Yamato no Kuni no Miyatsuko|Yamato clan]] troops, the Izumo forces, and the fishermen of Awaji Island in the Agokoro legend conveys some historical fact, and it is highly likely that these were condensed and linked together in one person called Yamato no Agoko. == Family tree == Many clans may be descendants of Furutama no Mikoto. This includes the {{ill|Owari clan|ja|尾張氏|en|12=draft}} and [[Yamato no Kuni no Miyatsuko]]. This is a subject of debate.{{Cite web|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160422190938/http://wwr2.ucom.ne.jp/hetoyc15/keihu/amabe/amabe-k2.htm|access-date=2023-12-13|website=web.archive.org}} In addition, the “Oyamato no Kuni no Miyatsuko Agoko no Sukune” presented Sahonoko Toriwake to the Shishihitobe, and “the Ministers of the Imperial Court, Tomo no Miyatsuko and Kuni no Miyatsuko, followed suit and continued to offer tribute.” 『日本書紀』雄略天皇2nd year 10月6日条{{Quote frame|"I hear through the grapevine that an extraordinary event has occurred to the Crown Prince. Preparing soldiers, we stand ready to offer assistance."}}As a character in the " [[Nihon Shoki]] ," he appears in relatively many places. Volume 11 of the Nihon Shoki records a dispute over the Yamato military fields and warehouses between {{ill|10=ja|11=額田大中彦皇子|Prince Nukata no Onakahiko|qq=draft|qq=draft}} and the {{ill|Tuntian|lt=military farm|en|10=ja|11=屯田|qq=draft|qq=draft}} administrator, {{ill|10=ja|11=淤宇宿禰|Ounosukune|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, which took place after the death of the Emperor in what is [[Emperor Ōjin|believed]] to be 310 (the 41st year of the reign of Emperor Ojin) and {{ill|10=ja|11=屯倉|the Imperial Throne|qq=draft|qq=draft}} was in a state of uncertainty. When Prince Nukata no Oonakahiko unilaterally confiscated his land, Ousukune appealed to Uji no Wakairoko and then to Osazaki no Mikoto (later [[Emperor Nintoku]] ), and it was discovered that Agoko, who was currently stationed in Karakuni, knew about the Wa military fields and military storehouses. Following the advice of Ootori-no-Mikoto, Ousukune traveled day and night to Korea with Awaji fishermen and returned with the child's basket. Akogo testified that the "{{ill|Tuntian|lt=military farms|en|10=ja|11=屯田|qq=draft|qq=draft}} (屯田) and {{ill|military granary|lt=granaries|ja|屯倉|qq=draft|qq=draft}} (屯倉) of Wa" were passed down to Emperor Keikō, who was [[Emperor Keikō|the crown prince]] during the reign of [[Emperor Suinin]], saying, "Generally, the {{ill|Tuntian|lt=military farms|en|10=ja|11=屯田|qq=draft|qq=draft}} (屯田) of Yamato are the military farms (屯田) of the current emperor. Even if one is the son of the emperor, he cannot be in charge unless he is the emperor's son," and that they were under the control of the emperor of the time. This caused Prince Nukata-Onakahiko to reflect on his actions, and the land management issue was resolved in Ousukune's favor. The [[Kojiki]] makes no mention of such circumstances. === Presentation from the Shishitobe === It is said that the Hihime who appears here and Sumiyoshi's younger sister, Hinohime, are the same person, and that there may be some confusion in the legends. The above description needs to be considered in conjunction with historical facts uncovered by archaeology, which show that the chiefs who became the ancestors of the Izumo no Omi clan in the first half of the 5th century were deeply involved with the Yamato government and engaged in negotiations with the Korean Peninsula. Furthermore, it is necessary to look at the connections with the {{ill|10=ja|11=淡路島|Awaji Island|qq=draft|qq=draft}} fishermen group and the relationship with the {{ill|Nomi no Sukune|en}} legend. == Research == A group of fishermen from Awaji Island appears frequently in the aforementioned story; sailors from this group were active when Ousukune went to retrieve the Akoko basket from Korea; and in the legend of Prince Sumiyoshi Nakatsu, "fishermen from Nojima on Awaji" are secretly active, led by {{ill|10=ja|11=阿曇浜子|Azumi no Muraji Hamako|qq=draft|qq=draft}}. Many artifacts indicating connections to the peninsula and Izumo have been excavated from the Kidohara and Uryu ruins on Awaji Island. Jasper rough stones from {{ill|10=ja|11=玉湯町|Kasenyama|qq=draft|qq=draft}} in Tamayu-cho, [[Matsue|Matsue City]] have been excavated from jade-making sites in the Kinai region, such as the Soga Site, Furu {{ill|10=ja|11=布留遺跡|Site|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, and Nagahara Site. In particular, jade-making sites using Izumo-style stone materials such as jasper and quartz have been found at the Tani Site near Ise, the base of the Yamato no Agoko clan. Outside the Nara Basin, small amounts of remains have been excavated from the Nagahara ruins in Kawachi Province. In addition to Yayoi period ruins, the remains of a jade-making workshop thought to date from the end of the 4th century to the beginning of the 5th century have been discovered along the coasts of Lake Shinji and Lake Nakaumi, and whetstones made from crystalline schist mined in the {{ill|10=ja|11=紀の川|Yoshino River|lt=Yoshino River|en|qq=draft|qq=draft}} and {{ill|10=ja|11=紀の川|Kinokawa_River|lt=Kino River|en|qq=draft|qq=draft}} basins in Nara Prefecture were used. {{ill|Ichishi no Nagaochi|fr}}, an ancestor of Yamato no Agoko, appears in the legends of {{ill|Amenohiboko|en|qq=draft|qq=draft}} and is also said to have gone to Izumo to welcome Nomi no Sukune. Nomi no Sukune was famous for his {{ill|10=ja|11=当麻蹴速|sumo|qq=draft|qq=draft}} match with Tagima no Kehaya, and according to Kikuchi Teruo, this story is the origin of the rice farming ritual in which the spirits of the earth are calmed by sumo. In this story, the land of Tagima that Nomi no Sukune acquired was located at the point where the Nara Basin emerges from [[Osaka Bay|Osaka]] Bay via {{ill|Takeuchi Pass|ja|竹内峠|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, where Sugawara Shrine is located, and it was a strategic transportation hub that also leads to {{ill|10=ja|11=葛城|Katsuragi|4=en|qq=draft|qq=draft}} to the south. The nearby Ota ruins are the remains of a settlement from the early Kofun period, and pottery from the {{ill|San'in region|en}} estimated to date to the first half of the 4th century has also been excavated. This suggests that there was evidence of a connection with the San'in region around the "Tagima Path" from the time of Nomi no Sukune. As described above, the relationship between the [[Yamato no Kuni no Miyatsuko|Yamato clan]] troops, the Izumo forces, and the fishermen of Awaji Island in the Agokoro legend conveys some historical fact, and it is highly likely that these were condensed and linked together in one person called Yamato no Agoko. == Family tree == Many clans may be descendants of Furutama no Mikoto. This includes the {{ill|Owari clan|ja|尾張氏|en|qq=draft|qq=draft}} and [[Yamato no Kuni no Miyatsuko]]. This is a subject of debate.{{Cite web|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160422190938/http://wwr2.ucom.ne.jp/hetoyc15/keihu/amabe/amabe-k2.htm|access-date=2023-12-13|website=web.archive.org}} revision.text:
{{基礎情報 公家 | 氏名 = 倭吾子籠 | 画像 = | 画像サイズ = | 画像説明 = | 時代 = [[古墳時代]] | 生誕 = 不明 | 死没 = 不明 | 改名 = | 別名 = | 諡号 = | 神号 = | 戒名 = | 墓所 = | 官位 = | 主君 = [[仁徳天皇]]、[[履中天皇]]、[[雄略天皇]] | 氏族 = [[倭氏|倭直]]（[[倭国造]]） | 父母 = | 兄弟 = | 妻 = | 子 = | 特記事項 = }} '''倭 吾子籠'''（やまと の あごこ、生没年不詳）は『[[日本書紀]]』などに伝わる古代日本の[[豪族]]。[[倭国造]]（やまとのくにのみやつこ）の祖先。『[[古事記]]』には彼に関する記載は存在しない。
== 記録 == 『[[日本書紀]]』の登場人物としては、比較的多くの箇所に出没する。 === 倭の屯田と屯倉 === 『日本書紀』巻第十一には、推定[[310年]]（[[応神天皇]]41年）の天皇崩御後、皇位が定まらぬ状態の中で争われた、[[額田大中彦皇子]]（ぬかたのおおなかつひこのみこ）と屯田司（みたのつかさ）の[[淤宇宿禰]]（おうのすくね）との、倭の[[屯田]]（みた）と[[屯倉]]を巡る争議のことが記されている。額田大中彦皇子に土地を一方的に接収された淤宇宿禰は、菟道稚郎子、ついで大鷦鷯尊（おおさざきのみこと、のちの[[仁徳天皇]]）に訴え出た結果、倭の屯田と屯倉のことは、現在韓国（からくに）に派遣されている吾子籠（あごこ）が知っていると判明した。淤宇宿禰は大鷦鷯尊の勧めにより、昼夜兼行で淡路の海人（あま）とともに韓国へ行き、吾子籠を連れて帰ってきた。
吾子籠は「倭の屯田・屯倉」は〔[[垂仁天皇]]〕の時代に、皇太子であった[[景行天皇]]〕に「凡（おおよ）そ倭の屯田は、毎（つね）に御宇帝皇（あめのした しらす すめらみこと＝現在即位している天皇)の屯田なり。其れ帝皇（みかど）の子（みこ）と雖（いえど）も、御宇（あめのした しら）すに非（あら）ずは、掌（つかさど）ること得（え）じ」として伝えられたものであって、時の天皇が管掌するものであることを証言した。これにより、額田大中彦皇子は自省し、土地管理問題は淤宇宿禰にとって有利なものとして決着した。
しかし、この事件のバックには、額田大中彦皇子の同母弟である[[大山守皇子]]がいたと思われ、彼はこの裁定に不服を唱え、事態は皇位抗争劇へと発展していった<ref>『日本書紀』仁徳天皇即位前紀条</ref>。
『[[古事記]]』にはこのような事情は語られていない。
=== 大井川の流木 === 同じく『書紀』巻十一は、以下のような物語を伝えている。
{{quotation|六十二年の夏五月（推定[[374年]]）に、[[遠淡海国造|遠江国司]]<small>（とほつあふみのくに の みこともち）</small>表上言<small>（まう）</small>さく、「大<small>（おほ）</small>きなる樹<small>（き）</small>有りて、[[大井川|大井河]]<small>（おほゐがは）</small>より流れて、河<small>（かは）</small>曲<small>（くま）</small>り停<small>（とどま）</small>れり。其大きさ十囲<small>（とうだき＝30尺、およそ300メートル）</small>。本<small>（もと）</small>は壱<small>（ひとつ）</small>にして末は両<small>（またまた）</small>なり」とまうす。時に倭直吾子籠<small>（やまとのあたひあごこ）</small>を遣<small>（つかは）</small>して船に造らしむ。而<small>（しかう）</small>して南海<small>（みなみのみち）</small>より運<small>（めぐら）</small>して、難波津<small>（なにはのつ）</small>に将<small>（ゐ）</small>て来<small>（きた）</small>りて、御船<small>（みふね）</small>に充<small>（あ）</small>てつ。<ref>『日本書紀』仁徳天皇62年5月条</ref>}}
大井川に流れ着いた巨木を、吾子籠が船に造り直した、というエピソードである。この時は吾子籠は「倭直」と呼ばれている。
ちなみに、『書紀』巻第十二では、[[履中天皇]]が両俣船（ふたまたぶね）を磐余市磯池（いわれのいちしのいけ）に浮かべている<ref>『日本書紀』履中天皇3年11月6日条</ref>。
=== 住吉仲皇子の反乱 === 『書紀』巻十二によると、住吉仲皇子（すみのえ の なかつ みこ）と倭直吾子籠とは親しい間柄であった。そのため、推定[[399年]]、仲皇子が皇太子の去来穂別皇子（いざほわけ の みこ、のちの履中天皇）に反旗を翻した際には、仲皇子に味方しようとし、精兵数百人を「攪食（かきはみ）の栗林（くるす）」（[[忍海郡]]来栖郷と言われている）というところに集めて、太子を待ち構えた。しかし、皇太子の兵が思いのほか多数であったことに気づくと態度を変え、
{{quotation|「伝<small>（つて）</small>に聞く、皇太子<small>（ひつぎのみこ）</small>、非常之事<small>（おもほえぬこと）</small>有<small>（ま）</small>しますと。助けまつらむとして兵<small>（つはもの）</small>を備<small>（そな）</small>へて待ちたてまつる」}}
猜疑心にとらわれていた皇太子は、吾子籠の心を疑い、殺そうとした。そこで、吾子籠は恐れ入って、妹の日之媛（ひのひめ）を献上し、死罪を免れた。この時から倭直は、采女を貢上するようになった、という<ref>『日本書紀』履中天皇即位前紀条</ref>。
履中即位前紀のほかの箇所には、皇太子が[[石上神宮]]に逃亡する際に、飛鳥山の登り口で少女に遭遇し、道の安全を尋ねる場面があるが、
「兵（つはもの）を執れる者、多（さは）に山中に満（いは）めり。廻（めぐりかへ）りて、当摩径（たぎまのみち）より踰（こ）えたまへ」
と忠告される場面も存在する。これらは倭直氏が伏兵がおけるほど、この周辺の地理に習熟していたことを示している。
=== 宍人部の献上 === 『書紀』巻第十四には、雄略天皇が御馬瀬（みませ）での猟の後で激怒して大津馬飼（おおつ の うまかい）を斬り殺し、その収拾のために、母親の[[忍坂大中姫]]皇太后が倭の采女「日媛」（ひのひめ）を献上する話がある。その時の会話がきっかけで[[宍人部]]（ししひとべ）が設置され、膳臣長野（かしわで の おみ ながの）ら3人が任命されるのだが、加えて、「大倭国造（おおやまとのくにのみやつこ）吾子籠宿禰」は狭穂子（さほのこ）鳥別（とりわけ）を献上して宍人部に加え、「臣連伴造国造、又随（したが）ひて続（つ）ぎて貢（たてまつ）る」<ref>『日本書紀』雄略天皇2年10月6日条</ref>とある。
ここに登場する日媛と、住吉の時の妹の「日之媛」は同一人物であり、伝承の混同があるのではないか、と言われている。
== 考証 == 以上の記述は、5世紀前半に出雲臣の祖となる首長たちが、大和政権と深くかかわり、朝鮮半島との交渉を行っていた、という考古学から判明した歴史的事実と合わせて考える必要がある。さらに言えば、[[淡路島]]の海人集団とのつながりや、[[野見宿禰]]伝承との関連をも見て行く必要がある。
前述の物語に頻繁に現れるのは淡路島の海人集団で、淤宇宿禰が韓国から吾子籠を迎えに行った際にも海人集団の水手が活躍しており、住吉仲皇子の伝承でも、[[阿曇浜子|阿曇連浜子]]に率いられて、「淡路の野嶋の海人」が暗躍している。
淡路島の木戸原遺跡・雨流遺跡からは半島や出雲との関係を示す遺物が多数発掘されている。曽我遺跡・[[布留遺跡]]・長原遺跡など、畿内の玉作の遺跡からは、[[松江市]][[玉湯町]]花仙山（かせんやま）産出の碧玉原石が出土しており、とりわけ、倭直の拠点である[[磯城]]周辺の谷遺跡などから、碧玉・水晶などの出雲系の石材を使用した玉作遺跡が見つかっている。奈良盆地以外では、河内国の長原遺跡からも少量の出土が確認できる。弥生時代の遺跡のほか、宍道湖・中海沿岸には4世紀末から5世紀はじめにかけてのものと思われる、玉作工房遺跡が発見され、奈良県の[[吉野川 (奈良県)|吉野川]]・[[紀ノ川]]流域で産出され結晶片岩製砥石が使用されている。
倭直の祖先である[[市磯長尾市]]（いちし の ながおち）は、[[アメノヒボコ|天日槍]]伝承などに「登場するが、野見宿禰を迎えに出雲へ行ったことも見受けられる。野見宿禰は[[当麻蹴速|当摩蹶速]]（たぎま の けはや）との相撲勝負で有名であり、菊池照夫によると、この話は相撲によって地霊を沈める稲作農耕儀礼の起源だとされているが、この話で、野見宿禰が獲得した当麻の地が、[[大阪湾]]から[[竹内峠]]を経由した奈良盆地に出たところに位置していること、菅原神社が鎮座し、南へゆくと[[葛城]]へも通じている交通の要衝の地であり、近隣の大田遺跡は古墳時代前期の集落遺跡で、4世紀前半のものと推定される[[山陰]]系の土器も出土されている。このことは、野見宿禰時代から、「当摩径」あたりに山陰地方との関わりの形跡があったことが窺われる。
以上のように、吾子籠伝承における倭直と出雲勢力、淡路島の海人集団との関係は、何らかの史実を伝えており、それらが倭吾子籠という一人物に集約されて結びつけられた可能性が高いといえる。

revision.text:
{{基礎情報 公家 | 氏名 = 倭吾子籠 | 画像 = | 画像サイズ = | 画像説明 = | 時代 = [[古墳時代]] | 生誕 = 不明 | 死没 = 不明 | 改名 = | 別名 = | 諡号 = | 神号 = | 戒名 = | 墓所 = | 官位 = | 主君 = [[仁徳天皇]]、[[履中天皇]]、[[雄略天皇]] | 氏族 = [[倭氏|倭直]]（[[倭国造]]） | 父母 = | 兄弟 = | 妻 = | 子 = | 特記事項 = }} '''倭 吾子籠'''（やまと の あごこ、生没年不詳）は『[[日本書紀]]』などに伝わる古代日本の[[豪族]]。[[倭国造]]（やまとのくにのみやつこ）の祖先。『[[古事記]]』には彼に関する記載は存在しない。
== 記録 == 『[[日本書紀]]』の登場人物としては、比較的多くの箇所に出没する。 === 倭の屯田と屯倉 === 『日本書紀』巻第十一には、推定[[310年]]（[[応神天皇]]41年）の天皇崩御後、皇位が定まらぬ状態の中で争われた、[[額田大中彦皇子]]（ぬかたのおおなかつひこのみこ）と屯田司（みたのつかさ）の[[淤宇宿禰]]（おうのすくね）との、倭の[[屯田]]（みた）と[[屯倉]]を巡る争議のことが記されている。額田大中彦皇子に土地を一方的に接収された淤宇宿禰は、菟道稚郎子、ついで大鷦鷯尊（おおさざきのみこと、のちの[[仁徳天皇]]）に訴え出た結果、倭の屯田と屯倉のことは、現在韓国（からくに）に派遣されている吾子籠（あごこ）が知っていると判明した。淤宇宿禰は大鷦鷯尊の勧めにより、昼夜兼行で淡路の海人（あま）とともに韓国へ行き、吾子籠を連れて帰ってきた。
吾子籠は「倭の屯田・屯倉」は〔[[垂仁天皇]]〕の時代に、皇太子であった[[景行天皇]]〕に「凡（おおよ）そ倭の屯田は、毎（つね）に御宇帝皇（あめのした しらす すめらみこと＝現在即位している天皇)の屯田なり。其れ帝皇（みかど）の子（みこ）と雖（いえど）も、御宇（あめのした しら）すに非（あら）ずは、掌（つかさど）ること得（え）じ」として伝えられたものであって、時の天皇が管掌するものであることを証言した。これにより、額田大中彦皇子は自省し、土地管理問題は淤宇宿禰にとって有利なものとして決着した。
しかし、この事件のバックには、額田大中彦皇子の同母弟である[[大山守皇子]]がいたと思われ、彼はこの裁定に不服を唱え、事態は皇位抗争劇へと発展していった<ref>『日本書紀』仁徳天皇即位前紀条</ref>。
『[[古事記]]』にはこのような事情は語られていない。
=== 大井川の流木 === 同じく『書紀』巻十一は、以下のような物語を伝えている。
{{quotation|六十二年の夏五月（推定[[374年]]）に、[[遠淡海国造|遠江国司]]<small>（とほつあふみのくに の みこともち）</small>表上言<small>（まう）</small>さく、「大<small>（おほ）</small>きなる樹<small>（き）</small>有りて、[[大井川|大井河]]<small>（おほゐがは）</small>より流れて、河<small>（かは）</small>曲<small>（くま）</small>り停<small>（とどま）</small>れり。其大きさ十囲<small>（とうだき＝30尺、およそ300メートル）</small>。本<small>（もと）</small>は壱<small>（ひとつ）</small>にして末は両<small>（またまた）</small>なり」とまうす。時に倭直吾子籠<small>（やまとのあたひあごこ）</small>を遣<small>（つかは）</small>して船に造らしむ。而<small>（しかう）</small>して南海<small>（みなみのみち）</small>より運<small>（めぐら）</small>して、難波津<small>（なにはのつ）</small>に将<small>（ゐ）</small>て来<small>（きた）</small>りて、御船<small>（みふね）</small>に充<small>（あ）</small>てつ。<ref>『日本書紀』仁徳天皇62年5月条</ref>}}
大井川に流れ着いた巨木を、吾子籠が船に造り直した、というエピソードである。この時は吾子籠は「倭直」と呼ばれている。
ちなみに、『書紀』巻第十二では、[[履中天皇]]が両俣船（ふたまたぶね）を磐余市磯池（いわれのいちしのいけ）に浮かべている<ref>『日本書紀』履中天皇3年11月6日条</ref>。
=== 住吉仲皇子の反乱 === 『書紀』巻十二によると、住吉仲皇子（すみのえ の なかつ みこ）と倭直吾子籠とは親しい間柄であった。そのため、推定[[399年]]、仲皇子が皇太子の去来穂別皇子（いざほわけ の みこ、のちの履中天皇）に反旗を翻した際には、仲皇子に味方しようとし、精兵数百人を「攪食（かきはみ）の栗林（くるす）」（[[忍海郡]]来栖郷と言われている）というところに集めて、太子を待ち構えた。しかし、皇太子の兵が思いのほか多数であったことに気づくと態度を変え、
{{quotation|「伝<small>（つて）</small>に聞く、皇太子<small>（ひつぎのみこ）</small>、非常之事<small>（おもほえぬこと）</small>有<small>（ま）</small>しますと。助けまつらむとして兵<small>（つはもの）</small>を備<small>（そな）</small>へて待ちたてまつる」}}
猜疑心にとらわれていた皇太子は、吾子籠の心を疑い、殺そうとした。そこで、吾子籠は恐れ入って、妹の日之媛（ひのひめ）を献上し、死罪を免れた。この時から倭直は、采女を貢上するようになった、という<ref>『日本書紀』履中天皇即位前紀条</ref>。
履中即位前紀のほかの箇所には、皇太子が[[石上神宮]]に逃亡する際に、飛鳥山の登り口で少女に遭遇し、道の安全を尋ねる場面があるが、
「兵（つはもの）を執れる者、多（さは）に山中に満（いは）めり。廻（めぐりかへ）りて、当摩径（たぎまのみち）より踰（こ）えたまへ」
と忠告される場面も存在する。これらは倭直氏が伏兵がおけるほど、この周辺の地理に習熟していたことを示している。
=== 宍人部の献上 === 『書紀』巻第十四には、雄略天皇が御馬瀬（みませ）での猟の後で激怒して大津馬飼（おおつ の うまかい）を斬り殺し、その収拾のために、母親の[[忍坂大中姫]]皇太后が倭の采女「日媛」（ひのひめ）を献上する話がある。その時の会話がきっかけで[[宍人部]]（ししひとべ）が設置され、膳臣長野（かしわで の おみ ながの）ら3人が任命されるのだが、加えて、「大倭国造（おおやまとのくにのみやつこ）吾子籠宿禰」は狭穂子（さほのこ）鳥別（とりわけ）を献上して宍人部に加え、「臣連伴造国造、又随（したが）ひて続（つ）ぎて貢（たてまつ）る」<ref>『日本書紀』雄略天皇2年10月6日条</ref>とある。
ここに登場する日媛と、住吉の時の妹の「日之媛」は同一人物であり、伝承の混同があるのではないか、と言われている。
== 考証 == 以上の記述は、5世紀前半に出雲臣の祖となる首長たちが、大和政権と深くかかわり、朝鮮半島との交渉を行っていた、という考古学から判明した歴史的事実と合わせて考える必要がある。さらに言えば、[[淡路島]]の海人集団とのつながりや、[[野見宿禰]]伝承との関連をも見て行く必要がある。
前述の物語に頻繁に現れるのは淡路島の海人集団で、淤宇宿禰が韓国から吾子籠を迎えに行った際にも海人集団の水手が活躍しており、住吉仲皇子の伝承でも、[[阿曇浜子|阿曇連浜子]]に率いられて、「淡路の野嶋の海人」が暗躍している。

倭直の祖先である[[市磯長尾市]]（いちし の ながおち）は、[[アメノヒボコ|天日槍]]伝承などに「登場するが、野見宿禰を迎えに出雲へ行ったことも見受けられる。野見宿禰は[[当麻蹴速|当摩蹶速]]（たぎま の けはや）との相撲勝負で有名であり、菊池照夫によると、この話は相撲によって地霊を沈める稲作農耕儀礼の起源だとされているが、この話で、野見宿禰が獲得した当麻の地が、[[大阪湾]]から[[竹内峠]]を経由した奈良盆地に出たところに位置していること、菅原神社が鎮座し、南へゆくと[[葛城]]へも通じている交通の要衝の地であり、近隣の大田遺跡は古墳時代前期の集落遺跡で、4世紀前半のものと推定される[[山陰]]系の土器も出土されている。このことは、野見宿禰時代から、「当摩径」あたりに山陰地方との関わりの形跡があったことが窺われる。

He served under [[Emperor Nintoku]] , [[Emperor Richū|Emperor Richu]] , and [[Emperor Yūryaku|Emperor Yuryaku]] == Origin == {{Short description|Japanese noble family}} Yamato no Agoko came from the [[Yamato no Kuni no Miyatsuko|Yamato no Atai clan]]. Their [[Ujigami]] or clan god is [[Yamato Okunitama]] of [[Ōyamato Shrine]]{{Cite web|title=International Symposium "Perspectives on Japanese history and literature from ancient historical replacing the emaciated Nunaki-iri-hime. {{ill|Ichishi no Nagaochi|ja|市磯長尾市|fr|qq=draft|qq=draft}} would be the ancestor of the Yamato no Kuni no Miyatsuko.{{Cite web|title=Page:Nihongi by Aston.djvu/208|url=https://en.wikisource.org/wiki/Page:Nihongi_by_Aston.djvu/208|access-date=2023-10-24|website=en.wikisource.org|language=en}} == Historical record == By the way, in the twelfth volume of the "Nihon Shoki," [[Emperor Richū|Emperor Richu]] floats a two-pronged boat on Iware City Isoike Pond. 『日本書紀』履中天皇3rd year 11月6日条 === The Yamato military fields and warehouses === Similarly, Volume 11 of the "Shoki" tells the following story: This is the story of how Agoko remade a giant tree that had washed up on the Oi River into a boat. At this time, Agoko was called "Yamato no Agoko." The Crown Prince, who was filled with suspicion, became suspicious of Agogo's true intentions and tried to kill him. So Agoko felt humbled and offered his younger sister, Hinohime, as a tribute, and was spared the death penalty. From this time on, Yamato no Agoko began to offer court ladies as tribute. 『日本書紀』履中天皇即位前紀条 According to Volume 12 of the "Shoki," Prince Sumiyoshi Nakatsu and Yamato Naokogo were on close terms. Therefore, when Prince Naka rebelled against the Crown Prince, Prince Izahowake (later Emperor Richu), presumably in the year 399, he tried to side with Prince Naka and gathered several hundred elite soldiers at a place called "Kakihami no Kurusu" (said to be Kurusu-go, {{ill|10=ja|11=忍海郡|Oshikai county|qq=draft|qq=draft}} ) and waited for the Crown Prince. However, when he realized that the Crown Prince's troops were more numerous than he had expected, he changed his attitude. === Driftwood of the Oi River === Another part of the Richū Sokui Chronicle states that the Crown Prince, on his way to {{ill|Isonokami Shrine|en|Isonokami Shrine}}, encounters a young girl at the foot of Mt. Asuka and asks her about the safety of the journey.{{Quote frame|In the summer of May of the 62nd year (estimated to be 374 AD), the governor of Tōtōmi Province reported, "There is a large tree that flowed from the {{ill|Ōi River|en}}, bending and stopping at the river's curve. Its size is around ten tōdaki (approximately 300 meters). Initially singular, it splits into two at the ends." At that time, Yamato no Ataī Agoko was dispatched to construct a ship from it. Thus, navigating from the Southern Sea, it arrived at Naniwa Port, where it was dedicated as a royal ship.『日本書紀』仁徳天皇62nd year 5月条|qq=draft|qq=draft}}This episode is about a massive log that had drifted to the Ōigawa River, which Agoko then remade into a ship. At this time, Agoko was referred to as "Yamato no Atai." Incidentally, in Volume 12 of the "Nihon Shoki," it is mentioned that Emperor Nintoku floated a bifurcated boat (a boat split into two parts) in the Iware Market Isopond. === Prince Sumiyoshi's Rebellion === The fourteenth volume of the "Shoki" tells the story of Emperor Yuryaku, who, in a fit of rage after a hunt at Mimase, killed Otsu no Umakai with the sword, and his mother, Empress {{ill|Oshisaka no Ōnakatsuhime|en}}, presenting the Wa court lady "Hinohime" to settle the matter. This conversation led to the establishment of the {{ill|10=ja|11=宍人部|Shishihitobe|qq=draft|qq=draft}} (the branch of the Shishihito clan), and the appointment of three members, including Kashiwadeno no Omi Nagano. In addition, the “Oyamato no Kuni no Miyatsuko Agoko no Sukune” presented Sahonoko Toriwake to the Shishihitobe, and “the Ministers of the Imperial Court, Tomo no Miyatsuko and Kuni no Miyatsuko, followed suit and continued to offer tribute.” 『日本書紀』雄略天皇2nd year 10月6日条{{Quote frame|"I hear through the grapevine that an extraordinary event has occurred to the Crown Prince. Preparing soldiers, we stand ready to offer assistance."}}As a character in the " [[Nihon Shoki]] ," he appears in relatively many places. Volume 11 of the Nihon Shoki records a dispute over the Yamato military fields and warehouses between {{ill|10=ja|11=額田大中彦皇子|Prince Nukata no Onakahiko|qq=draft|qq=draft}} and the {{ill|Tuntian|lt=military farm|en|10=ja|11=屯田|qq=draft|qq=draft}} administrator, {{ill|10=ja|11=淤宇宿禰|Ounosukune|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, which took place after the death of the Emperor in what is [[Emperor Ōjin|believed]] to be 310 (the 41st year of the reign of Emperor Ojin) and {{ill|10=ja|11=屯倉|the Imperial Throne|qq=draft|qq=draft}} was in a state of uncertainty. When Prince Nukata no Oonakahiko unilaterally confiscated his land, Ousukune appealed to Uji no Wakairoko and then to Osazaki no Mikoto (later [[Emperor Nintoku]] ), and it was discovered that Agoko, who was currently stationed in Karakuni, knew about the Wa military fields and military storehouses. Following the advice of Ootori-no-Mikoto, Ousukune traveled day and night to Korea with Awaji fishermen and returned with the child's basket. Akogo testified that the "{{ill|Tuntian|lt=military farms|en|10=ja|11=屯田|qq=draft|qq=draft}} (屯田) and {{ill|military granary|lt=granaries|ja|屯倉|qq=draft|qq=draft}} (屯倉) of Wa" were passed down to Emperor Keikō, who was [[Emperor Keikō|the crown prince]] during the reign of [[Emperor Suinin]], saying, "Generally, the {{ill|Tuntian|lt=military farms|en|10=ja|11=屯田|qq=draft|qq=draft}} (屯田) of Yamato are the military farms (屯田) of the current emperor. Even if one is the son of the emperor, he cannot be in charge unless he is the emperor's son," and that they were under the control of the emperor of the time. This caused Prince Nukata-Onakahiko to reflect on his actions, and the land management issue was resolved in Ousukune's favor. The [[Kojiki]] makes no mention of such circumstances. === Presentation from the Shishitobe === It is said that the Hihime who appears here and Sumiyoshi's younger sister, Hinohime, are the same person, and that there may be some confusion in the legends. The above description needs to be considered in conjunction with historical facts uncovered by archaeology, which show that the chiefs who became the ancestors of the Izumo no Omi clan in the first half of the 5th century were deeply involved with the Yamato government and engaged in negotiations with the Korean Peninsula. Furthermore, it is necessary to look at the connections with the {{ill|10=ja|11=淡路島|Awaji Island|qq=draft|qq=draft}} fishermen group and the relationship with the {{ill|Nomi no Sukune|en}} legend. == Research == A group of fishermen from Awaji Island appears frequently in the aforementioned story; sailors from this group were active when Ousukune went to retrieve the Akoko basket from Korea; and in the legend of Prince Sumiyoshi Nakatsu, "fishermen from Nojima on Awaji" are secretly active, led by {{ill|10=ja|11=阿曇浜子|Azumi no Muraji Hamako|qq=draft|qq=draft}}. Many artifacts indicating connections to the peninsula and Izumo have been excavated from the Kidohara and Uryu ruins on Awaji Island. Jasper rough stones from {{ill|10=ja|11=玉湯町|Kasenyama|qq=draft|qq=draft}} in Tamayu-cho, [[Matsue|Matsue City]] have been excavated from jade-making sites in the Kinai region, such as the Soga Site, Furu {{ill|10=ja|11=布留遺跡|Site|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, and Nagahara Site. In particular, jade-making sites using Izumo-style stone materials such as jasper and quartz have been found at the Tani Site near Ise, the base of the Yamato no Agoko clan. Outside the Nara Basin, small amounts of remains have been excavated from the Nagahara ruins in Kawachi Province. In addition to Yayoi period ruins, the remains of a jade-making workshop thought to date from the end of the 4th century to the beginning of the 5th century have been discovered along the coasts of Lake Shinji and Lake Nakaumi, and whetstones made from crystalline schist mined in the {{ill|10=ja|11=紀の川|Yoshino River|lt=Yoshino River|en|qq=draft|qq=draft}} and {{ill|10=ja|11=紀の川|Kinokawa_River|lt=Kino River|en|qq=draft|qq=draft}} basins in Nara Prefecture were used. {{ill|Ichishi no Nagaochi|fr}}, an ancestor of Yamato no Agoko, appears in the legends of {{ill|Amenohiboko|en|qq=draft|qq=draft}} and is also said to have gone to Izumo to welcome Nomi no Sukune. Nomi no Sukune was famous for his {{ill|10=ja|11=当麻蹴速|sumo|qq=draft|qq=draft}} match with Tagima no Kehaya, and according to Kikuchi Teruo, this story is the origin of the rice farming ritual in which the spirits of the earth are calmed by sumo. In this story, the land of Tagima that Nomi no Sukune acquired was located at the point where the Nara Basin emerges from [[Osaka Bay|Osaka]] Bay via {{ill|Takeuchi Pass|ja|竹内峠|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, where Sugawara Shrine is located, and it was a strategic transportation hub that also leads to {{ill|10=ja|11=葛城|Katsuragi|4=en|qq=draft|qq=draft}} to the south. The nearby Ota ruins are the remains of a settlement from the early Kofun period, and pottery from the {{ill|San'in region|en}} estimated to date to the first half of the 4th century has also been excavated. This suggests that there was evidence of a connection with the San'in region around the "Tagima Path" from the time of Nomi no Sukune. As described above, the relationship between the [[Yamato no Kuni no Miyatsuko|Yamato clan]] troops, the Izumo forces, and the fishermen of Awaji Island in the Agokoro legend conveys some historical fact, and it is highly likely that these were condensed and linked together in one person called Yamato no Agoko. == Family tree == Many clans may be descendants of Furutama no Mikoto. This includes the {{ill|Owari clan|ja|尾張氏|en|qq=draft|qq=draft}} and [[Yamato no Kuni no Miyatsuko]]. This is a subject of debate.{{Cite web|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160422190938/http://wwr2.ucom.ne.jp/hetoyc15/keihu/amabe/amabe-k2.htm|access-date=2023-12-13|website=web.archive.org}} Akogo testified that the "{{ill|Tuntian|lt=military farms|en|10=ja|11=屯田|qq=draft|qq=draft}} (屯田) and {{ill|military granary|lt=granaries|ja|屯倉|qq=draft|qq=draft}} (屯倉) of Wa" were passed down to Emperor Keikō, who was [[Emperor Keikō|the crown prince]] during the reign of [[Emperor Suinin]], saying, "Generally, the {{ill|Tuntian|lt=military farms|en|10=ja|11=屯田|qq=draft|qq=draft}} (屯田) of Yamato are the military farms (屯田) of the current emperor. Even if one is the son of the emperor, he cannot be in charge unless he is the emperor's son," and that they were under the control of the emperor of the time. This caused Prince Nukata-Onakahiko to reflect on his actions, and the land management issue was resolved in Ousukune's favor. The [[Kojiki]] makes no mention of such circumstances. === Presentation from the Shishitobe === It is said that the Hihime who appears here and Sumiyoshi's younger sister, Hinohime, are the same person, and that there may be some confusion in the legends. The above description needs to be considered in conjunction with historical facts uncovered by archaeology, which show that the chiefs who became the ancestors of the Izumo no Omi clan in the first half of the 5th century were deeply involved with the Yamato government and engaged in negotiations with the Korean Peninsula. Furthermore, it is necessary to look at the connections with the {{ill|10=ja|11=淡路島|Awaji Island|qq=draft|qq=draft}} fishermen group and the relationship with the {{ill|Nomi no Sukune|en}} legend. == Research == A group of fishermen from Awaji Island appears frequently in the aforementioned story; sailors from this group were active when Ousukune went to retrieve the Akoko basket from Korea; and in the legend of Prince Sumiyoshi Nakatsu, "fishermen from Nojima on Awaji" are secretly active, led by {{ill|10=ja|11=阿曇浜子|Azumi no Muraji Hamako|qq=draft|qq=draft}}. Many artifacts indicating connections to the peninsula and Izumo have been excavated from the Kidohara and Uryu ruins on Awaji Island. Jasper rough stones from {{ill|10=ja|11=玉湯町|Kasenyama|qq=draft|qq=draft}} in Tamayu-cho, [[Matsue|Matsue City]] have been excavated from jade-making sites in the Kinai region, such as the Soga Site, Furu {{ill|10=ja|11=布留遺跡|Site|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, and Nagahara Site. In particular, jade-making sites using Izumo-style stone materials such as jasper and quartz have been found at the Tani Site near Ise, the base of the Yamato no Agoko clan. Outside the Nara Basin, small amounts of remains have been excavated from the Nagahara ruins in Kawachi Province. In addition to Yayoi period ruins, the remains of a jade-making workshop thought to date from the end of the 4th century to the beginning of the 5th century have been discovered along the coasts of Lake Shinji and Lake Nakaumi, and whetstones made from crystalline schist mined in the {{ill|10=ja|11=紀の川|Yoshino River|lt=Yoshino River|en|qq=draft|qq=draft}} and {{ill|10=ja|11=紀の川|Kinokawa_River|lt=Kino River|en|qq=draft|qq=draft}} basins in Nara Prefecture were used. {{ill|Ichishi no Nagaochi|fr}}, an ancestor of Yamato no Agoko, appears in the legends of {{ill|Amenohiboko|en|qq=draft|qq=draft}} and is also said to have gone to Izumo to welcome Nomi no Sukune. Nomi no Sukune was famous for his {{ill|10=ja|11=当麻蹴速|sumo|qq=draft|qq=draft}} match with Tagima no Kehaya, and according to Kikuchi Teruo, this story is the origin of the rice farming ritual in which the spirits of the earth are calmed by sumo. In this story, the land of Tagima that Nomi no Sukune acquired was located at the point where the Nara Basin emerges from [[Osaka Bay|Osaka]] Bay via {{ill|Takeuchi Pass|ja|竹内峠|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, where Sugawara Shrine is located, and it was a strategic transportation hub that also leads to {{ill|10=ja|11=葛城|Katsuragi|4=en|qq=draft|qq=draft}} to the south. The nearby Ota ruins are the remains of a settlement from the early Kofun period, and pottery from the {{ill|San'in region|en}} estimated to date to the first half of the 4th century has also been excavated. This suggests that there was evidence of a connection with the San'in region around the "Tagima Path" from the time of Nomi no Sukune. As described above, the relationship between the [[Yamato no Kuni no Miyatsuko|Yamato clan]] troops, the Izumo forces, and the fishermen of Awaji Island in the Agokoro legend conveys some historical fact, and it is highly likely that these were condensed and linked together in one person called Yamato no Agoko. == Family tree == Many clans may be descendants of Furutama no Mikoto. This includes the {{ill|Owari clan|ja|尾張氏|en|qq=draft|qq=draft}} and [[Yamato no Kuni no Miyatsuko]]. This is a subject of debate.{{Cite web|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160422190938/http://wwr2.ucom.ne.jp/hetoyc15/keihu/amabe/amabe-k2.htm|access-date=2023-12-13|website=web.archive.org}} volume of the "Nihon Shoki," [[Emperor Richū|Emperor Richu]] floats a two-pronged boat on Iware City Isoike Pond. 『日本書紀』履中天皇3rd year 11月6日条 === The Yamato military fields and warehouses === Similarly, Volume 11 of the "Shoki" tells the following story: This is the story of how Agoko remade a giant tree that had washed up on the Oi River into a boat. At this time, Agoko was called "Yamato no Agoko." The Crown Prince, who was filled with suspicion, became suspicious of Agogo's true intentions and tried to kill him. So Agoko felt humbled and offered his younger sister, Hinohime, as a tribute, and was spared the death penalty. From this time on, Yamato no Agoko began to offer court ladies as tribute. 『日本書紀』履中天皇即位前紀条 According to Volume 12 of the "Shoki," Prince Sumiyoshi Nakatsu and Yamato Naokogo were on close terms. Therefore, when Prince Naka rebelled against the Crown Prince, Prince Izahowake (later Emperor Richu), presumably in the year 399, he tried to side with Prince Naka and gathered several hundred elite soldiers at a place called "Kakihami no Kurusu" (said to be Kurusu-go, {{ill|10=ja|11=忍海郡|Oshikai county|qq=draft|qq=draft}} ) and waited for the Crown Prince. However, when he realized that the Crown Prince's troops were more numerous than he had expected, he changed his attitude. === Driftwood of the Oi River === Another part of the Richū Sokui Chronicle states that the Crown Prince, on his way to {{ill|Isonokami Shrine|en|Isonokami Shrine}}, encounters a young girl at the foot of Mt. Asuka and asks her about the safety of the journey.{{Quote frame|In the summer of May of the 62nd year (estimated to be 374 AD), the governor of Tōtōmi Province reported, "There is a large tree that flowed from the {{ill|Ōi River|en}}, bending and stopping at the river's curve. Its size is around ten tōdaki (approximately 300 meters). Initially singular, it splits into two at the ends." At that time, Yamato no Ataī Agoko was dispatched to construct a ship from it. Thus, navigating from the Southern Sea, it arrived at Naniwa Port, where it was dedicated as a royal ship.『日本書紀』仁徳天皇62nd year 5月条|qq=draft|qq=draft}}This episode is about a massive log that had drifted to the Ōigawa River, which Agoko then remade into a ship. At this time, Agoko was referred to as "Yamato no Atai." Incidentally, in Volume 12 of the "Nihon Shoki," it is mentioned that Emperor Nintoku floated a bifurcated boat (a boat split into two parts) in the Iware Market Isopond. === Prince Sumiyoshi's Rebellion === The fourteenth volume of the "Shoki" tells the story of Emperor Yuryaku, who, in a fit of rage after a hunt at Mimase, killed Otsu no Umakai with the sword, and his mother, Empress {{ill|Oshisaka no Ōnakatsuhime|en}}, presenting the Wa court lady "Hinohime" to settle the matter. This conversation led to the establishment of the {{ill|10=ja|11=宍人部|Shishihitobe|qq=draft|qq=draft}} (the branch of the Shishihito clan), and the appointment of three members, including Kashiwadeno no Omi Nagano. In addition, the “Oyamato no Kuni no Miyatsuko Agoko no Sukune” presented Sahonoko Toriwake to the Shishihitobe, and “the Ministers of the Imperial Court, Tomo no Miyatsuko and Kuni no Miyatsuko, followed suit and continued to offer tribute.” 『日本書紀』雄略天皇2nd year 10月6日条{{Quote frame|"I hear through the grapevine that an extraordinary event has occurred to the Crown Prince. The nearby Ota ruins are the remains of a settlement from the early Kofun period, and pottery from the {{ill|San'in region|en}} estimated to date to the first half of the 4th century has also been excavated. This suggests that there was evidence of a connection with the San'in region around the "Tagima Path" from the time of Nomi no Sukune. As described above, the relationship between the [[Yamato no Kuni no Miyatsuko|Yamato clan]] troops, the Izumo forces, and the fishermen of Awaji Island in the Agokoro legend conveys some historical fact, and it is highly likely that these were condensed and linked together in one person called Yamato no Agoko. == Family tree == Many clans may be descendants of Furutama no Mikoto. This includes the {{ill|Owari clan|ja|尾張氏|en|qq=draft|qq=draft}} and [[Yamato no Kuni no Miyatsuko]]. This is a subject of debate.{{Cite web|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160422190938/http://wwr2.ucom.ne.jp/hetoyc15/keihu/amabe/amabe-k2.htm|access-date=2023-12-13|website=web.archive.org}} volume of the "Nihon Shoki," [[Emperor Richū|Emperor Richu]] floats a two-pronged boat on Iware City Isoike Pond. 『日本書紀』履中天皇3rd year 11月6日条 === The Yamato military fields and warehouses === Similarly, Volume 11 of the "Shoki" tells the following story: This is the story of how Agoko remade a giant tree that had washed up on the Oi River into a boat. At this time, Agoko was called "Yamato no Agoko." The Crown Prince, who was filled with suspicion, became suspicious of Agogo's true intentions and tried to kill him. So Agoko felt humbled and offered his younger sister, Hinohime, as a tribute, and was spared the death penalty. From this time on, Yamato no Agoko began to offer court ladies as tribute. 『日本書紀』履中天皇即位前紀条 According to Volume 12 of the "Shoki," Prince Sumiyoshi Nakatsu and Yamato Naokogo were on close terms. Therefore, when Prince Naka rebelled against the Crown Prince, Prince Izahowake (later Emperor Richu), presumably in the year 399, he tried to side with Prince Naka and gathered several hundred elite soldiers at a place called "Kakihami no Kurusu" (said to be Kurusu-go, {{ill|10=ja|11=忍海郡|Oshikai county|qq=draft|qq=draft}} ) and waited for the Crown Prince. However, when he realized that the Crown Prince's troops were more numerous than he had expected, he changed his attitude. === Driftwood of the Oi River === Another part of the Richū Sokui Chronicle states that the Crown Prince, on his way to {{ill|Isonokami Shrine|en|Isonokami Shrine}}, encounters a young girl at the foot of Mt. Asuka and asks her about the safety of the journey.{{Quote frame|In the summer of May of the 62nd year (estimated to be 374 AD), the governor of Tōtōmi Province reported, "There is a large tree that flowed from the {{ill|Ōi River|en}}, bending and stopping at the river's curve. Its size is around ten tōdaki (approximately 300 meters). Initially singular, it splits into two at the ends." At that time, Yamato no Ataī Agoko was dispatched to construct a ship from it. Thus, navigating from the Southern Sea, it arrived at Naniwa Port, where it was dedicated as a royal ship.『日本書紀』仁徳天皇62nd year 5月条|qq=draft|qq=draft}}This episode is about a massive log that had drifted to the Ōigawa River, which Agoko then remade into a ship. At this time, Agoko was referred to as "Yamato no Atai." Incidentally, in Volume 12 of the "Nihon Shoki," it is mentioned that Emperor Nintoku floated a bifurcated boat (a boat split into two parts) in the Iware Market Isopond. === Prince Sumiyoshi's Rebellion === The fourteenth volume of the "Shoki" tells the story of Emperor Yuryaku, who, in a fit of rage after a hunt at Mimase, killed Otsu no Umakai with the sword, and his mother, Empress {{ill|Oshisaka no Ōnakatsuhime|en}}, presenting the Wa court lady "Hinohime" to settle the matter. This conversation led to the establishment of the {{ill|10=ja|11=宍人部|Shishihitobe|qq=draft|qq=draft}} (the branch of the Shishihito clan), and the appointment of three members, including Kashiwadeno no Omi Nagano. In addition, the “Oyamato no Kuni no Miyatsuko Agoko no Sukune” presented Sahonoko Toriwake to the Shishihitobe, and “the Ministers of the Imperial Court, Tomo no Miyatsuko and Kuni no Miyatsuko, followed suit and continued to offer tribute.” 『日本書紀』雄略天皇2nd year 10月6日条{{Quote frame|"I hear through the grapevine that an extraordinary event has occurred to the Crown Prince. Preparing soldiers, we stand ready to offer assistance."}}As a character in the " [[Nihon Shoki]] ," he appears in relatively many places. Volume 11 of the Nihon Shoki records a dispute over the Yamato military fields and warehouses between {{ill|10=ja|11=額田大中彦皇子|Prince Nukata no Onakahiko|qq=draft|qq=draft}} and the {{ill|Tuntian|lt=military farm|en|10=ja|11=屯田|qq=draft|qq=draft}} administrator, {{ill|10=ja|11=淤宇宿禰|Ounosukune|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, which took place after the death of the Emperor in what is [[Emperor Ōjin|believed]] to be 310 (the 41st year of the reign of Emperor Ojin) and {{ill|10=ja|11=屯倉|the Imperial Throne|qq=draft|qq=draft}} was in a state of uncertainty. When Prince Nukata no Oonakahiko unilaterally confiscated his land, Ousukune appealed to Uji no Wakairoko and then to Osazaki no Mikoto (later [[Emperor Nintoku]] ), and it was discovered that Agoko, who was currently stationed in Karakuni, knew about the Wa military fields and military storehouses. Following the advice of Ootori-no-Mikoto, Ousukune traveled day and night to Korea with Awaji fishermen and returned with the child's basket. Akogo testified that the "{{ill|Tuntian|lt=military farms|en|10=ja|11=屯田|qq=draft|qq=draft}} (屯田) and {{ill|military granary|lt=granaries|ja|屯倉|qq=draft|qq=draft}} (屯倉) of Wa" were passed down to Emperor Keikō, who was [[Emperor Keikō|the crown prince]] during the reign of [[Emperor Suinin]], saying, "Generally, the {{ill|Tuntian|lt=military farms|en|10=ja|11=屯田|qq=draft|qq=draft}} (屯田) of Yamato are the military farms (屯田) of the current emperor. Even if one is the son of the emperor, he cannot be in charge unless he is the emperor's son," and that they were under the control of the emperor of the time. This caused Prince Nukata-Onakahiko to reflect on his actions, and the land management issue was resolved in Ousukune's favor. The [[Kojiki]] makes no mention of such circumstances. === Presentation from the Shishitobe === It is said that the Hihime who appears here and Sumiyoshi's younger sister, Hinohime, are the same person, and that there may be some confusion in the legends. The above description needs to be considered in conjunction with historical facts uncovered by archaeology, which show that the chiefs who became the ancestors of the Izumo no Omi clan in the first half of the 5th century were deeply involved with the Yamato government and engaged in negotiations with the Korean Peninsula. Furthermore, it is necessary to look at the connections with the {{ill|10=ja|11=淡路島|Awaji Island|qq=draft|qq=draft}} fishermen group and the relationship with the {{ill|Nomi no Sukune|en}} legend. == Research == A group of fishermen from Awaji Island appears frequently in the aforementioned story; sailors from this group were active when Ousukune went to retrieve the Akoko basket from Korea; and in the legend of Prince Sumiyoshi Nakatsu, "fishermen from Nojima on Awaji" are secretly active, led by {{ill|10=ja|11=阿曇浜子|Azumi no Muraji Hamako|qq=draft|qq=draft}}. Many artifacts indicating connections to the peninsula and Izumo have been excavated from the Kidohara and Uryu ruins on Awaji Island. Jasper rough stones from {{ill|10=ja|11=玉湯町|Kasenyama|qq=draft|qq=draft}} in Tamayu-cho, [[Matsue|Matsue City]] have been excavated from jade-making sites in the Kinai region, such as the Soga Site, Furu {{ill|10=ja|11=布留遺跡|Site|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, and Nagahara Site. In particular, jade-making sites using Izumo-style stone materials such as jasper and quartz have been found at the Tani Site near Ise, the base of the Yamato no Agoko clan. Outside the Nara Basin, small amounts of remains have been excavated from the Nagahara ruins in Kawachi Province. In addition to Yayoi period ruins, the remains of a jade-making workshop thought to date from the end of the 4th century to the beginning of the 5th century have been discovered along the coasts of Lake Shinji and Lake Nakaumi, and whetstones made from crystalline schist mined in the {{ill|10=ja|11=紀の川|Yoshino River|lt=Yoshino River|en|qq=draft|qq=draft}} and {{ill|10=ja|11=紀の川|Kinokawa_River|lt=Kino River|en|qq=draft|qq=draft}} basins in Nara Prefecture were used. {{ill|Ichishi no Nagaochi|fr}}, an ancestor of Yamato no Agoko, appears in the legends of {{ill|Amenohiboko|en|qq=draft|qq=draft}} and is also said to have gone to Izumo to welcome Nomi no Sukune. Nomi no Sukune was famous for his {{ill|10=ja|11=当麻蹴速|sumo|qq=draft|qq=draft}} match with Tagima no Kehaya, and according to Kikuchi Teruo, this story is the origin of the rice farming ritual in which the spirits of the earth are calmed by sumo. This suggests that there was evidence of a connection with the San'in region around the "Tagima Path" from the time of Nomi no Sukune.
