Aston.djvu/208|url=https://en.wikisource.org/wiki/Page:Nihongi_by_Aston.djvu/208|access-date=2023-10-24|website=en.wikisource.org|language=en}} == Historical record == By the way, in the twelfth volume of the "Nihon Shoki," [[:en:Emperor Richū|Emperor Richu]] floats a two-pronged boat on Iware City Isoike Pond. 『日本書紀』履中天皇3rd year 11月6日条 === The Yamato military fields and warehouses === Similarly, Volume 11 of the "Shoki" tells the following story: This is the story of how Agoko remade a giant tree that had washed up on the Oi River into a boat. At this time, Agoko was called "Yamato no Agoko." The Crown Prince, who was filled with suspicion, became suspicious of Agogo's true intentions and tried to kill him. So Agoko felt humbled and offered his younger sister, Hinohime, as a tribute, and was spared the death penalty. From this time on, Yamato no Agoko began to offer court ladies as tribute. 『日本書紀』履中天皇即位前紀条 According to Volume 12 of the "Shoki," Prince Sumiyoshi Nakatsu and Yamato Naokogo were on close terms. Therefore, when Prince Naka rebelled against the Crown Prince, Prince Izahowake (later Emperor Richu), presumably in the year 399, he tried to side with Prince Naka and gathered several hundred elite soldiers at a place called "Kakihami no Kurusu" (said to be Kurusu-go, {{ill|10=ja|11=忍海郡|Oshikai county|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/10=ja|qq=}} ) and waited for the Crown Prince. However, when he realized that the Crown Prince's troops were more numerous than he had expected, he changed his attitude. === Driftwood of the Oi River === Another part of the Richū Sokui Chronicle states that the Crown Prince, on his way to {{ill|Isonokami Jingu|lt=Isonokami Jingu|lt=Isonokami Shrine|en|Isonokami Jingu|lt=Isonokami Jingu|lt=Isonokami Shrine|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Isonokami Shrine|qq=}}, encounters a young girl at the foot of Mt. Asuka and asks her about the safety of the journey.{{Quote frame|In the summer of May of the 62nd year (estimated to be 374 AD), the governor of Tōtōmi Province reported, "There is a large tree that flowed from the {{ill|Ōi River|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ōi River|qq=}}, bending and stopping at the river's curve. Its size is around ten tōdaki (approximately 300 meters). Initially singular, it splits into two at the ends." At that time, Yamato no Ataī Agoko was dispatched to construct a ship from it. Thus, navigating from the Southern Sea, it arrived at Naniwa Port, where it was dedicated as a royal ship.『日本書紀』仁徳天皇62nd year 5月条|qq=draft}}This episode is about a massive log that had drifted to the Ōigawa River, which Agoko then remade into a ship. At this time, Agoko was referred to as "Yamato no Atai." Incidentally, in Volume 12 of the "Nihon Shoki," it is mentioned that Emperor Nintoku floated a bifurcated boat (a boat split into two parts) in the Iware Market Isopond. === Prince Sumiyoshi's Rebellion === The fourteenth volume of the "Shoki" tells the story of Emperor Yuryaku, who, in a fit of rage after a hunt at Mimase, killed Otsu no Umakai with the sword, and his mother, Empress {{ill|Oshisaka no Ōnakatsuhime|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Oshisaka no Ōnakatsuhime|qq=}}, presenting the Wa court lady "Hinohime" to settle the matter. This conversation led to the establishment of the {{ill|10=ja|11=宍人部|Shishihitobe|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/10=ja|qq=}} (the branch of the Shishihito clan), and the appointment of three members, including Kashiwadeno no Omi Nagano. In addition, the “Oyamato no Kuni no Miyatsuko Agoko no Sukune” presented Sahonoko Toriwake to the Shishihitobe, and “the Ministers of the Imperial Court, Tomo no Miyatsuko and Kuni no Miyatsuko, followed suit and continued to offer tribute.” 『日本書紀』雄略天皇2nd year 10月6日条{{Quote frame|"I hear through the grapevine that an extraordinary event has occurred to the Crown Prince. Preparing soldiers, we stand ready to offer assistance."}}As a character in the " [[Nihon Shoki]] ," he appears in relatively many places. Volume 11 of the Nihon Shoki records a dispute over the Yamato military fields and warehouses between {{ill|10=ja|11=額田大中彦皇子|Prince Nukata no Onakahiko|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/10=ja|qq=}} and the [[:en:Tuntian|military farm]] administrator, {{ill|10=ja|11=淤宇宿禰|Ounosukune|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/10=ja|qq=}}, which took place after the death of the Emperor in what is [[:en:Emperor Ōjin|believed]] to be 310 (the 41st year of the reign of Emperor Ojin) and {{ill|10=ja|11=屯倉|the Imperial Throne|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/10=ja|qq=}} was in a state of uncertainty. When Prince Nukata no Oonakahiko unilaterally confiscated his land, Ousukune appealed to Uji no Wakairoko and then to Osazaki no Mikoto (later [[:en:Emperor Nintoku|Emperor Nintoku]] ), and it was discovered that Agoko, who was currently stationed in Karakuni, knew about the Wa military fields and military storehouses. Following the advice of Ootori-no-Mikoto, Ousukune traveled day and night to Korea with Awaji fishermen and returned with the child's basket. Akogo testified that the "[[:en:Tuntian|military farms]] (屯田) and {{ill|military granary|lt=granaries|ja|屯倉|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/military granary|qq=}} (屯倉) of Wa" were passed down to Emperor Keikō, who was [[:en:Emperor Keikō|the crown prince]] during the reign of [[:en:Emperor Suinin|Emperor Suinin]], saying, "Generally, the [[:en:Tuntian|military farms]] (屯田) of Yamato are the military farms (屯田) of the current emperor. Even if one is the son of the emperor, he cannot be in charge unless he is the emperor's son," and that they were under the control of the emperor of the time. This caused Prince Nukata-Onakahiko to reflect on his actions, and the land management issue was resolved in Ousukune's favor. The [[Kojiki]] makes no mention of such circumstances. === Presentation from the Shishitobe === It is said that the Hihime who appears here and Sumiyoshi's younger sister, Hinohime, are the same person, and that there may be some confusion in the legends. The above description needs to be considered in conjunction with historical facts uncovered by archaeology, which show that the chiefs who became the ancestors of the Izumo no Omi clan in the first half of the 5th century were deeply involved with the Yamato government and engaged in negotiations with the Korean Peninsula. Furthermore, it is necessary to look at the connections with the [[:en:Awaji Island|Awaji Island]] fishermen group and the relationship with the {{ill|Nomi no Sukune|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Nomi no Sukune|qq=}} legend. == Research == A group of fishermen from Awaji Island appears frequently in the aforementioned story; sailors from this group were active when Ousukune went to retrieve the Akoko basket from Korea; and in the legend of Prince Sumiyoshi Nakatsu, "fishermen from Nojima on Awaji" are secretly active, led by {{ill|10=ja|11=阿曇浜子|Azumi no Muraji Hamako|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/10=ja|qq=}}. Many artifacts indicating connections to the peninsula and Izumo have been excavated from the Kidohara and Uryu ruins on Awaji Island. Jasper rough stones from [[:en:Tamayu, Shimane|Kasenyama]] in Tamayu-cho, [[:en:Matsue|Matsue City]] have been excavated from jade-making sites in the Kinai region, such as the Soga Site, Furu {{ill|10=ja|11=布留遺跡|Site|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/10=ja|qq=}}, and Nagahara Site. In particular, jade-making sites using Izumo-style stone materials such as jasper and quartz have been found at the Tani Site near Ise, the base of the Yamato no Agoko clan. Outside the Nara Basin, small amounts of remains have been excavated from the Nagahara ruins in Kawachi Province. In addition to Yayoi period ruins, the remains of a jade-making workshop thought to date from the end of the 4th century to the beginning of the 5th century have been discovered along the coasts of Lake Shinji and Lake Nakaumi, and whetstones made from crystalline schist mined in the [[:en:Kinokawa River|Yoshino River]] and [[:en:Kinokawa River|Kino River]] basins in Nara Prefecture were used. {{ill|Ichishi no Nagaochi|fr|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ichishi no Nagaochi|qq=}}, an ancestor of Yamato no Agoko, appears in the legends of {{ill|Amenohiboko|en|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Amenohiboko|qq=}} and is also said to have gone to Izumo to welcome Nomi no Sukune. Nomi no Sukune was famous for his {{ill|10=ja|11=当麻蹴速|sumo|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/10=ja|qq=}} match with Tagima no Kehaya, and according to Kikuchi Teruo, this story is the origin of the rice farming ritual in which the spirits of the earth are calmed by sumo. In this story, the land of Tagima that Nomi no Sukune acquired was located at the point where the Nara Basin emerges from [[:en:Osaka Bay|Osaka]] Bay via {{ill|Takeuchi Pass|ja|竹内峠|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Takeuchi Pass|qq=}}, where Sugawara Shrine is located, and it was a strategic transportation hub that also leads to {{ill|10=ja|11=葛城|Katsuragi|4=en|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/10=ja|qq=}} to the south. The nearby Ota ruins are the remains of a settlement from the early Kofun period, and pottery from the {{ill|San'in region|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/San'in region|qq=}} estimated to date to the first half of the 4th century has also been excavated. This suggests that there was evidence of a connection with the San'in region around the "Tagima Path" from the time of Nomi no Sukune. As described above, the relationship between the [[Yamato no Kuni no Miyatsuko|Yamato clan]] troops, the Izumo forces, and the fishermen of Awaji Island in the Agokoro legend conveys some historical fact, and it is highly likely that these were condensed and linked together in one person called Yamato no Agoko. == Family tree == Many clans may be descendants of Furutama no Mikoto. This includes the [[:en:Owari clan|Owari clan]] and [[Yamato no Kuni no Miyatsuko]]. This is a subject of debate.{{Cite web|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160422190938/http://wwr2.ucom.ne.jp/hetoyc15/keihu/amabe/amabe-k2.htm|access-date=2023-12-13|website=web.archive.org}} [[fr:Yamato no Agoko]][[ja:倭吾子籠]] {{Infobox person|gender={{ill|male|WD=Q6581097}}|father={{ill|Naruko no Sukune|WD=Q134850160}}}}{{afc comment|Wikidata entry [[d:Q55406552]] Wikidata name: Yamato no Agoko [[User:Immanuelle|Immanuelle]] ([[User talk:Immanuelle|talk]]) 10:26, 11 June 2025 (UTC)}} {{infobox deity|氏名=倭吾子籠|image=|imageサイズ=|image説明=|時代=[[古墳時代]]|生誕=不明|死没=不明|改名=|alternative names=|諡号=|神号=|戒名=|墓所=|官位=|主君=[[仁徳天皇]]、[[履中天皇]]、[[:en:Emperor Yūryaku|Emperor Yūryaku]]|氏族=[[倭氏|倭直]]（[[倭国造]]）|父母=|兄弟=|妻=|子=|特記事項=|image=Ohyamato-jinja Haiden.jpg|image caption=Oyamato Shrine, the main shrine of the {{ill|clan Yamato|en|Yamato no Kuni no Miyatsuko|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/clan Yamato|qq=}}|caption=[[Ōyamato Shrine]], the main shrine of the [[Yamato no Kuni no Miyatsuko]]|province of origin=[[:en:Yamato Province|Yamato Province]]|home province=[[:en:Yamato Province|Yamato Province]]|founder={{ill|Saonetsuhiko|ja|椎根津彦|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Saonetsuhiko|qq=}},
{{ill|Ichishi no Nagaochi|ja|市磯長尾市|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ichishi no Nagaochi|qq=}}|father='''{{ill|Naruko no Sukune|ja|鳴子宿祢|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Naruko no Sukune|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}'''|siblings={{ill|Maro no Sukune|ja|麻呂宿祢|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Maro no Sukune|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}, {{ill|Hinohime|ja|日之媛|complete=true|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Hinohime|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}}} '''Yamato''' no Agoko (years of birth and death unknown) was a {{ill|Gōzoku|lt=powerful|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Gōzoku|qq=}} clan leader of ancient Japan mentioned in the " [[Nihon Shoki]] " and other sources. Ancestor of [[Yamato no Kuni no Miyatsuko|the Yamato]] no Kuni no Miyatsuko. There is no mention of him in the [[Kojiki]] . He served under [[:en:Emperor Nintoku|Emperor Nintoku]] , [[:en:Emperor Richū|Emperor Richu]] , and [[:en:Emperor Yūryaku|Emperor Yuryaku]] == Origin == {{Short description|Japanese noble family}} Yamato no Agoko came from the [[Yamato no Kuni no Miyatsuko|Yamato no Atai clan]]. Their [[Ujigami]] or clan god is [[:en:Yamato Okunitama|Yamato Okunitama]] of [[Ōyamato Shrine]]{{Cite web|title=International Symposium "Perspectives on Japanese history and literature from ancient historical records"|url=https://www.waseda.jp/inst/sgu/news-en/2019/04/12/5171|access-date=2023-05-04|website=Top Global University Project: Waseda Goes Global|language=en}} Some scholars interpret the ''kami'' as being a variant or epithet of [[Ōmononushi]] who has much more widespread worship.{{Cite journal|last=Ellwood|first=Robert S.|date=1990|title=The Sujin Religious Revolution|journal=Japanese Journal of Religious Studies|volume=17|issue=2/3|pages=199–217|doi=10.18874/jjrs.17.2-3.1990.199-217|issn=0304-1042|jstor=30234018|doi-access=free}}{{Cite book|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=_Q81DQAAQBAJ|title=Shinto: A History|last=Hardacre|first=Helen|date=2017|publisher=Oxford University Press|isbn=978-0-19-062171-1|language=en}}{{rp|22}} There is a complex myth about the origins of modern worship of [[:en:Yamato Okunitama|Yamato Okunitama]] during the reign of [[:en:Emperor Sujin|Emperor Sujin]].{{Cite web|last=D|first=John|date=2012-11-10|title=Teeuwen on Shinto|url=https://www.greenshinto.com/2012/11/10/teeuwen-on-shinto/|access-date=2023-05-04|website=Green Shinto|language=en-GB}}https://www.japanpolicyforum.jp/pdf/2016/no35/DJweb_35_cul_02.pdfhttps://freidok.uni-freiburg.de/fedora/objects/freidok:4635/datastreams/FILE1/content{{Citation|title=Book V|url=https://en.wikisource.org/wiki/Nihongi:_Chronicles_of_Japan_from_the_Earliest_Times_to_A.D._697/Book_V|work=Nihongi: Chronicles of Japan from the Earliest Times to A.D. 697, Volume 1|access-date=2023-05-04}} [[File:Hibara-jinja,_torii_closeup.jpg|thumb|240x240px|Hibara Shrine, at the foot of [[:en:Mount Miwa|Mount Miwa]] in [[:en:Sakurai, Nara|Sakurai, Nara]], identified as the place where the Yata-no-Kagami and the Kusanagi-no-Tsurugi were first enshrined after their removal from the imperial palace.]] During {{ill|Jimmu%27s Eastern Expedition|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Jimmu%27s Eastern Expedition|qq=}} {{ill|Saonetsuhiko|ja|椎根津彦|fr|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Saonetsuhiko|qq=}} was given the position of governor of [[:en:Yamato Province|Yamato Province]] by [[:en:Emperor Jimmu|Emperor Jimmu]].{{Cite web|title=Friday: Kojiki (「乞食」ではなく『古事記』ですヨ！！) #26|url=https://japaneseexperts.net/972/|access-date=2023-05-04|website=Japanese Experts Net|language=en-US}} And Saonetsuhiko became their ancestor.{{Cite web|date=2023-10-26|title=Saonetsuhiko {{!}} 國學院大學デジタルミュージアム|url=https://d-museum.kokugakuin.ac.jp/eos/detail/id=9159|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20231026183115/https://d-museum.kokugakuin.ac.jp/eos/detail/id=9159|archive-date=2023-10-26|access-date=2023-12-04}} After the divination, {{ill|Ichishi no Nagaochi|ja|市磯長尾市|fr|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ichishi no Nagaochi|qq=}}, a descendant of {{ill|Saonetsuhiko|ja|椎根津彦|fr|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Saonetsuhiko|qq=}} would conduct the rites pertaining to Okunitama, replacing the emaciated Nunaki-iri-hime. {{ill|Ichishi no Nagaochi|ja|市磯長尾市|fr|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ichishi no Nagaochi|qq=}} would be the ancestor of the Yamato no Kuni no Miyatsuko.{{Cite web|title=Page:Nihongi by Aston.djvu/208|url=https://en.wikisource.org/wiki/Page:Nihongi_by_Aston.djvu/208|access-date=2023-10-24|website=en.wikisource.org|language=en}} == Historical record == By the way, in the twelfth volume of the "Nihon Shoki," [[:en:Emperor Richū|Emperor Richu]] floats a two-pronged boat on Iware City Isoike Pond. 『日本書紀』履中天皇3rd year 11月6日条 === The Yamato military fields and warehouses === Similarly, Volume 11 of the "Shoki" tells the following story: This is the story of how Agoko remade a giant tree that had washed up on the Oi River into a boat. At this time, Agoko was called "Yamato no Agoko." The Crown Prince, who was filled with suspicion, became suspicious of Agogo's true intentions and tried to kill him. So Agoko felt humbled and offered his younger sister, Hinohime, as a tribute, and was spared the death penalty. From this time on, Yamato no Agoko began to offer court ladies as tribute. 『日本書紀』履中天皇即位前紀条 According to Volume 12 of the "Shoki," Prince Sumiyoshi Nakatsu and Yamato Naokogo were on close terms. Therefore, when Prince Naka rebelled against the Crown Prince, Prince Izahowake (later Emperor Richu), presumably in the year 399, he tried to side with Prince Naka and gathered several hundred elite soldiers at a place called "Kakihami no Kurusu" (said to be Kurusu-go, {{ill|10=ja|11=忍海郡|Oshikai county|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/10=ja|qq=}} ) and waited for the Crown Prince. However, when he realized that the Crown Prince's troops were more numerous than he had expected, he changed his attitude. === Driftwood of the Oi River === Another part of the Richū Sokui Chronicle states that the Crown Prince, on his way to {{ill|Isonokami Jingu|lt=Isonokami Jingu|lt=Isonokami Shrine|en|Isonokami Jingu|lt=Isonokami Jingu|lt=Isonokami Shrine|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Isonokami Shrine|qq=}}, encounters a young girl at the foot of Mt. Asuka and asks her about the safety of the journey.{{Quote frame|In the summer of May of the 62nd year (estimated to be 374 AD), the governor of Tōtōmi Province reported, "There is a large tree that flowed from the {{ill|Ōi River|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ōi River|qq=}}, bending and stopping at the river's curve. Its size is around ten tōdaki (approximately 300 meters). Initially singular, it splits into two at the ends." At that time, Yamato no Ataī Agoko was dispatched to construct a ship from it. Thus, navigating from the Southern Sea, it arrived at Naniwa Port, where it was dedicated as a royal ship.『日本書紀』仁徳天皇62nd year 5月条|qq=draft}}This episode is about a massive log that had drifted to the Ōigawa River, which Agoko then remade into a ship. At this time, Agoko was referred to as "Yamato no Atai." Incidentally, in Volume 12 of the "Nihon Shoki," it is mentioned that Emperor Nintoku floated a bifurcated boat (a boat split into two parts) in the Iware Market Isopond. === Prince Sumiyoshi's Rebellion === The fourteenth volume of the "Shoki" tells the story of Emperor Yuryaku, who, in a fit of rage after a hunt at Mimase, killed Otsu no Umakai with the sword, and his mother, Empress {{ill|Oshisaka no Ōnakatsuhime|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Oshisaka no Ōnakatsuhime|qq=}}, presenting the Wa court lady "Hinohime" to settle the matter. This conversation led to the establishment of the {{ill|10=ja|11=宍人部|Shishihitobe|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/10=ja|qq=}} (the branch of the Shishihito clan), and the appointment of three members, including Kashiwadeno no Omi Nagano. In addition, the “Oyamato no Kuni no Miyatsuko Agoko no Sukune” presented Sahonoko Toriwake to the Shishihitobe, and “the Ministers of the Imperial Court, Tomo no Miyatsuko and Kuni no Miyatsuko, followed suit and continued to offer tribute.” 『日本書紀』雄略天皇2nd year 10月6日条{{Quote frame|"I hear through the grapevine that an extraordinary event has occurred to the Crown Prince. Preparing soldiers, we stand ready to offer assistance."}}As a character in the " [[Nihon Shoki]] ," he appears in relatively many places. Volume 11 of the Nihon Shoki records a dispute over the Yamato military fields and warehouses between {{ill|10=ja|11=額田大中彦皇子|Prince Nukata no Onakahiko|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/10=ja|qq=}} and the [[:en:Tuntian|military farm]] administrator, {{ill|10=ja|11=淤宇宿禰|Ounosukune|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/10=ja|qq=}}, which took place after the death of the Emperor in what is [[:en:Emperor Ōjin|believed]] to be 310 (the 41st year of the reign of Emperor Ojin) and {{ill|10=ja|11=屯倉|the Imperial Throne|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/10=ja|qq=}} was in a state of uncertainty. When Prince Nukata no Oonakahiko unilaterally confiscated his land, Ousukune appealed to Uji no Wakairoko and then to Osazaki no Mikoto (later [[:en:Emperor Nintoku|Emperor Nintoku]] ), and it was discovered that Agoko, who was currently stationed in Karakuni, knew about the Wa military fields and military storehouses. Following the advice of Ootori-no-Mikoto, Ousukune traveled day and night to Korea with Awaji fishermen and returned with the child's basket. Akogo testified that the "[[:en:Tuntian|military farms]] (屯田) and {{ill|military granary|lt=granaries|ja|屯倉|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/military granary|qq=}} (屯倉) of Wa" were passed down to Emperor Keikō, who was [[:en:Emperor Keikō|the crown prince]] during the reign of [[:en:Emperor Suinin|Emperor Suinin]], saying, "Generally, the [[:en:Tuntian|military farms]] (屯田) of Yamato are the military farms (屯田) of the current emperor. Even if one is the son of the emperor, he cannot be in charge unless he is the emperor's son," and that they were under the control of the emperor of the time. This caused Prince Nukata-Onakahiko to reflect on his actions, and the land management issue was resolved in Ousukune's favor. The [[Kojiki]] makes no mention of such circumstances. === Presentation from the Shishitobe === It is said that the Hihime who appears here and Sumiyoshi's younger sister, Hinohime, are the same person, and that there may be some confusion in the legends. The above description needs to be considered in conjunction with historical facts uncovered by archaeology, which show that the chiefs who became the ancestors of the Izumo no Omi clan in the first half of the 5th century were deeply involved with the Yamato government and engaged in negotiations with the Korean Peninsula. Furthermore, it is necessary to look at the connections with the [[:en:Awaji Island|Awaji Island]] fishermen group and the relationship with the {{ill|Nomi no Sukune|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Nomi no Sukune|qq=}} legend. == Research == A group of fishermen from Awaji Island appears frequently in the aforementioned story; sailors from this group were active when Ousukune went to retrieve the Akoko basket from Korea; and in the legend of Prince Sumiyoshi Nakatsu, "fishermen from Nojima on Awaji" are secretly active, led by {{ill|10=ja|11=阿曇浜子|Azumi no Muraji Hamako|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/10=ja|qq=}}. Many artifacts indicating connections to the peninsula and Izumo have been excavated from the Kidohara and Uryu ruins on Awaji Island. Jasper rough stones from [[:en:Tamayu, Shimane|Kasenyama]] in Tamayu-cho, [[:en:Matsue|Matsue City]] have been excavated from jade-making sites in the Kinai region, such as the Soga Site, Furu {{ill|10=ja|11=布留遺跡|Site|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/10=ja|qq=}}, and Nagahara Site. In particular, jade-making sites using Izumo-style stone materials such as jasper and quartz have been found at the Tani Site near Ise, the base of the Yamato no Agoko clan. Outside the Nara Basin, small amounts of remains have been excavated from the Nagahara ruins in Kawachi Province. In addition to Yayoi period ruins, the remains of a jade-making workshop thought to date from the end of the 4th century to the beginning of the 5th century have been discovered along the coasts of Lake Shinji and Lake Nakaumi, and whetstones made from crystalline schist mined in the [[:en:Kinokawa River|Yoshino River]] and [[:en:Kinokawa River|Kino River]] basins in Nara Prefecture were used. {{ill|Ichishi no Nagaochi|fr|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ichishi no Nagaochi|qq=}}, an ancestor of Yamato no Agoko, appears in the legends of {{ill|Amenohiboko|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Amenohiboko|qq=}} and is also said to have gone to Izumo to welcome Nomi no Sukune. Nomi no Sukune was famous for his {{ill|10=ja|11=当麻蹴速|sumo|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/10=ja|qq=}} match with Tagima no Kehaya, and according to Kikuchi Teruo, this story is the origin of the rice farming ritual in which the spirits of the earth are calmed by sumo. In this story, the land of Tagima that Nomi no Sukune acquired was located at the point where the Nara Basin emerges from [[:en:Osaka Bay|Osaka]] Bay via {{ill|Takeuchi Pass|ja|竹内峠|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Takeuchi Pass|qq=}}, where Sugawara Shrine is located, and it was a strategic transportation hub that also leads to {{ill|10=ja|11=葛城|Katsuragi|4=en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/10=ja|qq=}} to the south. The nearby Ota ruins are the remains of a settlement from the early Kofun period, and pottery from the {{ill|San'in region|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/San'in region|qq=}} estimated to date to the first half of the 4th century has also been excavated. This suggests that there was evidence of a connection with the San'in region around the "Tagima Path" from the time of Nomi no Sukune. As described above, the relationship between the [[Yamato no Kuni no Miyatsuko|Yamato clan]] troops, the Izumo forces, and the fishermen of Awaji Island in the Agokoro legend conveys some historical fact, and it is highly likely that these were condensed and linked together in one person called Yamato no Agoko. == Family tree == Many clans may be descendants of Furutama no Mikoto. This includes the [[:en:Owari clan|Owari clan]] and [[Yamato no Kuni no Miyatsuko]]. This is a subject of debate.{{Cite web|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160422190938/http://wwr2.ucom.ne.jp/hetoyc15/keihu/amabe/amabe-k2.htm|access-date=2023-12-13|website=web.archive.org}} {{ill|Ichishi no Nagaochi|ja|市磯長尾市|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ichishi no Nagaochi|qq=}}|father='''{{ill|Naruko no Sukune|ja|鳴子宿祢|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Naruko no Sukune|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}'''|siblings={{ill|Maro no Sukune|ja|麻呂宿祢|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Maro no Sukune|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}, {{ill|Hinohime|ja|日之媛|complete=true|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Hinohime|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}}} '''Yamato''' no Agoko (years of birth and death unknown) was a {{ill|Gōzoku|lt=powerful|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Gōzoku|qq=}} clan leader of ancient Japan mentioned in the " [[Nihon Shoki]] " and other sources. Ancestor of [[Yamato no Kuni no Miyatsuko|the Yamato]] no Kuni no Miyatsuko. There is no mention of him in the [[Kojiki]] . He served under [[:en:Emperor Nintoku|Emperor Nintoku]] , [[:en:Emperor Richū|Emperor Richu]] , and [[:en:Emperor Yūryaku|Emperor Yuryaku]] == Origin == {{Short description|Japanese noble family}} Yamato no Agoko came from the [[Yamato no Kuni no Miyatsuko|Yamato no Atai clan]]. Their [[Ujigami]] or clan god is [[:en:Yamato Okunitama|Yamato Okunitama]] of [[Ōyamato Shrine]]{{Cite web|title=International Symposium "Perspectives on Japanese history and literature from ancient historical records"|url=https://www.waseda.jp/inst/sgu/news-en/2019/04/12/5171|access-date=2023-05-04|website=Top Global University Project: Waseda Goes Global|language=en}} Some scholars interpret the ''kami'' as being a variant or epithet of [[Ōmononushi]] who has much more widespread worship.{{Cite journal|last=Ellwood|first=Robert S.|date=1990|title=The Sujin Religious Revolution|journal=Japanese Journal of Religious Studies|volume=17|issue=2/3|pages=199–217|doi=10.18874/jjrs.17.2-3.1990.199-217|issn=0304-1042|jstor=30234018|doi-access=free}}{{Cite book|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=_Q81DQAAQBAJ|title=Shinto: A History|last=Hardacre|first=Helen|date=2017|publisher=Oxford University Press|isbn=978-0-19-062171-1|language=en}}{{rp|22}} There is a complex myth about the origins of modern worship of [[:en:Yamato Okunitama|Yamato Okunitama]] during the reign of [[:en:Emperor Sujin|Emperor Sujin]].{{Cite web|last=D|first=John|date=2012-11-10|title=Teeuwen on Shinto|url=https://www.greenshinto.com/2012/11/10/teeuwen-on-shinto/|access-date=2023-05-04|website=Green Shinto|language=en-GB}}https://www.japanpolicyforum.jp/pdf/2016/no35/DJweb_35_cul_02.pdfhttps://freidok.uni-freiburg.de/fedora/objects/freidok:4635/datastreams/FILE1/content{{Citation|title=Book V|url=https://en.wikisource.org/wiki/Nihongi:_Chronicles_of_Japan_from_the_Earliest_Times_to_A.D._697/Book_V|work=Nihongi: Chronicles of Japan from the Earliest Times to A.D. 697, Volume 1|access-date=2023-05-04}} [[File:Hibara-jinja,_torii_closeup.jpg|thumb|240x240px|Hibara Shrine, at the foot of [[:en:Mount Miwa|Mount Miwa]] in [[:en:Sakurai, Nara|Sakurai, Nara]], identified as the place where the Yata-no-Kagami and the Kusanagi-no-Tsurugi were first enshrined after their removal from the imperial palace.]] During {{ill|Jimmu%27s Eastern Expedition|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Jimmu%27s Eastern Expedition|qq=}} {{ill|Saonetsuhiko|ja|椎根津彦|fr|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Saonetsuhiko|qq=}} was given the position of governor of [[:en:Yamato Province|Yamato Province]] by [[:en:Emperor Jimmu|Emperor Jimmu]].{{Cite web|title=Friday: Kojiki (「乞食」ではなく『古事記』ですヨ！！) #26|url=https://japaneseexperts.net/972/|access-date=2023-05-04|website=Japanese Experts Net|language=en-US}} And Saonetsuhiko became their ancestor.{{Cite web|date=2023-10-26|title=Saonetsuhiko {{!}} 國學院大學デジタルミュージアム|url=https://d-museum.kokugakuin.ac.jp/eos/detail/id=9159|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20231026183115/https://d-museum.kokugakuin.ac.jp/eos/detail/id=9159|archive-date=2023-10-26|access-date=2023-12-04}} After the divination, {{ill|Ichishi no Nagaochi|ja|市磯長尾市|fr|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ichishi no Nagaochi|qq=}}, a descendant of {{ill|Saonetsuhiko|ja|椎根津彦|fr|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Saonetsuhiko|qq=}} would conduct the rites pertaining to Okunitama, replacing the emaciated Nunaki-iri-hime. {{ill|Ichishi no Nagaochi|ja|市磯長尾市|fr|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ichishi no Nagaochi|qq=}} would be the ancestor of the Yamato no Kuni no Miyatsuko.{{Cite web|title=Page:Nihongi by Aston.djvu/208|url=https://en.wikisource.org/wiki/Page:Nihongi_by_Aston.djvu/208|access-date=2023-10-24|website=en.wikisource.org|language=en}} == Historical record == By the way, in the twelfth volume of the "Nihon Shoki," [[:en:Emperor Richū|Emperor Richu]] floats a two-pronged boat on Iware City Isoike Pond. 『日本書紀』履中天皇3rd year 11月6日条 === The Yamato military fields and warehouses === Similarly, Volume 11 of the "Shoki" tells the following story: This is the story of how Agoko remade a giant tree that had washed up on the Oi River into a boat. At this time, Agoko was called "Yamato no Agoko." The Crown Prince, who was filled with suspicion, became suspicious of Agogo's true intentions and tried to kill him. So Agoko felt humbled and offered his younger sister, Hinohime, as a tribute, and was spared the death penalty. From this time on, Yamato no Agoko began to offer court ladies as tribute. 『日本書紀』履中天皇即位前紀条 According to Volume 12 of the "Shoki," Prince Sumiyoshi Nakatsu and Yamato Naokogo were on close terms. Therefore, when Prince Naka rebelled against the Crown Prince, Prince Izahowake (later Emperor Richu), presumably in the year 399, he tried to side with Prince Naka and gathered several hundred elite soldiers at a place called "Kakihami no Kurusu" (said to be Kurusu-go, {{ill|10=ja|11=忍海郡|Oshikai county|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/10=ja|qq=}} ) and waited for the Crown Prince. However, when he realized that the Crown Prince's troops were more numerous than he had expected, he changed his attitude. === Driftwood of the Oi River === Another part of the Richū Sokui Chronicle states that the Crown Prince, on his way to {{ill|Isonokami Jingu|lt=Isonokami Jingu|lt=Isonokami Shrine|en|Isonokami Jingu|lt=Isonokami Jingu|lt=Isonokami Shrine|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Isonokami Shrine|qq=}}, encounters a young girl at the foot of Mt. Asuka and asks her about the safety of the journey.{{Quote frame|In the summer of May of the 62nd year (estimated to be 374 AD), the governor of Tōtōmi Province reported, "There is a large tree that flowed from the {{ill|Ōi River|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ōi River|qq=}}, bending and stopping at the river's curve. Its size is around ten tōdaki (approximately 300 meters). Initially singular, it splits into two at the ends." At that time, Yamato no Ataī Agoko was dispatched to construct a ship from it. Thus, navigating from the Southern Sea, it arrived at Naniwa Port, where it was dedicated as a royal ship.『日本書紀』仁徳天皇62nd year 5月条|qq=draft}}This episode is about a massive log that had drifted to the Ōigawa River, which Agoko then remade into a ship. At this time, Agoko was referred to as "Yamato no Atai." Incidentally, in Volume 12 of the "Nihon Shoki," it is mentioned that Emperor Nintoku floated a bifurcated boat (a boat split into two parts) in the Iware Market Isopond. === Prince Sumiyoshi's Rebellion === The fourteenth volume of the "Shoki" tells the story of Emperor Yuryaku, who, in a fit of rage after a hunt at Mimase, killed Otsu no Umakai with the sword, and his mother, Empress {{ill|Oshisaka no Ōnakatsuhime|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Oshisaka no Ōnakatsuhime|qq=}}, presenting the Wa court lady "Hinohime" to settle the matter. This conversation led to the establishment of the {{ill|10=ja|11=宍人部|Shishihitobe|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/10=ja|qq=}} (the branch of the Shishihito clan), and the appointment of three members, including Kashiwadeno no Omi Nagano. In addition, the “Oyamato no Kuni no Miyatsuko Agoko no Sukune” presented Sahonoko Toriwake to the Shishihitobe, and “the Ministers of the Imperial Court, Tomo no Miyatsuko and Kuni no Miyatsuko, followed suit and continued to offer tribute.” 『日本書紀』雄略天皇2nd year 10月6日条{{Quote frame|"I hear through the grapevine that an extraordinary event has occurred to the Crown Prince. Preparing soldiers, we stand ready to offer assistance."}}As a character in the " [[Nihon Shoki]] ," he appears in relatively many places. Volume 11 of the Nihon Shoki records a dispute over the Yamato military fields and warehouses between {{ill|10=ja|11=額田大中彦皇子|Prince Nukata no Onakahiko|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/10=ja|qq=}} and the [[:en:Tuntian|military farm]] administrator, {{ill|10=ja|11=淤宇宿禰|Ounosukune|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/10=ja|qq=}}, which took place after the death of the Emperor in what is [[:en:Emperor Ōjin|believed]] to be 310 (the 41st year of the reign of Emperor Ojin) and {{ill|10=ja|11=屯倉|the Imperial Throne|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/10=ja|qq=}} was in a state of uncertainty. When Prince Nukata no Oonakahiko unilaterally confiscated his land, Ousukune appealed to Uji no Wakairoko and then to Osazaki no Mikoto (later [[:en:Emperor Nintoku|Emperor Nintoku]] ), and it was discovered that Agoko, who was currently stationed in Karakuni, knew about the Wa military fields and military storehouses. Following the advice of Ootori-no-Mikoto, Ousukune traveled day and night to Korea with Awaji fishermen and returned with the child's basket. Akogo testified that the "[[:en:Tuntian|military farms]] (屯田) and {{ill|military granary|lt=granaries|ja|屯倉|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/military granary|qq=}} (屯倉) of Wa" were passed down to Emperor Keikō, who was [[:en:Emperor Keikō|the crown prince]] during the reign of [[:en:Emperor Suinin|Emperor Suinin]], saying, "Generally, the [[:en:Tuntian|military farms]] (屯田) of Yamato are the military farms (屯田) of the current emperor. Even if one is the son of the emperor, he cannot be in charge unless he is the emperor's son," and that they were under the control of the emperor of the time. This caused Prince Nukata-Onakahiko to reflect on his actions, and the land management issue was resolved in Ousukune's favor. The [[Kojiki]] makes no mention of such circumstances. === Presentation from the Shishitobe === It is said that the Hihime who appears here and Sumiyoshi's younger sister, Hinohime, are the same person, and that there may be some confusion in the legends. The above description needs to be considered in conjunction with historical facts uncovered by archaeology, which show that the chiefs who became the ancestors of the Izumo no Omi clan in the first half of the 5th century were deeply involved with the Yamato government and engaged in negotiations with the Korean Peninsula. Furthermore, it is necessary to look at the connections with the [[:en:Awaji Island|Awaji Island]] fishermen group and the relationship with the {{ill|Nomi no Sukune|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Nomi no Sukune|qq=}} legend. == Research == A group of fishermen from Awaji Island appears frequently in the aforementioned story; sailors from this group were active when Ousukune went to retrieve the Akoko basket from Korea; and in the legend of Prince Sumiyoshi Nakatsu, "fishermen from Nojima on Awaji" are secretly active, led by {{ill|10=ja|11=阿曇浜子|Azumi no Muraji Hamako|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/10=ja|qq=}}. Many artifacts indicating connections to the peninsula and Izumo have been excavated from the Kidohara and Uryu ruins on Awaji Island. Jasper rough stones from [[:en:Tamayu, Shimane|Kasenyama]] in Tamayu-cho, [[:en:Matsue|Matsue City]] have been excavated from jade-making sites in the Kinai region, such as the Soga Site, Furu {{ill|10=ja|11=布留遺跡|Site|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/10=ja|qq=}}, and Nagahara Site. In particular, jade-making sites using Izumo-style stone materials such as jasper and quartz have been found at the Tani Site near Ise, the base of the Yamato no Agoko clan. Outside the Nara Basin, small amounts of remains have been excavated from the Nagahara ruins in Kawachi Province. In addition to Yayoi period ruins, the remains of a jade-making workshop thought to date from the end of the 4th century to the beginning of the 5th century have been discovered along the coasts of Lake Shinji and Lake Nakaumi, and whetstones made from crystalline schist mined in the [[:en:Kinokawa River|Yoshino River]] and [[:en:Kinokawa River|Kino River]] basins in Nara Prefecture were used. {{ill|Ichishi no Nagaochi|fr|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ichishi no Nagaochi|qq=}}, an ancestor of Yamato no Agoko, appears in the legends of {{ill|Amenohiboko|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Amenohiboko|qq=}} and is also said to have gone to Izumo to welcome Nomi no Sukune. Nomi no Sukune was famous for his {{ill|10=ja|11=当麻蹴速|sumo|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/10=ja|qq=}} match with Tagima no Kehaya, and according to Kikuchi Teruo, this story is the origin of the rice farming ritual in which the spirits of the earth are calmed by sumo. In this story, the land of Tagima that Nomi no Sukune acquired was located at the point where the Nara Basin emerges from [[:en:Osaka Bay|Osaka]] Bay via {{ill|Takeuchi Pass|ja|竹内峠|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Takeuchi Pass|qq=}}, where Sugawara Shrine is located, and it was a strategic transportation hub that also leads to {{ill|10=ja|11=葛城|Katsuragi|4=en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/10=ja|qq=}} to the south. The nearby Ota ruins are the remains of a settlement from the early Kofun period, and pottery from the {{ill|San'in region|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/San'in region|qq=}} estimated to date to the first half of the 4th century has also been excavated. This suggests that there was evidence of a connection with the San'in region around the "Tagima Path" from the time of Nomi no Sukune. As described above, the relationship between the [[Yamato no Kuni no Miyatsuko|Yamato clan]] troops, the Izumo forces, and the fishermen of Awaji Island in the Agokoro legend conveys some historical fact, and it is highly likely that these were condensed and linked together in one person called Yamato no Agoko. == Family tree == Many clans may be descendants of Furutama no Mikoto. This includes the [[:en:Owari clan|Owari clan]] and [[Yamato no Kuni no Miyatsuko]]. This is a subject of debate.{{Cite web|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160422190938/http://wwr2.ucom.ne.jp/hetoyc15/keihu/amabe/amabe-k2.htm|access-date=2023-12-13|website=web.archive.org}} {{ill|Ichishi no Nagaochi|ja|市磯長尾市|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ichishi no Nagaochi|qq=}}|father='''{{ill|Naruko no Sukune|ja|鳴子宿祢|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Naruko no Sukune|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}'''|siblings={{ill|Maro no Sukune|ja|麻呂宿祢|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Maro no Sukune|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}, {{ill|Hinohime|ja|日之媛|complete=true|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Hinohime|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}}} '''Yamato''' no Agoko (years of birth and death unknown) was a {{ill|Gōzoku|lt=powerful|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Gōzoku|qq=}} clan leader of ancient Japan mentioned in the " [[Nihon Shoki]] " and other sources. Ancestor of [[Yamato no Kuni no Miyatsuko|the Yamato]] no Kuni no Miyatsuko. There is no mention of him in the [[Kojiki]] . He served under [[:en:Emperor Nintoku|Emperor Nintoku]] , [[:en:Emperor Richū|Emperor Richu]] , and [[:en:Emperor Yūryaku|Emperor Yuryaku]] == Origin == {{Short description|Japanese noble family}} Yamato no Agoko came from the [[Yamato no Kuni no Miyatsuko|Yamato no Atai clan]]. Their [[Ujigami]] or clan god is [[:en:Yamato Okunitama|Yamato Okunitama]] of [[Ōyamato Shrine]]{{Cite web|title=International Symposium "Perspectives on Japanese history and literature from ancient historical records"|url=https://www.waseda.jp/inst/sgu/news-en/2019/04/12/5171|access-date=2023-05-04|website=Top Global University Project: Waseda Goes Global|language=en}} Some scholars interpret the ''kami'' as being a variant or epithet of [[Ōmononushi]] who has much more widespread worship.{{Cite journal|last=Ellwood|first=Robert S.|date=1990|title=The Sujin Religious Revolution|journal=Japanese Journal of Religious Studies|volume=17|issue=2/3|pages=199–217|doi=10.18874/jjrs.17.2-3.1990.199-217|issn=0304-1042|jstor=30234018|doi-access=free}}{{Cite book|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=_Q81DQAAQBAJ|title=Shinto: A History|last=Hardacre|first=Helen|date=2017|publisher=Oxford University Press|isbn=978-0-19-062171-1|language=en}}{{rp|22}} There is a complex myth about the origins of modern worship of [[:en:Yamato Okunitama|Yamato Okunitama]] during the reign of [[:en:Emperor Sujin|Emperor Sujin]].{{Cite web|last=D|first=John|date=2012-11-10|title=Teeuwen on Shinto|url=https://www.greenshinto.com/2012/11/10/teeuwen-on-shinto/|access-date=2023-05-04|website=Green Shinto|language=en-GB}}https://www.japanpolicyforum.jp/pdf/2016/no35/DJweb_35_cul_02.pdfhttps://freidok.uni-freiburg.de/fedora/objects/freidok:4635/datastreams/FILE1/content{{Citation|title=Book V|url=https://en.wikisource.org/wiki/Nihongi:_Chronicles_of_Japan_from_the_Earliest_Times_to_A.D._697/Book_V|work=Nihongi: Chronicles of Japan from the Earliest Times to A.D. 697, Volume 1|access-date=2023-05-04}} [[File:Hibara-jinja,_torii_closeup.jpg|thumb|240x240px|Hibara Shrine, at the foot of [[:en:Mount Miwa|Mount Miwa]] in [[:en:Sakurai, Nara|Sakurai, Nara]], identified as the place where the Yata-no-Kagami and the Kusanagi-no-Tsurugi were first enshrined after their removal from the imperial palace.]] During {{ill|Jimmu%27s Eastern Expedition|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Jimmu%27s Eastern Expedition|qq=}} {{ill|Saonetsuhiko|ja|椎根津彦|fr|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Saonetsuhiko|qq=}} was given the position of governor of [[:en:Yamato Province|Yamato Province]] by [[:en:Emperor Jimmu|Emperor Jimmu]].{{Cite web|title=Friday: Kojiki (「乞食」ではなく『古事記』ですヨ！！) #26|url=https://japaneseexperts.net/972/|access-date=2023-05-04|website=Japanese Experts Net|language=en-US}} And Saonetsuhiko became their ancestor.{{Cite web|date=2023-10-26|title=Saonetsuhiko {{!}} 國學院大學デジタルミュージアム|url=https://d-museum.kokugakuin.ac.jp/eos/detail/id=9159|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20231026183115/https://d-museum.kokugakuin.ac.jp/eos/detail/id=9159|archive-date=2023-10-26|access-date=2023-12-04}} After the divination, {{ill|Ichishi no Nagaochi|ja|市磯長尾市|fr|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ichishi no Nagaochi|qq=}}, a descendant of {{ill|Saonetsuhiko|ja|椎根津彦|fr|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Saonetsuhiko|qq=}} would conduct the rites pertaining to Okunitama, replacing the emaciated Nunaki-iri-hime. {{ill|Ichishi no Nagaochi|ja|市磯長尾市|fr|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ichishi no Nagaochi|qq=}} would be the ancestor of the Yamato no Kuni no Miyatsuko.{{Cite web|title=Page:Nihongi by Aston.djvu/208|url=https://en.wikisource.org/wiki/Page:Nihongi_by_Aston.djvu/208|access-date=2023-10-24|website=en.wikisource.org|language=en}} == Historical record == By the way, in the twelfth volume of the "Nihon Shoki," [[:en:Emperor Richū|Emperor Richu]] floats a two-pronged boat on Iware City Isoike Pond. 『日本書紀』履中天皇3rd year 11月6日条 === The Yamato military fields and warehouses === Similarly, Volume 11 of the "Shoki" tells the following story: This is the story of how Agoko remade a giant tree that had washed up on the Oi River into a boat. At this time, Agoko was called "Yamato no Agoko." The Crown Prince, who was filled with suspicion, became suspicious of Agogo's true intentions and tried to kill him. So Agoko felt humbled and offered his younger sister, Hinohime, as a tribute, and was spared the death penalty. From this time on, Yamato no Agoko began to offer court ladies as tribute. 『日本書紀』履中天皇即位前紀条 According to Volume 12 of the "Shoki," Prince Sumiyoshi Nakatsu and Yamato Naokogo were on close terms. Therefore, when Prince Naka rebelled against the Crown Prince, Prince Izahowake (later Emperor Richu), presumably in the year 399, he tried to side with Prince Naka and gathered several hundred elite soldiers at a place called "Kakihami no Kurusu" (said to be Kurusu-go, {{ill|10=ja|11=忍海郡|Oshikai county|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/10=ja|qq=}} ) and waited for the Crown Prince. However, when he realized that the Crown Prince's troops were more numerous than he had expected, he changed his attitude. === Driftwood of the Oi River === Another part of the Richū Sokui Chronicle states that the Crown Prince, on his way to {{ill|Isonokami Jingu|lt=Isonokami Jingu|lt=Isonokami Shrine|en|Isonokami Jingu|lt=Isonokami Jingu|lt=Isonokami Shrine|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Isonokami Shrine|qq=}}, encounters a young girl at the foot of Mt. Asuka and asks her about the safety of the journey.{{Quote frame|In the summer of May of the 62nd year (estimated to be 374 AD), the governor of Tōtōmi Province reported, "There is a large tree that flowed from the {{ill|Ōi River|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ōi River|qq=}}, bending and stopping at the river's curve. Its size is around ten tōdaki (approximately 300 meters). Initially singular, it splits into two at the ends." At that time, Yamato no Ataī Agoko was dispatched to construct a ship from it. Thus, navigating from the Southern Sea, it arrived at Naniwa Port, where it was dedicated as a royal ship.『日本書紀』仁徳天皇62nd year 5月条|qq=draft}}This episode is about a massive log that had drifted to the Ōigawa River, which Agoko then remade into a ship. At this time, Agoko was referred to as "Yamato no Atai." Incidentally, in Volume 12 of the "Nihon Shoki," it is mentioned that Emperor Nintoku floated a bifurcated boat (a boat split into two parts) in the Iware Market Isopond. === Prince Sumiyoshi's Rebellion === The fourteenth volume of the "Shoki" tells the story of Emperor Yuryaku, who, in a fit of rage after a hunt at Mimase, killed Otsu no Umakai with the sword, and his mother, Empress {{ill|Oshisaka no Ōnakatsuhime|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Oshisaka no Ōnakatsuhime|qq=}}, presenting the Wa court lady "Hinohime" to settle the matter. This conversation led to the establishment of the {{ill|10=ja|11=宍人部|Shishihitobe|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/10=ja|qq=}} (the branch of the Shishihito clan), and the appointment of three members, including Kashiwadeno no Omi Nagano. In addition, the “Oyamato no Kuni no Miyatsuko Agoko no Sukune” presented Sahonoko Toriwake to the Shishihitobe, and “the Ministers of the Imperial Court, Tomo no Miyatsuko and Kuni no Miyatsuko, followed suit and continued to offer tribute.” 『日本書紀』雄略天皇2nd year 10月6日条{{Quote frame|"I hear through the grapevine that an extraordinary event has occurred to the Crown Prince. Preparing soldiers, we stand ready to offer assistance."}}As a character in the " [[Nihon Shoki]] ," he appears in relatively many places. Volume 11 of the Nihon Shoki records a dispute over the Yamato military fields and warehouses between {{ill|10=ja|11=額田大中彦皇子|Prince Nukata no Onakahiko|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/10=ja|qq=}} and the [[:en:Tuntian|military farm]] administrator, {{ill|10=ja|11=淤宇宿禰|Ounosukune|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/10=ja|qq=}}, which took place after the death of the Emperor in what is [[:en:Emperor Ōjin|believed]] to be 310 (the 41st year of the reign of Emperor Ojin) and {{ill|10=ja|11=屯倉|the Imperial Throne|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/10=ja|qq=}} was in a state of uncertainty. When Prince Nukata no Oonakahiko unilaterally confiscated his land, Ousukune appealed to Uji no Wakairoko and then to Osazaki no Mikoto (later [[:en:Emperor Nintoku|Emperor Nintoku]] ), and it was discovered that Agoko, who was currently stationed in Karakuni, knew about the Wa military fields and military storehouses. Following the advice of Ootori-no-Mikoto, Ousukune traveled day and night to Korea with Awaji fishermen and returned with the child's basket. Akogo testified that the "[[:en:Tuntian|military farms]] (屯田) and {{ill|military granary|lt=granaries|ja|屯倉|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/military granary|qq=}} (屯倉) of Wa" were passed down to Emperor Keikō, who was [[:en:Emperor Keikō|the crown prince]] during the reign of [[:en:Emperor Suinin|Emperor Suinin]], saying, "Generally, the [[:en:Tuntian|military farms]] (屯田) of Yamato are the military farms (屯田) of the current emperor. Even if one is the son of the emperor, he cannot be in charge unless he is the emperor's son," and that they were under the control of the emperor of the time. This caused Prince Nukata-Onakahiko to reflect on his actions, and the land management issue was resolved in Ousukune's favor. The [[Kojiki]] makes no mention of such circumstances. === Presentation from the Shishitobe === It is said that the Hihime who appears here and Sumiyoshi's younger sister, Hinohime, are the same person, and that there may be some confusion in the legends. The above description needs to be considered in conjunction with historical facts uncovered by archaeology, which show that the chiefs who became the ancestors of the Izumo no Omi clan in the first half of the 5th century were deeply involved with the Yamato government and engaged in negotiations with the Korean Peninsula. Furthermore, it is necessary to look at the connections with the [[:en:Awaji Island|Awaji Island]] fishermen group and the relationship with the {{ill|Nomi no Sukune|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Nomi no Sukune|qq=}} legend. == Research == A group of fishermen from Awaji Island appears frequently in the aforementioned story; sailors from this group were active when Ousukune went to retrieve the Akoko basket from Korea; and in the legend of Prince Sumiyoshi Nakatsu, "fishermen from Nojima on Awaji" are secretly active, led by {{ill|10=ja|11=阿曇浜子|Azumi no Muraji Hamako|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/10=ja|qq=}}. Many artifacts indicating connections to the peninsula and Izumo have been excavated from the Kidohara and Uryu ruins on Awaji Island. Jasper rough stones from [[:en:Tamayu, Shimane|Kasenyama]] in Tamayu-cho, [[:en:Matsue|Matsue City]] have been excavated from jade-making sites in the Kinai region, such as the Soga Site, Furu {{ill|10=ja|11=布留遺跡|Site|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/10=ja|qq=}}, and Nagahara Site. In particular, jade-making sites using Izumo-style stone materials such as jasper and quartz have been found at the Tani Site near Ise, the base of the Yamato no Agoko clan. Outside the Nara Basin, small amounts of remains have been excavated from the Nagahara ruins in Kawachi Province. In addition to Yayoi period ruins, the remains of a jade-making workshop thought to date from the end of the 4th century to the beginning of the 5th century have been discovered along the coasts of Lake Shinji and Lake Nakaumi, and whetstones made from crystalline schist mined in the [[:en:Kinokawa River|Yoshino River]] and [[:en:Kinokawa River|Kino River]] basins in Nara Prefecture were used. {{ill|Ichishi no Nagaochi|fr|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ichishi no Nagaochi|qq=}}, an ancestor of Yamato no Agoko, appears in the legends of {{ill|Amenohiboko|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Amenohiboko|qq=}} and is also said to have gone to Izumo to welcome Nomi no Sukune. Nomi no Sukune was famous for his {{ill|10=ja|11=当麻蹴速|sumo|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/10=ja|qq=}} match with Tagima no Kehaya, and according to Kikuchi Teruo, this story is the origin of the rice farming ritual in which the spirits of the earth are calmed by sumo. In this story, the land of Tagima that Nomi no Sukune acquired was located at the point where the Nara Basin emerges from [[:en:Osaka Bay|Osaka]] Bay via {{ill|Takeuchi Pass|ja|竹内峠|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Takeuchi Pass|qq=}}, where Sugawara Shrine is located, and it was a strategic transportation hub that also leads to {{ill|10=ja|11=葛城|Katsuragi|4=en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/10=ja|qq=}} to the south. The nearby Ota ruins are the remains of a settlement from the early Kofun period, and pottery from the {{ill|San'in region|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/San'in region|qq=}} estimated to date to the first half of the 4th century has also been excavated. This suggests that there was evidence of a connection with the San'in region around the "Tagima Path" from the time of Nomi no Sukune. As described above, the relationship between the [[Yamato no Kuni no Miyatsuko|Yamato clan]] troops, the Izumo forces, and the fishermen of Awaji Island in the Agokoro legend conveys some historical fact, and it is highly likely that these were condensed and linked together in one person called Yamato no Agoko. == Family tree == Many clans may be descendants of Furutama no Mikoto. This includes the [[:en:Owari clan|Owari clan]] and [[Yamato no Kuni no Miyatsuko]]. This is a subject of debate.{{Cite web|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160422190938/http://wwr2.ucom.ne.jp/hetoyc15/keihu/amabe/amabe-k2.htm|access-date=2023-12-13|website=web.archive.org}} Ancestor of [[Yamato no Kuni no Miyatsuko|the Yamato]] no Kuni no Miyatsuko. There is no mention of him in the [[Kojiki]] . He served under [[:en:Emperor Nintoku|Emperor Nintoku]] , [[:en:Emperor Richū|Emperor Richu]] , and [[:en:Emperor Yūryaku|Emperor Yuryaku]] == Origin == {{Short description|Japanese noble family}} Yamato no Agoko came from the [[Yamato no Kuni no Miyatsuko|Yamato no Atai clan]]. Their [[Ujigami]] or clan god is [[:en:Yamato Okunitama|Yamato Okunitama]] of [[Ōyamato Shrine]]{{Cite web|title=International Symposium "Perspectives on Japanese history and literature from ancient Aston.djvu/208|url=https://en.wikisource.org/wiki/Page:Nihongi_by_Aston.djvu/208|access-date=2023-10-24|website=en.wikisource.org|language=en}} == Historical record == By the way, in the twelfth volume of the "Nihon Shoki," [[:en:Emperor Richū|Emperor Richu]] floats a two-pronged boat on Iware City Isoike Pond. 『日本書紀』履中天皇3rd year 11月6日条 === The Yamato military fields and warehouses === Similarly, Volume 11 of the "Shoki" tells the following story: This is the story of how Agoko remade a giant tree that had washed up on the Oi River into a boat. At this time, Agoko was called "Yamato no Agoko." The Crown Prince, who was filled with suspicion, became suspicious of Agogo's true intentions and tried to kill him. So Agoko felt humbled and offered his younger sister, Hinohime, as a tribute, and was spared the death penalty. From this time on, Yamato no Agoko began to offer court ladies as tribute. 『日本書紀』履中天皇即位前紀条 According to Volume 12 of the "Shoki," Prince Sumiyoshi Nakatsu and Yamato Naokogo were on close terms. Therefore, when Prince Naka rebelled against the Crown Prince, Prince Izahowake (later Emperor Richu), presumably in the year 399, he tried to side with Prince Naka and gathered several hundred elite soldiers at a place called "Kakihami no Kurusu" (said to be Kurusu-go, {{ill|10=ja|11=忍海郡|Oshikai county|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/10=ja|qq=}} ) and waited for the Crown Prince. However, when he realized that the Crown Prince's troops were more numerous than he had expected, he changed his attitude. === Driftwood of the Oi River === Another part of the Richū Sokui Chronicle states that the Crown Prince, on his way to {{ill|Isonokami Jingu|lt=Isonokami Jingu|lt=Isonokami Shrine|en|Isonokami Jingu|lt=Isonokami Jingu|lt=Isonokami Shrine|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Isonokami Shrine|qq=}}, encounters a young girl at the foot of Mt. Asuka and asks her about the safety of the journey.{{Quote frame|In the summer of May of the 62nd year (estimated to be 374 AD), the governor of Tōtōmi Province reported, "There is a large tree that flowed from the {{ill|Ōi River|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ōi River|qq=}}, bending and stopping at the river's curve. Its size is around ten tōdaki (approximately 300 meters). Initially singular, it splits into two at the ends." At that time, Yamato no Ataī Agoko was dispatched to construct a ship from it. Thus, navigating from the Southern Sea, it arrived at Naniwa Port, where it was dedicated as a royal ship.『日本書紀』仁徳天皇62nd year 5月条|qq=draft}}This episode is about a massive log that had drifted to the Ōigawa River, which Agoko then remade into a ship. At this time, Agoko was referred to as "Yamato no Atai." Incidentally, in Volume 12 of the "Nihon Shoki," it is mentioned that Emperor Nintoku floated a bifurcated boat (a boat split into two parts) in the Iware Market Isopond. === Prince Sumiyoshi's Rebellion === The fourteenth volume of the "Shoki" tells the story of Emperor Yuryaku, who, in a fit of rage after a hunt at Mimase, killed Otsu no Umakai with the sword, and his mother, Empress {{ill|Oshisaka no Ōnakatsuhime|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Oshisaka no Ōnakatsuhime|qq=}}, presenting the Wa court lady "Hinohime" to settle the matter. This conversation led to the establishment of the {{ill|10=ja|11=宍人部|Shishihitobe|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/10=ja|qq=}} (the branch of the Shishihito clan), and the appointment of three members, including Kashiwadeno no Omi Nagano. In addition, the “Oyamato no Kuni no Miyatsuko Agoko no Sukune” presented Sahonoko Toriwake to the Shishihitobe, and “the Ministers of the Imperial Court, Tomo no Miyatsuko and Kuni no Miyatsuko, followed suit and continued to offer tribute.” 『日本書紀』雄略天皇2nd year 10月6日条{{Quote frame|"I hear through the grapevine that an extraordinary event has occurred to the Crown Prince. Preparing soldiers, we stand ready to offer assistance."}}As a character in the " [[Nihon Shoki]] ," he appears in relatively many places. Volume 11 of the Nihon Shoki records a dispute over the Yamato military fields and warehouses between {{ill|10=ja|11=額田大中彦皇子|Prince Nukata no Onakahiko|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/10=ja|qq=}} and the [[:en:Tuntian|military farm]] administrator, {{ill|10=ja|11=淤宇宿禰|Ounosukune|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/10=ja|qq=}}, which took place after the death of the Emperor in what is [[:en:Emperor Ōjin|believed]] to be 310 (the 41st year of the reign of Emperor Ojin) and {{ill|10=ja|11=屯倉|the Imperial Throne|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/10=ja|qq=}} was in a state of uncertainty. When Prince Nukata no Oonakahiko unilaterally confiscated his land, Ousukune appealed to Uji no Wakairoko and then to Osazaki no Mikoto (later [[:en:Emperor Nintoku|Emperor Nintoku]] ), and it was discovered that Agoko, who was currently stationed in Karakuni, knew about the Wa military fields and military storehouses. Following the advice of Ootori-no-Mikoto, Ousukune traveled day and night to Korea with Awaji fishermen and returned with the child's basket. Akogo testified that the "[[:en:Tuntian|military farms]] (屯田) and {{ill|military granary|lt=granaries|ja|屯倉|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/military granary|qq=}} (屯倉) of Wa" were passed down to Emperor Keikō, who was [[:en:Emperor Keikō|the crown prince]] during the reign of [[:en:Emperor Suinin|Emperor Suinin]], saying, "Generally, the [[:en:Tuntian|military farms]] (屯田) of Yamato are the military farms (屯田) of the current emperor. Even if one is the son of the emperor, he cannot be in charge unless he is the emperor's son," and that they were under the control of the emperor of the time. This caused Prince Nukata-Onakahiko to reflect on his actions, and the land management issue was resolved in Ousukune's favor. The [[Kojiki]] makes no mention of such circumstances. === Presentation from the Shishitobe === It is said that the Hihime who appears here and Sumiyoshi's younger sister, Hinohime, are the same person, and that there may be some confusion in the legends. The above description needs to be considered in conjunction with historical facts uncovered by archaeology, which show that the chiefs who became the ancestors of the Izumo no Omi clan in the first half of the 5th century were deeply involved with the Yamato government and engaged in negotiations with the Korean Peninsula. Furthermore, it is necessary to look at the connections with the [[:en:Awaji Island|Awaji Island]] fishermen group and the relationship with the {{ill|Nomi no Sukune|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Nomi no Sukune|qq=}} legend. == Research == A group of fishermen from Awaji Island appears frequently in the aforementioned story; sailors from this group were active when Ousukune went to retrieve the Akoko basket from Korea; and in the legend of Prince Sumiyoshi Nakatsu, "fishermen from Nojima on Awaji" are secretly active, led by {{ill|10=ja|11=阿曇浜子|Azumi no Muraji Hamako|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/10=ja|qq=}}. Many artifacts indicating connections to the peninsula and Izumo have been excavated from the Kidohara and Uryu ruins on Awaji Island. Jasper rough stones from [[:en:Tamayu, Shimane|Kasenyama]] in Tamayu-cho, [[:en:Matsue|Matsue City]] have been excavated from jade-making sites in the Kinai region, such as the Soga Site, Furu {{ill|10=ja|11=布留遺跡|Site|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/10=ja|qq=}}, and Nagahara Site. In particular, jade-making sites using Izumo-style stone materials such as jasper and quartz have been found at the Tani Site near Ise, the base of the Yamato no Agoko clan. Outside the Nara Basin, small amounts of remains have been excavated from the Nagahara ruins in Kawachi Province. In addition to Yayoi period ruins, the remains of a jade-making workshop thought to date from the end of the 4th century to the beginning of the 5th century have been discovered along the coasts of Lake Shinji and Lake Nakaumi, and whetstones made from crystalline schist mined in the [[:en:Kinokawa River|Yoshino River]] and [[:en:Kinokawa River|Kino River]] basins in Nara Prefecture were used. {{ill|Ichishi no Nagaochi|fr|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ichishi no Nagaochi|qq=}}, an ancestor of Yamato no Agoko, appears in the legends of {{ill|Amenohiboko|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Amenohiboko|qq=}} and is also said to have gone to Izumo to welcome Nomi no Sukune. Nomi no Sukune was famous for his {{ill|10=ja|11=当麻蹴速|sumo|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/10=ja|qq=}} match with Tagima no Kehaya, and according to Kikuchi Teruo, this story is the origin of the rice farming ritual in which the spirits of the earth are calmed by sumo. In this story, the land of Tagima that Nomi no Sukune acquired was located at the point where the Nara Basin emerges from [[:en:Osaka Bay|Osaka]] Bay via {{ill|Takeuchi Pass|ja|竹内峠|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Takeuchi Pass|qq=}}, where Sugawara Shrine is located, and it was a strategic transportation hub that also leads to {{ill|10=ja|11=葛城|Katsuragi|4=en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/10=ja|qq=}} to the south. The nearby Ota ruins are the remains of a settlement from the early Kofun period, and pottery from the {{ill|San'in region|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/San'in region|qq=}} estimated to date to the first half of the 4th century has also been excavated. This suggests that there was evidence of a connection with the San'in region around the "Tagima Path" from the time of Nomi no Sukune. As described above, the relationship between the [[Yamato no Kuni no Miyatsuko|Yamato clan]] troops, the Izumo forces, and the fishermen of Awaji Island in the Agokoro legend conveys some historical fact, and it is highly likely that these were condensed and linked together in one person called Yamato no Agoko. == Family tree == Many clans may be descendants of Furutama no Mikoto. This includes the [[:en:Owari clan|Owari clan]] and [[Yamato no Kuni no Miyatsuko]]. This is a subject of debate.{{Cite web|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160422190938/http://wwr2.ucom.ne.jp/hetoyc15/keihu/amabe/amabe-k2.htm|access-date=2023-12-13|website=web.archive.org}} Ancestor of [[Yamato no Kuni no Miyatsuko|the Yamato]] no Kuni no Miyatsuko. There is no mention of him in the [[Kojiki]] . He served under [[:en:Emperor Nintoku|Emperor Nintoku]] , [[:en:Emperor Richū|Emperor Richu]] , and [[:en:Emperor Yūryaku|Emperor Yuryaku]] == Origin == {{Short description|Japanese noble family}} Yamato no Agoko came from the [[Yamato no Kuni no Miyatsuko|Yamato no Atai clan]]. Their [[Ujigami]] or clan god is [[:en:Yamato Okunitama|Yamato Okunitama]] of [[Ōyamato Shrine]]{{Cite web|title=International Symposium "Perspectives on Japanese history and literature from ancient Aston.djvu/208|url=https://en.wikisource.org/wiki/Page:Nihongi_by_Aston.djvu/208|access-date=2023-10-24|website=en.wikisource.org|language=en}} == Historical record == By the way, in the twelfth volume of the "Nihon Shoki," [[:en:Emperor Richū|Emperor Richu]] floats a two-pronged boat on Iware City Isoike Pond. 『日本書紀』履中天皇3rd year 11月6日条 === The Yamato military fields and warehouses === Similarly, Volume 11 of the "Shoki" tells the following story: This is the story of how Agoko remade a giant tree that had washed up on the Oi River into a boat. At this time, Agoko was called "Yamato no Agoko." The Crown Prince, who was filled with suspicion, became suspicious of Agogo's true intentions and tried to kill him. So Agoko felt humbled and offered his younger sister, Hinohime, as a tribute, and was spared the death penalty. From this time on, Yamato no Agoko began to offer court ladies as tribute. 『日本書紀』履中天皇即位前紀条 According to Volume 12 of the "Shoki," Prince Sumiyoshi Nakatsu and Yamato Naokogo were on close terms. Therefore, when Prince Naka rebelled against the Crown Prince, Prince Izahowake (later Emperor Richu), presumably in the year 399, he tried to side with Prince Naka and gathered several hundred elite soldiers at a place called "Kakihami no Kurusu" (said to be Kurusu-go, {{ill|10=ja|11=忍海郡|Oshikai county|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/10=ja|qq=}} ) and waited for the Crown Prince. However, when he realized that the Crown Prince's troops were more numerous than he had expected, he changed his attitude. === Driftwood of the Oi River === Another part of the Richū Sokui Chronicle states that the Crown Prince, on his way to {{ill|Isonokami Jingu|lt=Isonokami Jingu|lt=Isonokami Shrine|en|Isonokami Jingu|lt=Isonokami Jingu|lt=Isonokami Shrine|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Isonokami Shrine|qq=}}, encounters a young girl at the foot of Mt. Asuka and asks her about the safety of the journey.{{Quote frame|In the summer of May of the 62nd year (estimated to be 374 AD), the governor of Tōtōmi Province reported, "There is a large tree that flowed from the {{ill|Ōi River|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ōi River|qq=}}, bending and stopping at the river's curve. Its size is around ten tōdaki (approximately 300 meters). Initially singular, it splits into two at the ends." At that time, Yamato no Ataī Agoko was dispatched to construct a ship from it. Thus, navigating from the Southern Sea, it arrived at Naniwa Port, where it was dedicated as a royal ship.『日本書紀』仁徳天皇62nd year 5月条|qq=draft}}This episode is about a massive log that had drifted to the Ōigawa River, which Agoko then remade into a ship. At this time, Agoko was referred to as "Yamato no Atai." Incidentally, in Volume 12 of the "Nihon Shoki," it is mentioned that Emperor Nintoku floated a bifurcated boat (a boat split into two parts) in the Iware Market Isopond. === Prince Sumiyoshi's Rebellion === The fourteenth volume of the "Shoki" tells the story of Emperor Yuryaku, who, in a fit of rage after a hunt at Mimase, killed Otsu no Umakai with the sword, and his mother, Empress {{ill|Oshisaka no Ōnakatsuhime|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Oshisaka no Ōnakatsuhime|qq=}}, presenting the Wa court lady "Hinohime" to settle the matter. This conversation led to the establishment of the {{ill|10=ja|11=宍人部|Shishihitobe|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/10=ja|qq=}} (the branch of the Shishihito clan), and the appointment of three members, including Kashiwadeno no Omi Nagano. In addition, the “Oyamato no Kuni no Miyatsuko Agoko no Sukune” presented Sahonoko Toriwake to the Shishihitobe, and “the Ministers of the Imperial Court, Tomo no Miyatsuko and Kuni no Miyatsuko, followed suit and continued to offer tribute.” 『日本書紀』雄略天皇2nd year 10月6日条{{Quote frame|"I hear through the grapevine that an extraordinary event has occurred to the Crown Prince. Preparing soldiers, we stand ready to offer assistance."}}As a character in the " [[Nihon Shoki]] ," he appears in relatively many places. Volume 11 of the Nihon Shoki records a dispute over the Yamato military fields and warehouses between {{ill|10=ja|11=額田大中彦皇子|Prince Nukata no Onakahiko|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/10=ja|qq=}} and the [[:en:Tuntian|military farm]] administrator, {{ill|10=ja|11=淤宇宿禰|Ounosukune|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/10=ja|qq=}}, which took place after the death of the Emperor in what is [[:en:Emperor Ōjin|believed]] to be 310 (the 41st year of the reign of Emperor Ojin) and {{ill|10=ja|11=屯倉|the Imperial Throne|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/10=ja|qq=}} was in a state of uncertainty. When Prince Nukata no Oonakahiko unilaterally confiscated his land, Ousukune appealed to Uji no Wakairoko and then to Osazaki no Mikoto (later [[:en:Emperor Nintoku|Emperor Nintoku]] ), and it was discovered that Agoko, who was currently stationed in Karakuni, knew about the Wa military fields and military storehouses. Following the advice of Ootori-no-Mikoto, Ousukune traveled day and night to Korea with Awaji fishermen and returned with the child's basket. Akogo testified that the "[[:en:Tuntian|military farms]] (屯田) and {{ill|military granary|lt=granaries|ja|屯倉|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/military granary|qq=}} (屯倉) of Wa" were passed down to Emperor Keikō, who was [[:en:Emperor Keikō|the crown prince]] during the reign of [[:en:Emperor Suinin|Emperor Suinin]], saying, "Generally, the [[:en:Tuntian|military farms]] (屯田) of Yamato are the military farms (屯田) of the current emperor. Even if one is the son of the emperor, he cannot be in charge unless he is the emperor's son," and that they were under the control of the emperor of the time. This caused Prince Nukata-Onakahiko to reflect on his actions, and the land management issue was resolved in Ousukune's favor. The [[Kojiki]] makes no mention of such circumstances. === Presentation from the Shishitobe === It is said that the Hihime who appears here and Sumiyoshi's younger sister, Hinohime, are the same person, and that there may be some confusion in the legends. The above description needs to be considered in conjunction with historical facts uncovered by archaeology, which show that the chiefs who became the ancestors of the Izumo no Omi clan in the first half of the 5th century were deeply involved with the Yamato government and engaged in negotiations with the Korean Peninsula. Furthermore, it is necessary to look at the connections with the [[:en:Awaji Island|Awaji Island]] fishermen group and the relationship with the {{ill|Nomi no Sukune|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Nomi no Sukune|qq=}} legend. == Research == A group of fishermen from Awaji Island appears frequently in the aforementioned story; sailors from this group were active when Ousukune went to retrieve the Akoko basket from Korea; and in the legend of Prince Sumiyoshi Nakatsu, "fishermen from Nojima on Awaji" are secretly active, led by {{ill|10=ja|11=阿曇浜子|Azumi no Muraji Hamako|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/10=ja|qq=}}. Many artifacts indicating connections to the peninsula and Izumo have been excavated from the Kidohara and Uryu ruins on Awaji Island. Jasper rough stones from [[:en:Tamayu, Shimane|Kasenyama]] in Tamayu-cho, [[:en:Matsue|Matsue City]] have been excavated from jade-making sites in the Kinai region, such as the Soga Site, Furu {{ill|10=ja|11=布留遺跡|Site|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/10=ja|qq=}}, and Nagahara Site. In particular, jade-making sites using Izumo-style stone materials such as jasper and quartz have been found at the Tani Site near Ise, the base of the Yamato no Agoko clan. Outside the Nara Basin, small amounts of remains have been excavated from the Nagahara ruins in Kawachi Province. In addition to Yayoi period ruins, the remains of a jade-making workshop thought to date from the end of the 4th century to the beginning of the 5th century have been discovered along the coasts of Lake Shinji and Lake Nakaumi, and whetstones made from crystalline schist mined in the [[:en:Kinokawa River|Yoshino River]] and [[:en:Kinokawa River|Kino River]] basins in Nara Prefecture were used. {{ill|Ichishi no Nagaochi|fr|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ichishi no Nagaochi|qq=}}, an ancestor of Yamato no Agoko, appears in the legends of {{ill|Amenohiboko|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Amenohiboko|qq=}} and is also said to have gone to Izumo to welcome Nomi no Sukune. Nomi no Sukune was famous for his {{ill|10=ja|11=当麻蹴速|sumo|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/10=ja|qq=}} match with Tagima no Kehaya, and according to Kikuchi Teruo, this story is the origin of the rice farming ritual in which the spirits of the earth are calmed by sumo. In this story, the land of Tagima that Nomi no Sukune acquired was located at the point where the Nara Basin emerges from [[:en:Osaka Bay|Osaka]] Bay via {{ill|Takeuchi Pass|ja|竹内峠|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Takeuchi Pass|qq=}}, where Sugawara Shrine is located, and it was a strategic transportation hub that also leads to {{ill|10=ja|11=葛城|Katsuragi|4=en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/10=ja|qq=}} to the south. The nearby Ota ruins are the remains of a settlement from the early Kofun period, and pottery from the {{ill|San'in region|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/San'in region|qq=}} estimated to date to the first half of the 4th century has also been excavated. This suggests that there was evidence of a connection with the San'in region around the "Tagima Path" from the time of Nomi no Sukune. As described above, the relationship between the [[Yamato no Kuni no Miyatsuko|Yamato clan]] troops, the Izumo forces, and the fishermen of Awaji Island in the Agokoro legend conveys some historical fact, and it is highly likely that these were condensed and linked together in one person called Yamato no Agoko. == Family tree == Many clans may be descendants of Furutama no Mikoto. This includes the [[:en:Owari clan|Owari clan]] and [[Yamato no Kuni no Miyatsuko]]. This is a subject of debate.{{Cite web|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160422190938/http://wwr2.ucom.ne.jp/hetoyc15/keihu/amabe/amabe-k2.htm|access-date=2023-12-13|website=web.archive.org}} Ancestor of [[Yamato no Kuni no Miyatsuko|the Yamato]] no Kuni no Miyatsuko. There is no mention of him in the [[Kojiki]] . He served under [[:en:Emperor Nintoku|Emperor Nintoku]] , [[:en:Emperor Richū|Emperor Richu]] , and [[:en:Emperor Yūryaku|Emperor Yuryaku]] == Origin == {{Short description|Japanese noble family}} Yamato no Agoko came from the [[Yamato no Kuni no Miyatsuko|Yamato no Atai clan]]. Their [[Ujigami]] or clan god is [[:en:Yamato Okunitama|Yamato Okunitama]] of [[Ōyamato Shrine]]{{Cite web|title=International Symposium "Perspectives on Japanese history and literature from ancient
